544328|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 14.98% YoY to ₹104.93 crore, driven by tractors (+36.29%) while cranes were flat at ₹52.86 crore.
544328|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue from operations grew 14.98% YoY to ₹104.93 crore and EBITDA rose 10.84% to ₹13.09 crore. Tractor revenue grew 36.29% to ₹52.08 crore, while crane revenue was flat at ₹52.86 crore, which management attributed to the Tier III to Tier V emission norm transition and full utilisation of the existing crane plant. Management maintained FY27 guidance of 20–25% overall revenue growth and 12.5–13% standalone EBITDA margin. The new Bhud plant is targeted for commercial production by end-November 2026, with tower crane production planned for the new line.

segments.name: Tractors
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue ₹52.08 crore, up 36.29% YoY. Management guides 25–30% FY27 growth; utilisation of ~12,000-unit capacity is about 35–40%, and no capacity addition planned. Dealer network about 225.

segments.name: Cranes
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue ₹52.86 crore, flat YoY. Existing plant at full capacity (~1,000–1,200 units); guidance 15–20% FY27 growth from existing plant. Dealer network about 25, stagnant for three quarters. New Bhud plant capacity 3,600 units.

guidance_outlook: FY27 overall revenue growth maintained at ~20–25% (existing plant only; new plant contribution mainly assumed in Q4).
Tractor revenue growth ~25–30% in FY27; management says 30%-plus over 3–5 years.
Crane revenue growth ~15–20% in FY27 from existing plant.
Standalone EBITDA margin 12.5–13% for FY27; consolidated margin said to be similar to last year (~14–15% per analyst’s reading).

New Bhud plant: commercial production targeted by end-November 2026; machinery expected in October. First year utilisation ~30% (Q1 of operations), 35–40% next quarter, ~40–45% average in FY28 (1,500–1,800 cranes).
Crane price hike taken; further price hike planned in coming months; management expects cost pass-through from Q2 FY27.
capex_capacity: New Bhud crane plant: 3,600-unit capacity; civil work in progress; almost all major machines ready; commercial production targeted by end-November 2026.
Tower crane: first prototype passed testing; first lot of 10 machines targeted within Q2 FY27, subject to imported components; some tower crane numbers to be built at the old factory.
Capex funds: ~₹45 crore still held in bank; management says it will be fully deployed by March, possibly by buying 6–8 of 10 planned machines and deferring the rest by up to three months.
Tractor capacity ~12,000 units; no addition planned. Crane machine shop utilisation ~80–85%; crane assembly ~30–35%.
demand_pricing: Crane dealers ~25 (stagnant for three quarters vs. 50-plus target cited by analyst); management plans ~20–25 more dealers within six to12 months of new plant start; Shubham cited a roadmap of ~60-plus dealers nationally, taking one to one-and-a-half years.
Some existing dealers being replaced to match performance expectations; management says working in only ~20–25% of the addressable area.
Tractor dealers ~225; growth tied to dealer development, retail financing, and village-level demos.
Barota Finance finances ~20% of new Indo Farm tractors; refinances old tractors of all brands.
Crane competitors cited: Escorts Construction (premium pricing) and one Faridabad-based peer at similar pricing. Peer ACE grew more than 20% per analyst.
Management says tractor price hikes will follow industry; crane price hike already taken.

qa_highlights.question: Has the crane input cost increase been passed on, and will margins normalise from Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins should hold from Q2 as demand improves; the Tier III to V transition took about three quarters to stabilise, and cost increases can now be passed on.

qa_highlights.question: Why is crane dealer count stagnant at 25, and what is the plan to absorb new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Dealers to be added once capacity is in place; some dealers replaced. Roadmap of ~60-plus dealers nationally, taking one to one-and-a-half years. FY28 needs ~20–25 dealers to sell 1,500–1,800 cranes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the crane sales volume and YoY volume growth in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Not provided on the call; management said figures would be shared by email via the Finance Head.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tractor utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Tractor utilisation ~35–40%; assembly ~30–35%; machine shop ~80–85% because many crane components are made in-house.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 EBITDA margin on a consolidated basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone guidance 12.5–13%; consolidated said to move on similar lines to last year, which the analyst interpreted as 14–15%; management confirmed the analyst’s reading.

qa_highlights.question: Will the ₹45 crore capex cash be used by Q3 to start commercialisation by January?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it may buy 6–8 of 10 machines and defer up to three months; full deployment by March. Commercial production still targeted for November.

qa_highlights.question: Can crane growth of 15–20% be achieved with existing capacity before the new plant starts?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management confirmed existing capacity is sufficient for 15–20% growth until the new plant starts.

risks_watch: Crane growth: Q1 flat; FY27 guidance 15–20% depends on July–August demand recovery and dealer additions.
Bhud plant timing: November commercial production depends on machinery arriving in October and on imported tower crane components.
Dealer quality and ramp-up: management says new dealers take 6–18 months; utilisation of new plant guided at 30% in year one.
Tractor volume growth of 25–30% contingent on dealer build-out, financing, and village-level demand; utilisation still ~35–40%.
Price hikes: crane price increase taken; further hikes depend on demand and input costs; tractor pricing follows industry.
Volume disclosure: Q1 unit volumes not disclosed on the call; to be shared later by email.
544328|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on tractors and the new plant timeline, but evasive on specifics: crane dealer targets, unit volumes, and consolidated margin were deferred or loosely answered. Management repeatedly tied crane recovery to Q2 demand without quantifying it.
key_quotes: From this quarter onwards, because demand has increased, I think everything can be passed on to the customers.
We expect to complete these 10 machines within this quarter, subject to receipt of the few components we are expecting from outside.
The new capacity is 3,600 cranes, yes.
Over three to five years in the tractor business, we are very sure that 30% -plus growth will continue.

financial_highlights.change: Cited by analyst; not verified in call

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Crane price hike taken and further hike planned with cost pass-through expected from Q2, but standalone Q1 EBITDA margin was ~12.5% (13.09/104.93) against the 12.5–13% FY27 guide, so there is little room for expansion yet.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: New Bhud crane plant with 3,600-unit capacity is under construction, machinery arrives in October, and existing crane plant is at full utilisation (~1,000–1,200 units), so the new capacity is firmly committed with a date.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.when: FY27 (tractors through Q4; cranes from Q3 once the new plant
rows.why: Tractor revenue is guided to grow 25–30% in FY27 (Q1 +36.29%), and the new plant's 3,600-unit capacity is expected to be ~30% utilised in year one, but Q1 unit volumes were not disclosed and crane volumes were flat.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Tractor utilisation is only ~35–40% on ~12,000 units with no addition planned, and ~₹45 crore of capex cash is to be fully deployed by March within already-committed projects, so no fresh capex is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 overall growth of 20–25% was only held, not raised, with crane revenue flat at ₹52.86 crore in Q1 and dealers stagnant at ~25.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Crane revenue was flat YoY in Q1 yet FY27 crane guidance is 15–20%, which depends on July–August demand recovery and dealer additions, and the new plant's November start depends on October machinery arrival and imported tower crane components.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: First prototype of the tower crane passed testing and a first lot of 10 machines is targeted within Q2 FY27, subject to imported components.

rows.label: Crane dealer network build-out (~25 to 45-plus)
rows.why: Management plans ~20–25 more dealers within six to 12 months of the new plant start, against ~25 dealers today and a roadmap of ~60-plus nationally over one to one-and-a-half years.

rows.label: Further crane price hike
rows.when: coming months, cost pass-through from Q2 FY27
rows.why: A crane price hike is already taken and a further hike is planned, with management expecting cost pass-through from Q2 FY27 after the Tier III to V transition took about three quarters to stabilise.

rows.label: Remaining ₹45 crore capex deployment
rows.why: About ₹45 crore is still held in bank, and management says it will be fully deployed by March, buying 6–8 of 10 planned machines and deferring the rest by up to three months.

tone.note: Management was confident on tractor growth and the November Bhud plant timeline but evasive on crane dealer targets, Q1 unit volumes and consolidated margin; analysts pushed on the flat crane segment and the stagnant dealer count of ~25 against a 50-plus target.

544332|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated total income rose 46.93% to ₹221.72 crore, but standalone EBITDA fell 21.5% to ₹12.96 crore on margin investments.
544332|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a year of investment in capabilities, data centre, solar and semiconductor entry at tighter margins, and reported consolidated PAT of ₹15.82 crore (up 18.95%). Standalone PAT fell 24.75% to ₹9.06 crore, and standalone EBITDA fell 21.5% to ₹12.96 crore. Order book is stated at about ₹199 crore with a ₹480 crore pipeline, and management expects it to rise to ₹275–300 crore within about 15–20 days. Management flagged higher debt and working capital in FY27, with margin recovery and a larger takeoff expected from FY28.

financial_highlights.change: management says it has gone up since year end

segments.name: Kelvin Air Conditioning & Ventilation Systems (60.53% stake)
segments.commentary: HVAC arm providing complete system integration; management plans to raise stake to 70–72%. Expanding into data centres, industrial and solar.

segments.name: Advantek (34.99% stake after Altair merger)
segments.commentary: AHU manufacturer for backward integration. Altair merger caused a one-time ₹1 crore legacy hit; management expects EU certification to drive growth.

segments.name: Aart Integrated Projects (28% stake)
segments.commentary: Design and engineering arm for semiconductor, solar and non-pharma. Revenue reportedly rose from ₹14 crore to ₹34 crore, driven by non-pharma and microelectronics wins.

guidance_outlook: Management guided to 20–30% growth in FY27, described as conservative; it aims to hold margins while revenue grows.
Largest solar ticket (Waaree, ~₹68 crore) expected to be commissioned by July 2026.
Order book of ~₹199 crore expected to rise to ₹275–300 crore within 15–20 days; execution targeted by September–October 2026.
Management said the ~₹1 crore Altair drag and ~₹80 lakh NCLT-related write-off will not recur, implying about ₹18 crore PAT without them.
Management said H2 is historically stronger than H1 over the last four to five years.
capex_capacity: Hyderabad facility on about 2 acres, ~50,000 sq ft built-up area, capacity ~2,000 sq m per day, with one puff line and one rock wool panel line.
Factory capacity described as significantly enhanced and automated; gas and power shortages forced use of cylinders.
Management said no acquisitions are currently planned; focus is on consolidating existing entities.
demand_pricing: Solar: about 23 active hot leads; Waaree reference being completed; Satvik and Gupin references being established.
Semiconductor: CG Electronics AHU-based cleanroom cited as reference, under confidentiality; management said Japanese competitors are already present.
Data centres: project slowed as technology shifted from conventional HVAC to immersion cooling.
Pricing: company is seeking price revisions from clients under force majeure due to raw material (aluminium, steel) inflation and supply disruption.
Management accepted tighter margins on data centre, solar and semiconductor orders to build references.

qa_highlights.question: How will the order book diversify from solar into semiconductor, data centres and biotech?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said solar references were built first, with a pipeline of about 23 hot solar leads. Semiconductor entry will follow but faces Japanese incumbents, and life sciences turnkey remains the mainstay.

qa_highlights.question: Can the ₹200 crore order book be executed within H1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was possible, with a caveat that client-requested start dates can push timelines; it expects the book to be executed within six months.

qa_highlights.question: Are large-ticket orders of ₹70–100 crore coming?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said one or two orders of ₹60–80 crore were expected soon.

qa_highlights.question: What is the T-grid system and its TAM?
qa_highlights.answer: Aart's Rajesh Gupte described a modular ceiling grid (1200x1200 mm) with FFU-based class control, load capacity of about 1,500–1,600 kg, and variants of 70, 130 and 210–230 mm heights; no TAM figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins on the current order book be normalised or lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the margin is subject to supply chain pressures; it is guiding to conservative growth and maintaining margins, with business decisions on new projects after commissioning.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company acquire more capabilities or increase stakes in subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: No acquisition is currently planned. Stake increases in Kelvin (to 70–72%) and possibly Advantek are targeted, with Aart dependent on compliance readiness.

risks_watch: Working capital and debt rising in FY27 as retention money is pending; management expects improvement only from FY28.
Supply chain and raw material shortages (aluminium, steel, gas, power) with price revision requests to clients not guaranteed.
Standalone EBITDA and PAT declined sharply; consolidated gains rely on subsidiaries such as Aart and Kelvin.
Governance: information security issue addressed, NCLT-related write-off, and management acknowledged subsidiaries need better compliance.
Waaree commissioning slipping from schedule; delivery started in February 2026.
544332|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and promotional on long-term positioning and the order book, but evasive on specific margins, FY27 numbers and the Waaree delay. Management answered several questions with generalities and deferred others.
key_quotes: We are entering the new year with 199 and in 15 days time you will see the numbers going to upwards of 275 to 300 crores.
FY26 was a year of preparation and position. The foundation for the next phase of growth is now largely in place.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Standalone EBITDA fell 21.5% to ₹12.96 crore on tighter data centre, solar and semiconductor margins, and management says margin on current book is subject to supply-chain pressure; margin recovery is only flagged from FY28.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant or line is planned; the Hyderabad facility (~2,000 sq m/day, one puff line, one rock wool line) is already commissioned and no utilisation figure was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book ~₹199 crore rising to ₹275–300 crore within 15–20 days, ~₹200 crore to be executed within six months, and management guides 20–30% FY27 growth (midpoint 25%, called conservative).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed and no capex plan was stated; the only expansion is the Kelvin stake increase, and no acquisitions are planned.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management calls the 20–30% FY27 guide conservative and says H2 has been stronger than H1 for four to five years, but the Waaree delay and raw material costs cap the upside.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Waaree (~₹68 crore) slipped from schedule and is now targeted for July 2026, raw material (aluminium, steel) inflation is pushing for client price revisions, and working capital and debt are set to rise in FY27.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Aart's T-grid modular ceiling grid (1200x1200 mm, 70/130/210–230 mm heights) is described, but no launch date or TAM was given.

rows.label: Large-ticket solar and cleanroom orders
rows.why: Management expects one or two orders of ₹60–80 crore soon and has about 23 hot solar leads, but client start dates can push timelines.

rows.label: Working capital and debt rise in FY27
rows.why: Retention money is pending and management expects working capital and debt to rise in FY27, with improvement only from FY28.

rows.label: Kelvin stake increase to 70–72%
rows.why: Management plans to lift its 60.53% stake in Kelvin to 70–72%, with a possible Advantek increase, though no timing was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on the order book, the 20–30% FY27 guide and H2 seasonality, but evasive on specific margins, the Waaree delay and FY27 debt; analysts pushed on order execution timing and margin normalisation.

544332|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose about 75% to ₹133.23 crore, PAT up about 55% to ₹5.15 crore, with order book at ₹468 crore.
544332|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue rose about 75% YoY to ₹133.23 crore and EBITA rose 75% to ₹10.28 crore, with EBITA margin at 7.67%. PAT rose about 55% to ₹5.15 crore (EPS ₹4.18). Order book stood at ₹468 crore as of 30 September, more than double March levels, and receivables rose to ₹129 crore, which management attributed to milestone-linked terms on reference projects. Management guided H2 PAT to exceed H1 substantially and said working capital should ease by March/April 2027.

financial_highlights.value: ₹468 crore standalone; ₹517 crore consolidated per Q&A reconciliation
₹40 crore against net worth of ₹112 crore (~0.37x)

segments.name: Pharma and life sciences
segments.commentary: Order book rose from ₹42 crore to ₹217 crore in six months; a ₹92 crore order for Meril Life Sciences was finalised, described as the largest pharma ticket in the industry.

segments.name: Renewable energy
segments.commentary: Order book of ₹195 crore at 30 September; management said new solar orders are at better margins than the Waaree reference project.

segments.name: Data centres, semiconductors and other
segments.commentary: ₹56 crore of order book in data centres, semiconductors and other industries. Kelvin has delivered for NSE, Nxtra, CtrlS and Qualcomm; Kelvin pushed back ~₹120 crore of projects that were priced as reference deals.

guidance_outlook: Internal plan for FY27 revised to 70–80% revenue growth, versus the externally guided 20–30%, with margins held at the same percentage as the prior year.
H2 PAT expected to exceed H1 PAT substantially; H2 EBITDA margin expected above the ~12% of H2 FY26, per management in Q&A.
Management expects FY27 order book conversion of roughly ₹400–450 crore, with about ₹200 crore delivered in the next few months.
Hot pipeline of ~₹600 crore (of ₹1,250 crore total offers), with ₹250 crore expected to finalise in Q3 and ₹350 crore in Q4.
Working capital expected to ease by March/April 2027; management targets positive operating cash flow in FY28.
Long-term targets: top-three cleanroom player in India by end FY27 and number one by 2030; 25–30% market share by FY30; internal PAT margin target of 8–10%.
capex_capacity: Hyderabad plant added about 50,000 sq m of capacity on about two acres near Genome Valley, with roll forming, CNC laser cutting, powder coating and a dedicated puff and Rockwool panel line; ISO 9001:2015, FM 4880/4882 and RoHS certified.
Umbergaon (Gujarat) automation lifting output and consistency.

Capital plan under preparation; banks described as ready to fund. Management said it would not dilute without a real opportunity, and mentioned consolidating Kelvin and a possible Southeast Asian manufacturing facility.
Management stated it is in talks with multinationals on possible 5–10% stake sales in subsidiaries, has refused most proposals, and is open to acquisitions of smaller companies and vendors.
Semiconductor project of 75,000 sq m class 1000 cleanroom referred to; management said semiconductor ticket sizes range from ₹200 crore to ₹1,000 crore.
demand_pricing: Ticket sizes rising, especially in life sciences and microelectronics; a good share of new orders from repeat customers.
Management is selecting orders on better commercial terms and says it now has the liberty to pick and choose.

Competition: management cited Japanese multinationals as incumbents, with European and British players expected to enter; it said the company's references and subject-matter expertise are its right to win.

Raw material volatility: aluminium moved from about ₹220 to ₹440 in two months and oil from about $67–68 to $95–97, per management. Management said it had not hedged and has not passed through cost escalations broadly; escalation has been applied in some cases.
Management said the Indian cleanroom market is ~₹5,000 crore per year growing 50–70%, with Fabtech holding ~7–8% share.

qa_highlights.question: What is the execution period for the ~₹470 crore order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said execution is possible in three months, but customer readiness governs timing; about ₹200 crore would be delivered in the next few months and FY27 conversion is ~₹400–450 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was H1 revenue (~₹130 crore) below the ~₹170–180 crore implied by monthly order book updates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no orders were cancelled; deliveries were deferred because customer buildings were not ready, and design changes stretched approval from about three weeks to eight or nine weeks on one project.

qa_highlights.question: Why do the order book figures not reconcile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the ₹468 crore figure is standalone; adding the subsidiary (consolidated) gives about ₹517 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the target margin and how do H2 margins compare?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said internal target is an 8–10% PAT margin; in response to a follow-up, it said H2 EBITDA margin should be above H2 FY26's ~12%, and PAT in H2 should exceed H1.

qa_highlights.question: Are the company's cash flows turning positive?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Arihant Dhariwal said the internal target is positive cash flow and better working capital position in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company hedging raw material prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not currently hedge; the CEO suggested that a captive steel plant and aluminium extrusion would help, and said it will look at futures-based hedging.

risks_watch: Receivables of ₹129 crore and working capital pressure; management expects easing by March/April 2027 and collection progress in Q3 and Q4.
Customer readiness and site delays causing deferred deliveries and slower billing versus monthly order book disclosures.
Raw material cost volatility (aluminium, steel, Rockwool, PUFF chemicals) with no hedging policy in place.
Management's FY27 guidance of 70–80% growth and 8–10% PAT margin depends on converting the ₹600 crore pipeline and on H2 margin recovery.
Capital requirement for growth remains unquantified; possible external capital or stake sale in subsidiaries.
544332|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth, order book and long-term targets, with repeated emphasis on the 70–80% growth plan. Evasive on quantified capital needs, hedging and margin specifics, and on raw material outlook, which management described as unpredictable.
key_quotes: We are firmly on course for a full year guidance we have given you.
Receivables were a choice we made, not an accident.
Cash flows is the only scorecard I, as the largest shareholder and the founder promoter of this company, will accept.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided H2 EBITDA margin above H2 FY26's ~12% and H2 PAT to exceed H1 substantially, though raw material costs (aluminium ~₹220 to ₹440 in two months) are unhedged and only partly passed through.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Hyderabad plant adding ~50,000 sq m near Genome Valley is already commissioned and now part of the manufacturing base, with Umbergaon automation also commissioned.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book of ₹468 crore standalone (₹517 crore consolidated) is more than double March levels, with ~₹200 crore to be delivered in the next few months and FY27 conversion of ₹400-450 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capital plan is under preparation with banks ready to fund, but the quantum is unquantified and management said it would not dilute without a real opportunity; semiconductor tickets of ₹200-1,000 crore are referenced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Internal FY27 plan is 70-80% revenue growth versus the externally guided 20-30%, but this is an internal plan and conversion of the ~₹600 crore hot pipeline is not yet confirmed.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue of ~₹133 crore fell short of the ~₹170-180 crore implied by monthly order book updates due to deferred deliveries, and the 70-80% growth plan depends on H2 conversion and margin recovery.

rows.label: Working capital ease and positive FY28 cash flow
rows.why: Management expects working capital to ease by March/April 2027 and targets positive operating cash flow in FY28, against receivables of ₹129 crore and borrowings of ₹40 crore.

rows.label: Hot pipeline conversion of ~₹600 crore
rows.why: ₹250 crore expected to finalise in Q3 and ₹350 crore in Q4, out of ₹1,250 crore total offers, with a ₹92 crore Meril Life Sciences order finalised.

rows.label: Better-margin solar orders and selective order intake
rows.why: Management says new solar orders carry better margins than the Waaree reference project and it is selecting orders on commercial terms, while Kelvin pushed back ~₹120 crore of reference-priced projects.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 70-80% growth plan, the ₹468 crore order book and long-term targets, but cautious or evasive on capital needs, hedging and raw material outlook; analysts probed the H1 revenue shortfall versus order book updates, the order book reconciliation, and margins.

544333|2026-03.headline: Standard Engineering Technology posted FY26 total income of INR793 crores (+26.7% YoY) and PAT of INR83 crores (+21%), but Q4 gross margin fell to ~32% from ~39% in Q3.
544333|2026-03.overview: Management called FY26 the best year in company history, with revenue, profitability, operating cash flow and working capital all improving together. Q4 total income was INR231 crores (+35% YoY), with EBITDA of INR36 crores (15.5% margin) and PAT of INR21 crores (9.1% margin). Q4 EBITDA was pressured by higher metal input prices and deliberate manpower additions ahead of expected FY27 growth. Management guided FY27 growth and margin improvement qualitatively, with no numeric guidance, and disclosed a new INR130 crore greenfield facility on a 36-acre campus, due in two phases in April 2027 and April 2028.

segments.name: Glass-lined equipment
segments.commentary: Management says glass lining is still about 30% of the business and remains one of the most profitable verticals, though its share is shrinking as other lines grow. Shell and tube glass-lined heat exchangers (with GL HAKKO, Japan) have over 200 units in order book, with 100 delivered.

segments.name: C2C Engineering (acquired)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue was INR24 crores, with order book of about INR46-47 crores. FY27 target is INR60 crores, and margins are said to be similar to the group average.

segments.name: Scigenics (acquired)
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR20 crores in FY26 (consolidated for only part of the year). Management targets about INR60 crores in FY27, with margins similar to the group.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue roughly doubled in FY26 versus FY25 per management, but the Q4 export share was 5.3% against guidance of 12-13%. Export order book is only about INR30 crores.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue to grow faster than FY26's 25% rate, per management; no numeric target given.
EBITDA margin in FY27 to improve over FY26 (17.4%); management declined to give a number, and said 'figure I can't confirm' on a 16-17% margin.
Working capital days targeted around 170 in FY27 (vs 150 in FY26), with cash conversion expected to improve versus FY26.
Management expects a INR250-300 crore quarterly revenue run rate from FY27 onwards; said 'possible and definitely we are going to do'.
Capex of INR130 crores over two years for the greenfield facility (INR65 crores in FY27 and INR65 crores in FY28), plus INR35-40 crores for modernisation of existing plants.
Heat exchanger full-fledged Indian manufacturing to start July 1, 2026, with capacity of 200 units per month.
Nuclear and oil and gas entry targeted around FY28.
Pre-cast building subsidiary is being set up to serve pharma and chemical clients only.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was about INR40 crores; modernisation of existing plants with robotic and automatic welding and polishing machines continues with another INR35-40 crores planned.
Existing plants run at 70-80% utilisation; management says they can handle 60-70% more revenue after modernisation, taking existing capacity to about INR2,000 crores.
Greenfield 36-acre campus: INR130 crores capex, two phases. Phase 1 (50%) due April 1, 2027; phase 2 due April 1, 2028. Adds about INR2,000 crores capacity, for a total of about INR4,000 crores.

Heat exchanger unit: 80% of equipment is built in Japan and 20% in India. About 50 units were made and sold in India in FY26 (per management), with another 50 in order book. Full-scale Indian manufacturing starts July 1, 2026, at 200 units per month capacity.
Pre-cast building capability for production blocks, targeted to finish in about six months; greenfield projects to complete in 12-14 months.
demand_pricing: Order book is about INR1,000 crores, with about INR30 crores from exports and the balance domestic. Execution is expected in about 8-10 months. Management declined to split the order book by segment.
Advances of 10-30% are taken from customers, typically 20-30%.
Management says it is booking raw materials once orders are received because metal prices are volatile. Freight on exports is passed to customers.

Management said it would not commit to the projected INR1,000-1,200 crore of project completions in FY27.
capex_capacity: Equipment base of 230+ construction equipment and vehicles; workforce above 1,100 employees.

Preferential issue of convertible warrants up to INR13.09 crore approved; proceeds targeted at working capital needs in about 10-12 months.
Borrowing limits enhancement proposed to support larger projects.
Acquired 10% stake in Virtuoso Infra Meditech LLP (Indore real-estate build, completion in about 2-2.5 years).

Company prefers large tickets: NH projects above INR500 crore and building projects above INR50 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the order book fall YoY, and is tender flow slowing?

qa_highlights.question: What margin should investors expect going forward?

qa_highlights.question: What is the wastewater margin, and how will mix evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Wastewater EBITDA margin was cited at 15-20%. Management expects wastewater at about 20-25% of revenue in the near future, with the balance from roads, buildings, RMC and toll. It is currently subcontracting or name-lending because it lacks credentials.

qa_highlights.question: How did FY26 growth split across business lines?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave FY26 revenue split of about 49% road, 3% RMC, 47% toll, with wastewater very small. Road and toll drove the growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company exposed to fuel price increases?

qa_highlights.question: What are the biggest opportunities and risks?

risks_watch: Order book fell YoY to about INR1,235 crore; conversion of about INR1,500-2,000 crore pending bids is key to FY27 growth.
Wastewater margin claims (15-20%) are unproven; the company lacks credentials and works as subcontractor or name-lender; competition is intense.
Management declined to commit to FY27 completions of INR1,000-1,200 crore, citing geopolitical and macro uncertainty.
Toll segment margin (about 2.5-4%) is much lower than EPC, so mix shift toward toll dilutes margin.

Management did not provide an order book figure as of 31 May 2026.

544335|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose about 61% to INR550 crore and PAT about 38% to INR22 crore, while EBITDA grew only about 28%.
544335|2026-09.overview: H1 FY27 revenue from operations was about INR550 crore versus INR342 crore in H1 FY26, with EPC at about INR303 crore and toll collection (TCC) at about INR236 crore. EBITA excluding other income was about INR35 crore versus INR27 crore, and PAT was about INR22 crore versus INR16 crore. Management attributed the margin gap to a lower-margin toll mix and higher petroleum-linked input costs (bitumen, diesel, cement). Order book stood at INR1,755 crore at 30 September 2026, after about INR1,087 crore of gross inflows in H1, with toll contracts forming the largest share.

segments.name: EPC (roads, buildings, wastewater)
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 EPC revenue about INR303 crore. EPC order book about INR589 crore roads, INR72 crore buildings and INR132 crore wastewater, executable over 6 to 24 months. EPC strike ratio is about 10-15%.

segments.name: Toll collection contracts (TCC)
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 TCC revenue about INR236 crore. TCC order book about INR962 crore; company operates about 24 toll plazas (management also cited 10 toll contracts in a separate answer). Strike ratio above 75% (management gave 70-75% and 75%).

segments.name: Wastewater and sewage
segments.commentary: Unexecuted order book about INR132 crore; management expects INR80-90 crore execution in H2 FY27 and INR300-400 crore of new orders by year end, via JVs or partnerships since the company is not yet eligible to bid solely.

segments.name: RMC (ready-mix concrete)
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 1.8 lakh cubic metres per year at Indore plant (set up 2008), utilisation about 70% in H1 FY27 per analyst; management said 80-85% of capacity (90% of available operational capacity). New 1.8 lakh cubic metre plant in Indore approved by board, expected operational in H1 FY27-28.

segments.name: Residential plotting (BRG Hillview)
segments.commentary: About 1.6 lakh sq ft of plots unsold; no new customer sales booked in the current financial year as the company has paused sales.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth target of 25-30% for FY27, after FY26 turnover of INR824 crore; conservative long-term target of 20-25% annual growth.
Management expects 40-50% of toll contract order revenue to be recognised in FY27; revenue mix expected to stay about 50:50 EPC and TCC over the next 2-3 years.
PAT margin of large infra peers 8-10%; company aspires to these levels over time but not in the current year.
EPC order book expected to reach about INR1,000-1,500 crore by 31 March 2027, with EPC bidding of about INR5,000 crore planned for FY27.
Total order book expected to rise by about INR1,000-1,500 crore in FY27; management said H2 performance should be good and in line with plan.
capex_capacity: New 1.8 lakh cubic metre RMC plant in Indore approved by board; expected operational in H1 FY27-28.
Company has not set internal capital-exposure limits for toll contracts; may bid for 2-3, or about 5, toll plazas in FY27.
Exploring TOT (toll operate transfer, 20-year, upfront payment), HAM and BOT projects; no HAM/PPP bid won so far.

Working capital limit raised from INR35 crore to INR50 crore in April 2026; equipment loan enhanced by about INR10 crore; no new limits expected for 1-1.5 years unless order book reaches about INR5,000 crore.
demand_pricing: H1 FY27 gross order inflow about INR1,087 crore, including Bundelkhand Expressway toll and O&M contract from UPEIDA at INR377.54 crore for two years, and six NHAI toll plazas (about INR587 crore combined).
Escalation: government is compensating diesel and bitumen cost increases under special provisions, per management, with no profitability impact.
EBITDA margin pressure attributed to lower-margin TCC mix and higher petroleum-linked costs in EPC.
Management says EPC procurement policy changes may slow EPC awards for 1.5-2 years before a positive shift; private building opportunities being pursued in Indore (CyberCity project).

qa_highlights.question: Revenue expected from toll collection contracts in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 40-50% of toll contract revenue is expected in the current financial year (FY27).

qa_highlights.question: Sustainable EBITDA margin and ROCE for toll collection versus EPC?
qa_highlights.answer: TCC needs about 5% working capital and nil plant and machinery cost; ROCE is 30-50% versus 15-25% for EPC, rising to 60-70% at scale. Contracts are one-year fixed-collection contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Why EBITDA growth (28%) lags revenue growth (61%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lower blended EBITDA margin from TCC growth and higher petroleum-linked costs (bitumen, diesel, cement) in EPC.

qa_highlights.question: Will working capital and bank guarantee needs rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Fund-based limit is INR50 crore; total BG about INR315 crore plus cash credit; surety bonds accepted by central agencies including NHAI toll division, so no new limits expected for 1-1.5 years unless order book reaches about INR5,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Wastewater expansion: organic or partnerships?
qa_highlights.answer: Strategic partnerships or JVs for now because the company lacks eligibility for direct bids in this new segment; INR300-400 crore of new orders targeted by year end.

qa_highlights.question: RMC capacity and Hillview plotting status?
qa_highlights.answer: RMC utilisation about 80-85% (90% of available capacity); new 1.8 lakh cubic metre plant planned. About 1.6 lakh sq ft of Hillview plots unsold; sales paused.

risks_watch: Margin dilution: EBITDA grew 28% against revenue growth of 61%; other expenses rose to INR392 crore from INR305 crore.
Dependence on TCC (about 50% of revenue expected): one-year contracts require re-bidding; NHAI contract renewals and bid pipeline must hold.
EPC strike ratio of 10-15% and EPC policy changes may slow awards for 1.5-2 years.
Finance cost rose after the INR15 crore working capital enhancement; watch borrowing costs as order book grows.
Cost pressure from petroleum-linked inputs; government escalation support is stated but not yet quantified.
No HAM/PPP wins to date; BOT and TOT entry depends on internal accruals and bank support.
Wastewater business has no direct eligibility; growth depends on partners.

544339|2026-03.headline: Laxmi Dental Q4 FY26 revenue rose 21.9% YoY to Rs 74 crore with EBITDA margin at 18.3%, and FY26 revenue grew 16.2% to Rs 277.9 crore.
544339|2026-03.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as a recovery quarter with highest-ever quarterly revenue of Rs 74 crore, up 21.9% YoY, and broad-based growth across dental lab, aligners and pediatric segments. EBITDA rose 41.8% YoY to Rs 13.5 crore and PAT reached Rs 10.1 crore, helped by a Rs 1.3 crore tax benefit tied to a labour code gratuity item. FY26 closed with revenue of Rs 277.9 crore, EBITDA of Rs 43.4 crore and PAT of Rs 28.9 crore, against a weak Q3. Management declined to give FY27 margin or growth guidance, and cited the company's Rs 99 crore cash balance and ongoing scanner deployment as strategic priorities.

financial_highlights.change: Minor sequential improvement; ~76% excluding scanner sales
vs Rs 4.3 crore in Q4 FY25; includes Rs 1.3 crore tax benefit
vs Rs 1.3 crore last year; company debt-free

financial_highlights.metric: Cash and bank balance incl. investments

segments.name: Dental lab (total)
segments.commentary: Record quarterly revenue of Rs 45.9 crore, up 27% YoY, with international lab up 40.9% YoY and domestic lab up 16.3% YoY to Rs 23.7 crore. Digital penetration in domestic lab is about 80%, with a medium-term target above 90%.

segments.name: Bizdent (domestic clear aligners)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 10.9% YoY in Q4 after a sequential recovery; management said margins were prioritised over pricing, which had been under pressure in prior quarters.

segments.name: Vedia (aligner raw material, mainly export)
segments.commentary: Revenue of Rs 7.3 crore, stable sequentially. Some March shipments slipped to April because freight costs roughly doubled, and in some cases nearly tripled, which delayed revenue recognition.

segments.name: Kids-e-Dental (pediatric)
segments.commentary: Quarterly revenue of Rs 5.4 crore. International registrations are in progress, with some regulatory steps cleared; no firm timeline given.

segments.name: Scanners
segments.commentary: Scanner sales were 211 units in Q4 FY26 and 1,009 units in FY26. Scanners carry lower margins and weighed on consolidated gross margin in Q4.

guidance_outlook: No numerical FY27 guidance. Management said it wants to do better than the 16.2% FY26 growth over the next two to three years, but did not endorse a 20% CAGR.

Management did not reaffirm the earlier target of 18-20% EBITDA margin, 75-80% gross margin and 13-15% PAT margin by FY27 or FY28. It said Q4 margins were in line with that range but would not give a timeline today.
Operating leverage is expected as people costs grow less than revenue; COGS will scale in proportion to sales. Automation and digital dentistry investments are planned.
Capex for FY27 will be set based on operational needs and revenue growth, funded from IPO proceeds still on hand.
US tariff is now about 10% (was about 50%). Management said this is not a deal breaker and expects US business to keep growing.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was about Rs 18.4 crore. FY27 capex will be balanced against operational capabilities and revenue growth, with no fixed amount given.
Scanner deployment remains a strategic priority: 211 units in Q4 FY26 and 1,009 units in FY26. Management wants to place as many as possible before scanners become commoditised.
Investment in automation and AI (AI Dent) continues to support cost structure and digital dentistry.
demand_pricing: Export share of revenue is about 33-34%. US is about 20% of revenue, and management said it is well diversified across customers, not dependent on Heartland Dental.
Management said the US tariff eased to about 10% from about 50%, and it absorbed higher tariff costs in the first half of Q4. It said the scale-up in the US was gradual and cautious.
Domestic aligner pricing was under pressure in prior quarters; management chose to protect margins, with Bizdent recovering in Q4.
Vedia orders were delayed by freight costs, but management said YoY growth is good and the business is not facing structural uncertainty.

The iScope 360 remote oral-health and aligner-monitoring product launched about two weeks before the call. It is sold through dentists at about Rs 2,000 retail with points-based subscription, and it may also be offered in export markets.
Competition is rising in domestic aligners and from funded players. Management said 22,000 dentists are active with Laxmi, against about 3 lakh dentists in India.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Bizdent revenue stay flat FY25 to FY26, and how much of the Q4 recovery came from pricing versus volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it chose to protect margins over price cuts during the pricing pressure. It did not split Q4 recovery between price and volume, and said it will keep balancing price against growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Vedia lower QoQ despite rupee depreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight costs roughly doubled, and in some cases nearly tripled, which delayed March shipments into April. Management said YoY growth is good and there is no structural problem.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the lab business run rate of about Rs 40-45 crore per quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot give a number today, but expects growth in both domestic and international lab over the next two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for margins and growth for FY27 and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give FY27 guidance. It said it wants to improve margins over the next two to three years and that Q3 was an exception. Q4 EBITDA margin was 18%.

qa_highlights.question: Is Heartland Dental's contract under review, and are more US DSOs coming?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there has been no change to the Heartland contract. It said more DSOs are being added but will not be announced individually, and that the business is diversified.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company considering acquisitions with its cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will evaluate opportunities that add value and will disclose them only once completed. It gave no specifics.

risks_watch: US tariff regime remains volatile. Current 10% rate could change, and the US is about 20% of revenue.
Freight costs and global shipping disruption caused Vedia export delays, which could recur at quarter-end.
Bizdent faces pricing pressure from domestic and funded competitors. Management is weighing margin against growth.
Gross margin is diluted by scanner sales, which carry lower margins. Scanner margin trajectory matters for consolidated margin.
Management has not reaffirmed the earlier margin targets. Watch whether FY27 margins hold at Q4 levels.
Kids-e-Dental international registration timing is uncertain.
Recent labour code changes affected Q3 gratuity and tax; Q4 PAT included a Rs 1.3 crore tax benefit that will not recur.

Scanner business is for us an enabler.

rows.why: US is about 20% of revenue and management says more DSOs are being added, though they will not be announced individually; US tariff fell to about 10% from about 50%, and the Heartland contract is unchanged.

544339|2026-06.headline: Laxmi Dental Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13.9% y-o-y to about INR75 crore, a record, with EBITDA margin at 19.2% and PAT up 23.8%.
544339|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue, with consolidated revenue from operations of INR74.7 crore against INR65.6 crore a year earlier. Gross margin was 78.6% and EBITDA rose 20.6% y-o-y to INR14.4 crore at a 19.2% margin, helped by favourable mix and a scanner trading contribution. Dental lab grew 23.5% y-o-y, with international up 37.4%, while aligners grew 28.6%. Management flagged a new US CEO hire, a planned Palghar land purchase to replace rented facilities, and FY27 scanner deployment of 800 to 1,000 units. The company remains debt-free.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR65.6 crore in Q1 FY26 (about +13.9% y-o-y)
vs INR12.5 crore in Q1 FY26; driven by freight, ECL provisions and AI automation
vs INR14.8 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Dental lab
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 23.5% y-o-y across domestic and international. Domestic lab excluding scanners grew about 12% y-o-y in Q1, per the analyst's question and management's confirmation.

segments.name: International (within dental lab)
segments.commentary: Grew 37.4% y-o-y. CFO said USD moved from about INR85 to INR95, roughly 12% y-o-y currency tailwind, so constant-currency growth is lower but still strong.

segments.name: Aligner solutions
segments.commentary: Grew 28.6% y-o-y. Bizdent grew 27.8% and Vedia grew 29.3%. Management linked growth to the iScope at-home monitoring launch and dentist education.

segments.name: Kids-e-Dental (paediatric)
segments.commentary: Grew 54.4% y-o-y in the quarter. The company holds 60% of its PAT in its adjusted EBITDA calculation.

segments.name: Scanners (trading)
segments.commentary: Sold at about INR3 lakh average to dentists with a trading margin of about 15% to 20%. Scanner mix causes quarter-to-quarter margin swings.

Scanner deployment of 800 to 1,000 units targeted for FY27, with the company saying it is on track.
AI-led automation costs are elevated this year and expected to fall next year as scale rises.

No disruption to revenue or productivity expected during the transition, which will be phased. Management cited a 2020 export-unit move from Kandivali to Boisar as precedent.
Aligner capacity utilisation about 70%, with reasonable headroom. Lab utilisation is at a constant 90% to 95% because of custom work.
Digital penetration in domestic network about 75% to 80% (dental lab and aligner combined); international is mostly digital.

qa_highlights.answer: The CFO confirmed the margin uses total income including other income (about INR10.55 crore) as the denominator. Excluding other income the EBITDA margin is about 34%, so the reported 31% is on the total-income basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why were trade-show and marketing costs reduced, and why did other expenses rise about 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Middle East trade-show commitments were cut because of the West Asia situation and spend was redirected to demand gen, US/UK/Europe events. Other expenses rose because Middle East staff are supplied via a third party (technical fees) and marketing spend was reallocated, not cut.

qa_highlights.question: What are the parameters for M&A and Epitome's margin effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described four criteria: services company with some IP, majority export revenue, profitable and growing, and a technology or domain specialisation. The CFO said targets must have EBITDA margins in line with the company and bring synergy and new technology or manpower. Management said margins would improve post-deal.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there no buyback given the cash position, and what is the dividend policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no buyback is planned for now, with capital directed to growth and acquisitions. The CFO said the dividend payout is intended to be about 20-25% of profit, including the final dividend, and a buyback may be reconsidered in about a year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 target breakdown and the three-year plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 35% is a combined organic and inorganic guidance and a three-year aim of INR200 crore top line with a stable or better margin. The CFO said the 'medium term' reference meant one year, for which 35% growth is projected.

risks_watch: Organic growth: FY26 growth was largely from pricing and the Middle East; FY27 depends on INR20-25 crore net new revenue and the slipped large ramp-ups.
Epitome integration: completion in 8-12 weeks and a Salesforce revenue-operations niche with only 7 onsite US staff; the EBITDA impact and the PAT contribution are not disclosed.
Margin: the 33% FY27 target includes other income, so operating margin is lower (about 24% ex-other income per an analyst's calculation); other income of INR10.55 crore is a large share of PBT.
Middle East: the top-five client exposure with teams no longer travelling; BFSI concentration.
Share price weakness below the IPO price and questions on shareholder returns; no buyback planned.
Use of about INR170 crore cash across acquisitions versus organic investment; capital allocation policy not fully defined.
544343|2026-03.management_tone: Management was candid about the miss versus internal expectations and explained it as slipped deal closures and Middle East disruption. The tone turned assertive on the FY27 35% target, the Epitome deal and the acquisition pipeline, but was evasive on share price, buybacks and the organic growth split.
key_quotes: During the second half of financial year '26, we expected elongated enterprise decision-making cycles and delayed ramp -ups in certain large engagements, some of which now shifted into financial year '27.
So the projection that I am giving of 35% is basically the most pessimistic projection and we will revise it as the company -- as the situation evolves in the future.
Financial year 26 was the year of investment, capability building and strategic positioning of the company.

rows.why: Management targets EBITDA margin recovering gradually toward 33% (on total income incl. other income of INR10.55 cr) from 31% in FY26, but Middle East investments, Gurgaon expansion, senior hires and AI build-out are weighing on costs and an analyst estimates ~24% ex-other income.

rows.why: Epitome Cloud adds ~55 people (7 onsite US, ~45 India) and ~INR28-30 cr revenue, completion expected in 8-12 weeks, and a physical US office is planned after the deal.

rows.why: Guidance of minimum 35% revenue growth (called pessimistic) backed by Epitome's ~INR28-30 cr target revenue (25-30% uplift) plus INR20-25 cr organic net new revenue after ~10% churn on a base of INR105.05 cr; FY26 revenue grew only ~5% (INR99.7 cr to INR105.05 cr) as large ramp-ups slipped into FY27.

rows.why: Cash and investments of ~INR171.3 cr, debt-free, and management plans 2-3 further AI/fintech/healthtech acquisitions, but no capex plan or utilisation figure was disclosed; the INR40 cr Epitome deal is an acquisition, not capacity capex.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management called 35% a pessimistic case and subject to revision, but FY26 revenue missed internal expectations as enterprise decision cycles elongated and ramp-ups slipped, so an upgrade needs evidence of conversion from 500 qualified leads with 6-12 month deal cycles still pending.

rows.why: Organic growth depends on INR20-25 cr net new revenue, Middle East (~11% of revenue, top-five client, BFSI only) new-logo acquisition is on hold, and FY26 revenue missed internal expectations.

rows.why: Two Fortune 500 wins in FY26 (healthcare analytics/warehouse management; UiPath automation) and ~500 qualified leads from 9 trade shows, but 6-12 month deal cycles mean conversions are still pending.

rows.why: INR40 cr consideration funded by IPO proceeds and internal accruals with no external debt, completion in 8-12 weeks; management plans two to three more acquisitions in AI with fintech or healthtech focus.

rows.why: Large enterprise ramp-ups slipped from FY26 into FY27 and deal cycles elongated, which supports the FY27 revenue step-up if they convert as guided.

tone.note: Management was candid about the FY26 miss and confident on the 35% FY27 target, Epitome and the M&A pipeline, but evasive on share price, buybacks and the organic vs inorganic split, which analysts pressed on alongside margin dilution and the Middle East exposure.

544344|2026-06.headline: SPR Auto Technologies Q1 FY27: consolidated total income up 51% YoY and EBITDA up 27% YoY, with PAT up 9% after higher finance costs.
544344|2026-06.overview: Management reported 51% YoY growth in consolidated total income and 27% YoY growth in consolidated EBITDA for Q1 FY27. Consolidated PBT rose 7% and PAT rose 9% YoY, with higher finance costs from the debt used to fund the automotive interiors and lighting (Antolin) acquisition. Management attributed a near-term margin squeeze to commodity cost pass-through lagging by about a quarter, which it said it expects to recover next quarter. Standalone legacy growth of about 12% trailed the industry, which management attributed to mix shifts and weak exports.

financial_highlights.value: INR 300 million (per investor presentation, as cited by analyst)

financial_highlights.metric: Powertrain-agnostic businesses share of consolidated total income

segments.name: Legacy engine components (standalone)
segments.commentary: Management said manufacturing growth in the industry was about 12-14% against company growth of over 16%, though the analyst cited ~12% standalone growth. Two-wheelers grew ~19-20%, passenger cars ~11%, CV and tractor ~7-8%, and other segments ~4-5% (per management). Exports were hit by the West Asia situation.

segments.name: Automotive interiors and lighting (Antolin)
segments.commentary: Margins improved from 7-8% to early-to-mid teens after synergies and fixed-cost cuts. Management said the segment won several new customer programs post-acquisition. Ex-Antolin consolidated topline growth was said to be over 16%.

segments.name: Electric motors and controllers (EMFI)
segments.commentary: Management said the business doubled turnover in FY26 after Coimbatore capacity commissioned by end-December 2025, and expects full-year benefit in FY27. Management declined to disclose capacity or market share.

segments.name: High precision injection molded components / plastics (Takahata, TGPEL)
segments.commentary: Management said the injection-molded business saw very significant growth in Q1 and that plastics revenue grew about 2x last year. Takahata phase-four expansion has started, with new business revenue expected from early next year; TGPEL second Noida plant is filling up.

segments.name: Non-auto components
segments.commentary: Management said non-auto (compressors, marine, defense, railways, snowmobiles, lawn mowers, medical, music keyboards) has grown 15-20% a year over four years, but did not disclose its share of revenue.

guidance_outlook: Management expects volume momentum after GST 2.0 to continue through FY27 across two-wheeler, passenger car, CV and tractor segments.
Commodity cost increases are passed to customers with a one-quarter lag; management hopes the gap normalises in the current quarter (Q2 FY27).
Finance costs are expected to be temporary and normalise as acquisition-related debt is repaid.
Management said export markets (US, Europe, Middle East, Turkey, Egypt) have not yet recovered and expects normalisation to take more time.
Management expects to recover the lost margin from commodity inflation and said it will not lose margin.
Management said it targets consolidated EBITDA margins in the high teens and aims for Antolin margins closer to mid-teens.
capex_capacity: Acquired the piston manufacturing plant and machinery from Sunbeam Lightweighting Solutions Ltd; completed in Q1 FY27, adding piston capacity.
Capacity expansion underway across plastics, EV motors and controllers, interiors and legacy pistons; management did not disclose capacity figures.
Takahata phase-four expansion started, building a new plant adjacent to the existing facility on five acres of additional land; new business revenue expected from early next year.
TGPEL: second Noida plant has full capacity available and is filling up.
EMFI: Coimbatore capacity commissioned around end-December 2025.
Legacy CAFE-compliant piston and ring coating technologies already available at Ghaziabad and Pathredi plants; management said products are under customer testing and validation.
Management said all the tested flex-fuel products up to E85 are ready, requiring different plating with capacity already available.
demand_pricing: Management said realisation may rise to some extent with newer CAFE-compliant technologies, which cost more; management said it is leading the competition on these.
Mix shift toward smaller vehicles post GST 2.0 lowered value realisation per piece, per management.
Management said commodity prices have started to fall from unprecedented levels, and it expects normalisation within the next quarter.
Standalone gross margin was around 56-57% in the past two quarters versus 59-61% historically; management attributed this to product mix and commodity impact.
Management said it has back-to-back pass-through arrangements with customers across legacy, plastics, motors and interiors, with a one-quarter lag.
Management said the Q1 wage hike, effective 1 April, had a small impact on employee cost percentage.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone legacy growth (~12%) trail the industry growth of ~20% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said manufacturing growth was 12-14% versus company growth over 16%, and that exports were hit by the war situation, so manufacturing shifted toward OE customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone gross margin hold while EBITDA margin fell ~200 bps QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a mix of product, market, and volume effects, plus aftermarket lag in Q1 and the commodity pass-through lag.

qa_highlights.question: Is any price increase needed from OEMs to recover the commodity impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said back-to-back contracts exist with a one-quarter lag, so the increase for the prior quarter's average commodity price is recovered the following quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is net debt and what are the leverage thresholds?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated net debt was about INR 550 crore as of June; net debt to equity is 0.2x, and management said it will not cross 1x.

qa_highlights.question: How is the fundraise going to be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said funds are fungible and will be split across acquisitions, debt repayment and ongoing investments; no split was given. It said the fundraise is progressing as per target.

risks_watch: Commodity-cost pass-through lag: management expects normalisation in Q2 FY27, so the Q2 margin is a key check.
Export weakness in the US, Europe and Middle East, with no clear recovery timeline per management.
Finance cost burden from acquisition debt, which management said will normalise over time; watch the repayment schedule.
Standalone legacy growth trailing industry manufacturing growth in Q1.
Undisclosed segment breakup: management declined to give plastics, Antolin and EMFI revenue and EBITDA for the quarter.
544344|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand, integration and margin recovery, but evasive on specifics: management declined to give segment splits, EMFI capacity, market share, non-auto revenue share and the wage-cost impact. On exports, it was candid that recovery is slow.

We are not going to lose on our margins.
So, we have outgrown the industry even as we speak.
At present it is only 0.2x. So, we don't see any reason why we have to even go up to 1x.
I'd really request all of you to reach out to our secretarial department for the questions so that we can answer back one on one.

rows.why: Management said these export markets have not yet recovered and normalisation will take more time after the West Asia situation hit exports.

544344|2026-09.headline: Consolidated total income rose 61% YoY to INR 16,746 million in Q2 FY27, with EBITDA up 29% to INR 3,004 million, though margin fell to 17.9%.
544344|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated total income grew 61% YoY to INR 16,746 million and EBITDA rose 29% to INR 3,004 million, with H1 total income at INR 31,738 million (up 56%). Growth was helped by the three Antolin India entities acquired recently, while standalone total income grew 17% YoY to INR 10,500 million. EBITDA margin was 17.9%, hit by commodity and direct material costs, a sales mix shift toward OEM and minimum wage revisions, with management calling much of this timing-related. Finance costs of INR 234 million in Q2 (INR 486 million in H1) from acquisition debt weighed on PBT, which management says would have grown 23% in Q2 excluding it. A QIP of INR 10,000 million was completed in late August.

segments.name: Standalone powertrain components (pistons, pins, rings, valves)
segments.commentary: Total income up 17% YoY to INR 10,500 million in Q2, in line with the weighted industry production growth of about 17%. Standalone EBITDA margin was 19.9% per management, versus about 21% earlier, as mix shifted toward OEM.

segments.name: High-precision injection molded components
segments.commentary: Gaining from ABS-related demand for 2-wheelers. New Neemrana plant to supply by April, as customers need parts in place by then.

segments.name: EV motors and controllers (TGPEL, Coimbatore)
segments.commentary: Scaling through new Coimbatore facility and a growing customer base. TGPEL capex is ongoing; no figures disclosed.

segments.name: Automotive interiors and lighting (Antolin India, 3 entities)
segments.commentary: Acquired entities are delivering strong operational and financial performance and new customer wins. Lighting is growing faster than the rest of interiors and was close to 20% of interiors revenue at acquisition. Headliner speakerless acoustic technology is at proof-of-concept with 2-3 customers.

guidance_outlook: Management expects piston growth to moderate to a 7-8% CAGR over the next two years, not the 17-20% seen in FY27, citing the high base.
New business wins are expected to add over INR 1,000 crore of mature-year revenue, on top of the existing base of about INR 6,000 crore.
Management expects finance costs to normalise as debt is repaid, with some improvement expected from Q3 FY27.
Management expects to grow in line with or ahead of end markets; it does not give capex figures.
Management is not planning to raise further debt or equity now, but is evaluating acquisitions.
Commodity pass-through lags by about one quarter; a fall in aluminium prices may not add much to margins.
capex_capacity: Capacity additions are under way at Pithampur, Pathredi (recently expanded), Ghaziabad (precision injection molding), a new plant next to the existing Neemrana facility, TGPEL, and Antolin interiors.
Management declined to give an FY27 capex figure, calling it 'very sizable' and subject to change with ongoing decisions.
Capacity is being added ahead of demand; management says there should be no capacity constraint going forward.
Raw material is held for at least 3 months of production in precision plastics, which weighs on working capital.
demand_pricing: Domestic auto production rose about 17% on a weighted-average basis; PV, CV, 2W and 3W all posted record Q2 sales.
Standalone capacity utilisation is around 75-80%, and an OEM surge forced a shift in mix away from aftermarket and exports.
Raw material costs (aluminium, copper, steel, plastics, tools and oils) are passed through to customers with about a one-quarter lag, with recovery described as near 100%.
Gross margin fell to around 55-56% from about 60%. Management could not split the decline between mix and timing lag.
Management expects EV penetration to rise from about 9-10% to 15-16% by 2030, while ICE demand continues.
Headliner content per vehicle is 15-18% higher for small cars and 30-40% higher for larger vehicles (management's estimate).

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 capex plans, and why did trade payables fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no capex figure, calling it 'very sizable'. Working capital is described as normal across the group, and raw material stock of at least 3 months was held in precision plastics.

qa_highlights.question: Can 10-12% piston growth be sustained over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth would moderate to a 7-8% CAGR in the next two years because of the high FY27 base, and that it does not expect 17-20% to continue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the RM impact in Q2 and the outlook for Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RM costs are fully passed through on a one-quarter lag. Aluminium prices are falling, but oil- and tool-linked costs are rising, so the net Q3 effect depends on the war.

qa_highlights.question: Will standalone EBITDA margin stay around 18%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said standalone margin was 19.9% in Q2, near 20% and among the best in the industry, and that the 1-2 point drop was mainly mix.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company raise debt or equity for acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no debt or equity raise is planned now, the balance sheet is strong, and acquisitions are being evaluated.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company keep growing after Antolin is consolidated in the base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to outgrow end markets, with growth depending on wins and mix, including lighting and complete-assembly interiors modules.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a defence or aerospace opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees defence as the focus, supplying Shaktiman trucks and the Avadi vehicle factory, but volumes are limited. Aerospace needs 3-5 years of qualification and is not the focus.

risks_watch: Gross margin trend (about 55-56%) and whether the mix and time-lag effects reverse.
Middle East war effects on oil, tool and direct material costs, which are not yet recovered.
Finance cost normalisation in Q3 FY27 as acquisition debt is repaid.
Capacity build-out (Neemrana precision plastics, Ghaziabad, Pithampur, TGPEL, Antolin) and execution.
Minimum wage and gratuity impact on employee costs, with management saying it is fully absorbed.
Piston growth moderating to 7-8% after the FY27 high base.
544344|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on growth and volumes, with a cautious note on margins and commodity exposure. Management was evasive on specific capex, order-win details and the split of margin decline between mix and timing lag.
key_quotes: Commodity movements are usually passed through to our customers under back-to-back arrangements with a lag of about a quarter.
So I expect that the next 2 years will get more or less toned down to the CAGR to achieve a total CAGR of around 7% to 8%.

We are putting capacities almost in all the areas, including our legacy business because even with the legacy business, we see that with a 7% or 8% market growth and kind of penetration that we have in the electric segment, we will still require more ICE engines in 2030 and 2032.

rows.why: Management says new business wins should add over INR 1,000 crore of mature-year revenue, about 17% on the existing ~INR 6,000 crore base, though order details were evasive.

rows.label: Finance cost normalisation as acquisition debt is repaid
rows.why: Finance costs were INR 234 million in Q2 and INR 486 million in H1 from Antolin acquisition debt, and management expects improvement from Q3 FY27 with no new debt planned.

rows.why: Defence is the stated focus with supply to Shaktiman and Avadi, but management says volumes are limited, and aerospace needs 3-5 years of qualification.

544345|2026-03.headline: Denta FY26 revenue rose over 23% to Rs 2,503.8 mn with order book of Rs 7,278 mn, but Q4 EBITDA margin fell to about 19%, and management gave no firm order-inflow guidance.
544345|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue from operations of Rs 2,503.8 mn (over 23% growth), EBITDA of Rs 834.9 mn and PAT of Rs 609 mn, with an order book of about Rs 7,278 mn across 38 ongoing projects as of March 31, 2026. Analysts pressed on a sharp Q3/Q4 run-rate slowdown and a Q4 EBITDA margin of about 19% versus roughly 33% in the first three quarters, which management attributed to the Iran-US war, petroleum-linked raw material costs and a mix shift to smaller projects. Order-book inflow was described as pending new tenders under the new Karnataka government, with no order value committed. Working capital of about Rs 295 crore (inventory, receivables and other assets) is expected to convert largely in December-January, and management guided to about 20% FY27 revenue growth with an EBITDA margin of around 25%.

segments.name: Water management (core)
segments.commentary: Management says about 90% of the water order book sits in the water sector, covering drinking water, STP, irrigation and tank regeneration. The company has bagged 3-4 FTP projects covering about 15-16 cities in Karnataka.

segments.name: Amrut 2 and Jal Jivan Mission
segments.commentary: One Amrut 2 order of Rs 232 crore (Kuknuru and Yelburga, Koppal) and four Jal Jivan Mission projects in Karnataka. Management says about 70% of these projects is complete, with the balance 30% targeted this year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 20% stated as the minimum projection; closing remarks cited a 20-25% target.
EBITDA margin guided at about 25% (confirmed in Q&A), down from about 33% run-rate in Q1-Q3 FY26.
No firm order-inflow number given; management expects to announce new orders shortly and aims for a healthy order-book increase by end-March 2027.
Management declined to give an absolute FY27 profit figure, saying it depends on project execution and raw material investment.
Government payments expected to accelerate from July-August 2026, with many payments in Q2-Q3 FY27, per management.
Possible price-escalation relief for HDPE/PVC items expected in July or Q2 FY27, per management.
capex_capacity: Inventory, receivables and other assets of about Rs 295 crore are tied up in working capital; management expects about 60% (about Rs 200 crore) to be realised in FY27, mainly by December-January.
Payment on supply is roughly 55% after material is laid, with the balance 35% on laying and the remainder on completion, per management.
Company is adopting NEBR and CAMUS-based STP technologies, claiming about 95% purity, largely through subcontracting to patent holders.
Bidding pipeline of about 5-6 projects worth about Rs 600 crore; management is aggressively bidding for 5-6 tenders and 2-3 major tenders.
Four to five projects identified in Madhya Pradesh under the National Water Management Programme (NWMP); a Mahanadi barrage tender in Odisha is yet to be floated.
demand_pricing: Karnataka's new government (formed late May/early June 2026) is expected to push infrastructure tenders after a roughly six-month slowdown.
Raw material risk: 20-30% of raw material is UPVC and HDPE pipe, with prices up in Q4 FY26, April and May 2026 after the Iran-US war; some suppliers seeking higher prices.
Price escalation clauses exist on projects above Rs 100 crore but not on smaller projects, per management.
Management said the company is taking smaller-value projects (Rs 10-50 crore) alongside larger ones (up to Rs 300 crore), which dilutes margin.
Q3 and Q4 FY26 execution slowdown was attributed to war-related disruption and irregular payments.

qa_highlights.question: Trajectory of order flow and government payment status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is aggressively bidding for 5-6 tenders and expects to announce new orders in the coming quarter; payments are expected to pick up from July-August 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Margin trajectory and FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management first said margin would be maintained around 30%, then confirmed a 25% EBITDA margin guidance for FY27 after repeated questioning; it said smaller projects will dilute margin.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital liquidation timeline (Rs 295 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects cash in December-January, with about 60% (about Rs 200 crore) targeted in FY27, after laying and completion of projects by October.

qa_highlights.question: Order book fall from Rs 841 crore (Dec 2025) to Rs 727 crore (Mar 2026)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the reduction to revenue conversion and investment in completing old projects, and said the audit team would provide the exact reconciliation; it did not confirm any cancellation.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 revenue and profit outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to a minimum of 20% revenue growth but declined to give an absolute profit number, saying it depends on project implementation and raw material investment.

544350|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue crossed INR 2,000 crore (up 21.6% to INR 2,080 crore) with PAT up 52.4% to INR 168 crore; FY27 plans 60 new facilities.
544350|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue from operations up 22.6% YoY to INR 564-565 crore, with Ind AS EBITDA of INR 174 crore (30.2% margin, the highest quarterly margin of the year) despite 19 facility openings. Full-year FY26 revenue from operations reached INR 2,080 crore, EBITDA INR 614 crore (28.9% margin) and PAT INR 168 crore (7.9% margin). Same-store sales growth was about 14%, split roughly equally between volume and value. Management guided to FY27 growth at a similar pace to FY26, EBITDA margins stable, 60 new facilities (40 surgical, 20 clinics), and a merger timeline of roughly Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex breakdown and the acquisition-related cash outflow?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is INR 380-400 crore including the CMS facility; acquisition payments are about INR 60-65 crore, versus about INR 85 crore in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What losses do new greenfield facilities carry, and will they recur?
qa_highlights.answer: New FY26 branches had unit-level operating losses of about INR 30 crore (FY25 cohort about INR 21 crore). Management expects a similar drag in FY27, with per-branch losses falling from FY27 onwards, mainly in Delhi.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise in the listed subsidiary?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 one-off merger costs of about INR 80 lakh; corporate office rent of about INR 1 crore for the year; about INR 3.3 crore extra Facebook marketing spend. Merger costs are one-off, rent recurs.

qa_highlights.question: Are the FY27 facility additions all organic, and how many facilities closed in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: All 60 planned centres are organic; partner deals are not in the pipeline. Five eye clinics were closed in FY26, and AEHL's rental outflow for FY27 is about INR 32 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What limits the pace of openings?
qa_highlights.answer: Real estate at the right cost and compliance with state clinical licences, which can delay openings. Management will ramp up only if the new centres perform.

Paramedical attrition of 21-25% and fixed increments of about 9.5-10%.

544350|2026-06.headline: Dr. Agarwal's Q1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 26% YoY to INR614 crores, with Ind AS EBITDA of INR177 crores (28.5% margin) and PAT margin at 8.9%.
544350|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 delivered revenue from operations of INR614 crores (+26% YoY, +8.8% QoQ) and Ind AS EBITDA of INR177 crores (+25.2% YoY), with EBITDA margin up 30 bps to 28.5%. PAT margin expanded 127 bps to 8.9% despite greenfield losses of about INR20 crores at corporate EBITDA level. The company commissioned 18 new facilities (16 surgical), a record for a single quarter, and reiterated a FY27 plan of 60 additions including 40 surgical centres. Same-store growth for the oldest cohort (pre-FY23) was 16.3%, driven roughly equally by volume and value.
