qa_highlights.answer: COO Rahul Agarwal said premiumisation contributed about 7.5% and price hikes about 0.5% so far this year, so close to 8% like-to-like value growth against about 15-16% volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: What are the losses from new facilities?
qa_highlights.answer: Greenfield losses are about INR20 crores at corporate EBITDA level, covering FY26 and FY27 centres and including pre-operating losses.

qa_highlights.question: What were the deferred consideration payments and lease interest?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Yashwanth Venkat said about INR25 crores of acquisition liabilities were paid in Q1, and lease liability interest was about INR18 crores; interest on deferred acquisition payables fell to INR3.6 crores from INR6.8 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Is the North growth only from Delhi NCR?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO Adil Agarwal said Delhi is a new entry, growing from one branch last year to seven now, and Punjab and J&K rebounded from the prior-year Operation Sindoor and flood impact; growth is broad-based across North branches.

qa_highlights.question: Will doctor additions drive future revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most of the doctor additions are for new centres and productivity should improve as centres mature; senior doctor attrition is 2-3% versus 16-17% group-wide attrition including juniors.

qa_highlights.question: Can realisation growth of about 10% continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth should continue, while value growth depends on lens upgrades and Femto adoption; it could not confirm whether 10% or 8% realisation growth would persist, but the direction is upward.

qa_highlights.question: Why is facility addition pace constrained given cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is working to raise launch pace and has a pipeline, but some sites require strict compliance clearances before launch.

Greenfield drag: about INR20 crores of losses at corporate EBITDA level, including pre-operating losses, while 16 surgical centres were added in one quarter; margin resilience depends on these ramping.
Doctor productivity: about 1,057 doctors (+23% YoY) with 100 added in four months; group attrition at 16-17%, with senior doctor attrition at 2-3%. New-centre productivity is still to be shown.
Merger closure targeted around mid-November 2026; management gave no detail on terms or impact on the reported numbers.

Delhi NCR and North: growth partly reflects Delhi being a new entry and a rebound from Operation Sindoor and floods in the prior year, and management said Delhi is a long way from South-level maturity.

544350|2026-09.headline: Dr. Agarwal's Q2 FY27 revenue rose 31.4% YoY to INR 655 crores, with PAT up 55.8% to INR 57 crores and facility guidance raised to 65 additions.
544350|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 31.4% YoY to INR 655 crores, with Ind AS EBITDA up 28.8% to INR 186 crores at a stable margin near 28%. PAT rose 55.8% YoY to INR 57 crores, with PAT margin up about 134 bps to 8.5%, despite start-up losses at newer centres. Management added 21 facilities in Q2 (19 Greenfield plus 2 acquired in Delhi NCR) and raised FY27 guidance to 65 facility additions, including 55 surgical centres, with capex raised from INR 400 crores to INR 500 crores. SSSG was 18.8% in Q2 and 17.7% in H1, and the company disclosed its first acquisition in a while (INR 55 crores, two Delhi NCR centres).

qa_highlights.question: What is the steel and pricing outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Steel prices rose; management hopes for softening after US primaries in September-November; a calibrated price increase is planned, likely starting within Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Are inorganic opportunities being pursued aggressively given the cash?

Steel and fuel cost inflation with unclear timing of price increases and possible competitive pushback.
Government payment delays to contractors and under-spending on infrastructure.
Recovery of deferred non-SLCM volumes expected August-September; need to verify.
Export revenue recognition timing and country/currency risk.
Investor-call audio quality issues reported by several participants during the call.

544362|2026-09.headline: Hexaware Q3 CY26 revenue rose 1.6% QoQ to $411.9M, below plan; adjusted EBIT margin 13.8%; no current-quarter guidance given.
544362|2026-09.overview: Hexaware's Q3 CY26 (quarter ended September 2026) revenue was $411.9M, up 1.6% QoQ and 4.3% YoY, which management called below its own expectations due to a GSE client slowdown and delayed large-deal ramps. Adjusted EBIT margin was 13.8% (reported 12.2%) after 160 bps of one-offs including the Netherlands restructuring, earn-out reversals and CEO transition. The company narrowed its CY26 adjusted EBIT margin guidance to 13% to 13.5% and declined to give a Q4 outlook. New CEO Vivek Jetley, in his first call, committed to a 90-day strategy review and tighter forecasting process.

segments.name: Financial Services
segments.commentary: Grew 3.0% QoQ and 2.4% YoY; a GSE client under cost optimisation is a headwind expected to persist in Q4, so FY growth expected below company average.

segments.name: Healthcare & Insurance
segments.commentary: Declined 40 bps QoQ on lower asset revenue but grew 6.3% YoY; management expects it to be among the strongest YoY drivers for FY, though decisions have been delayed in H&I.

segments.name: Manufacturing & Consumer
segments.commentary: Grew 1.8% QoQ and 3% YoY, fifth consecutive quarter of YoY growth; deal closures converting to revenue.

segments.name: Professional Services
segments.commentary: Broadly stable QoQ (normal seasonality after strong Q2 from largest client); 7.8% YoY growth.

segments.name: Banking
segments.commentary: Grew 6.6% QoQ and 13.5% YoY; management expects a strong Q4 and full year.

segments.name: Travel & Transportation
segments.commentary: Declined 3.5% QoQ and 8.5% YoY on end-client softness and Middle East conflict; expected soft for full year.

segments.name: TPP (Technology Products & Platforms)
segments.commentary: Grew 7.2% QoQ and 9.7% YoY; reported separately since this year on a smaller base.

segments.name: Geographies
segments.commentary: Americas +1.5% QoQ, +1.1% YoY; Europe +3.1% QoQ, +12.8% YoY; Asia Pacific +20% YoY, with GTT softness in APAC from the Middle East situation.

guidance_outlook: No guidance given for Q4 CY26; management says Q4 will follow the usual seasonal pattern with furloughs and fewer working days causing a sequential decline.

Sales incentives: hunting team moved from quota-based to commission-based plan earlier this year; to be reviewed.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add or double down on service lines or verticals, and change sales incentives?
qa_highlights.answer: New CEO will run a 90-day strategy review covering where to play, competition, go-to-market and delivery focus, and investments; hunting team already moved to commission-based pay.

qa_highlights.question: With Q3 at 1.7% growth, what Q4 traction would be needed to meet the ~6-7% guidance, which implies a 4-5% ask rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number and said Q4 should follow the usual seasonal sequential decline from furloughs and fewer working days.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue impact from liquidating Mobiquity Netherlands?
qa_highlights.answer: Marginal revenue impact, as work had already moved offshore; restructuring was needed because costs could not be cut in line with declining revenue under Dutch labour law.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q3 miss a broad-based slowdown in deal ramps or client-specific, and how to assess the momentum?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ramp delay is one account only (rebadging deal) and the pipeline and momentum are intact; deals slipped into Q4 or Q1 due to client decision cycles.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a process change needed after repeated guidance misses?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Jetley said he is still reviewing root causes; will tighten the sales-to-forecast process and expand safety margins in forecasts.

qa_highlights.question: How are the recent acquisitions (SMC, CyberSolve) performing and what drove the earn-out adjustments?
qa_highlights.answer: SMC (GCC capability) fell short of year-two targets, giving a 530 bps earn-out reversal as clients slowed GCC setups amid AI; CyberSolve outperformed, causing a 110 bps extra charge. Net 420 bps credit in other income, offset by 140 bps amortisation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the growth slowdown due to weak demand and aggressive competitor bidding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed slowdown mainly to vendor consolidation and client-specific timing; said it is a buyer's market with pricing pressure in initial phases, but incumbents tend to lose more than challengers.

544367|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue crossed INR 1,000 crore (INR 1,007 cr, +157% YoY) with 23.5% EBITDA margin, despite a INR 25.7 crore non-cash Ind AS 29 charge.
544367|2026-03.overview: Management reported first-ever INR 1,000 crore+ annual consolidated revenue, FY26 EBITDA of INR 236 crore (up 98%) and PAT of INR 185 crore (up 85%), above the revised guidance of about INR 900 crore revenue and 22% margin. Q4 was the highest-ever quarter at about INR 310 crore total revenue, but consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 19.1% from 27.9% in Q3 because of a INR 25.7 crore Ind AS 29 net monetary loss at Turkish subsidiary Endoks and one-time Labour Code provisions. Order book exiting FY26 was above INR 1,400 crore. FY27 guidance is muted at about 15-20% growth as new capacity ramps, with management expecting above 50% growth in FY28.

segments.name: Quality Power (standalone, incl. projects)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR 246 crore per management; EBIT margin about 33% for Quality Power and 21% for QP projects. Order book above INR 520 crore, with data-centre order book about INR 520 crore cited in Q&A.

segments.name: Mehru Electrical and Mechanical Engineers
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR 318 crore; margin about 20% in Q4 and 15% for the year; annualised EBIT margin about 15%. Order book about INR 430 crore; management sees only 30-35% further capacity headroom at current plant.

segments.name: Endoks Energy (Turkey)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR 468 crore; reported EBIT margin 23% including Ind AS 29 effect, about 29-30% without it; management cites about 32% EBITDA on stable-currency basis. Order book about INR 450 crore; Q4 cash flow about INR 136 crore.

segments.name: Sukrut (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Turnaround underway; losses halved versus last year and management targets 70-75% growth this year without losses.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: about 15-20% growth in revenue and margin band of 15-20%, reflecting an S-curve stabilisation year; growth to resume above 50% in FY28 (management said this is 'correct' when asked).
Order book target of INR 1,500-1,800 crore before start of FY27 per management.
Expect some near-term gross margin pressure in Q1-Q2 FY27 from raw material and commodity price increases; pass-through to customers is with a lag.

Targeted BESS converter orders of USD 60-80 million this year against USD 31 million current BESS order book; PCS factory in Turkey (about USD 2 million investment) expected to start billing by Q4 FY26 or Q1 FY27.
Dividend: final dividend of INR 1 per share recommended; promoters waived their entitlement.
capex_capacity: New Sangli factory (global coil, HVDC, PCS, CTC, magnet wire) expected to commence operations around July-August 2026; management also said trial production by end-2026 and project managers stick to Dec-Jan start; commissioning on track for Q3 FY27 per CFO.
New high-voltage test laboratory to be commissioned alongside the new factory.

Mehru: additional oven capacity post-September 2026; GIS manufacturing and testing infrastructure with first prototypes around July-August 2026; INR 17.2 crore capex for GIS and HV testing equipment. Current plant saturation at about 30-35% above FY26 output of about INR 320 crore.
Endoks: new PCS facility at Nigde targeted for December 2026; new BESS manufacturing facility on in-house technology; 1,725 kW PCS inverter expected to launch within next two quarters.
Capital WIP of INR 73 crore; management says Sangli peak revenue potential of about INR 1,500 crore subject to CTC cable expansion and insulator supply.
demand_pricing: Order book exiting FY26 above INR 1,400 crore (about 1.4x FY26 revenue); Q4 order intake about INR 870 crore per corrected figure, with INR 300 crore executed in the quarter.
Pipeline of opportunities above INR 1,100 crore for QP alone across FACTS, renewables and data centres; demand cited across Middle East, Europe, US and Australia.
BESS: management sees BESS PCS as 40-50% of project cost; converter margins about 10-12% at bid level, targeted to reach 17-18% at volume; battery pass-through about 2-3%.

Data centres: first US data-centre order of about INR 49 crore won; management expects a couple more projects in coming quarters; US reactor market for data centres sized at about INR 1,500 crore per year by management.

Supply chain constraints: insulator deliveries running 18-24 months; cable constraints mitigated by vertical integration. Order intake in Sangli and Delhi largely closed for next quarter; only strategic orders being taken.
Transformer bids in US (USD 80-100 million) were largely lost; management is not prioritising transformers at lower margins.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the BESS and data-centre opportunity and what products will be supplied?
qa_highlights.answer: BESS order book about USD 31 million with a further USD 30-50 million expected by year-end; management targets USD 60-80 million of orders this year and sees a billion-dollar opportunity. Data-centre orders are booked out with 6-7 month delivery timelines.

qa_highlights.question: Who are the BESS competitors?
qa_highlights.answer: Chinese players are seen as the largest competition; GE is at a high price level and not yet competed with directly. Company says it competes on software/EMS and service in Europe, US and Australia.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance for FY27 revenue and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance of about 15-20% growth in FY27; traditional HV margins are steady with a couple of points of pressure from conflict-related price increases; BESS converter margins are in an investment phase.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 revenue flat QoQ and what is the Endoks seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Mehru's Q4 is its highest-profit quarter and Endoks' Q1 is seasonally muted; it reports Endoks on a Jan-Dec basis so QoQ comparison is not like-for-like.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fundraising plan given about INR 250 crore cash?
qa_highlights.answer: The USD 75 million enabling resolution is a dry-powder authorisation, not an immediate raise; company says it will draw much lower than the cap, cash is needed for organic growth and acquisitions, and it prefers zero debt.

qa_highlights.question: What is the other expenses increase in Q4 beyond the Ind AS 29 charge?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said freight outward of about INR 12 crore and liquidated damages of about INR 5 crore (pre-acquisition Mehru item, since curtailed) also rose other expenses; net monetary loss was INR 25 crore.

risks_watch: Ind AS 29 treatment at Endoks creates quarter-to-quarter swings in other expenses and reported margins (Q3 net monetary gain vs Q4 loss of INR 25.7 crore); management states it is non-cash and symmetric, but reported margins will fluctuate with index movements.
Supply chain: insulator lead times of 18-24 months and winding conductor shortages are delaying projects; management said the board is considering an insulator solution without details.
Raw material and commodity price inflation with a lag in pass-through; management flagged possible Q1-Q2 FY27 margin dip, with no price-variation clauses noted by analysts.
Commissioning timelines slipping: Sangli plant guided to July-August 2026 with trial production by end-2026; Endoks Nigde PCS facility targeted December 2026.
Turkey geopolitical exposure: management says operations are stable after 16 years, but analysts flagged India-Turkey tensions; Turkey also hosts BESS PCS ramp.

Governance and dilution: promoters and management waived incremental salary (second year) and dividend entitlement tied to the fundraise; enabling resolution for USD 75 million; BDNA committee evaluating acquisitions larger than cash on hand.
Disclosure inconsistencies to verify: order inflow quoted as INR 600 crore then corrected to INR 870 crore; Mehru and Endoks EBIT and EBITDA margin figures were given on differing bases.

544397|2026-06.headline: Ather Energy Q1 FY27: wholesale volumes up 81% to 83,000 units, first-ever positive EBITDA of Rs 9 crore (~0.8% margin), AGM down to 22.4%.
544397|2026-06.overview: Management described a sharp demand upswing driven by policy support, fuel-availability concerns and TCO gains, with registrations up 102% YoY and paid preorders up 158% to 1.5 lakh. Production was constrained at the Hosur plant (35,000 units/month max, reached near full utilisation by June), leaving dealer inventory at about 3 days versus 14 days earlier. Commodity costs rose sharply, cutting adjusted gross margin by 5.6 percentage points to 22.4%, partly offset by an average selling price rise to Rs 1.61 lakh and disciplined fixed-cost control that delivered the first positive EBITDA. Management expects further commodity hits of 100-200 bps, to be largely offset by price increases that were only partly reflected in Q1.

segments.commentary: Retail grew 141% YoY, the highest of all zones in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Rest of India
segments.commentary: Retail grew 118% YoY in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: South India
segments.commentary: Retail grew 76% YoY in Q1 FY27.

segments.commentary: AtherStack Pro is the largest non-vehicle item; service revenue is about 2-3% of revenue versus 10-12% for established two-wheeler peers; accessories undisclosed.

guidance_outlook: Commodity headwind: management expects a further 100-200 bps hit beyond the 5.6% in Q1, to be largely absorbed through price hikes; Q2 full-quarter ASP benefit expected.

AURIC Phase 1 (Aurangabad, Factory 3.0) go-live later in calendar 2026; expected to take total capacity from 4.2 lakh to 9.2 lakh units per year; full ramp to 42,000 units/month in 4-5 months, possibly spilling into early FY28.
EL scooter (brand name to be unveiled) launch later in August 2026; target 60,000 units/month capacity across Aurangabad and Hosur (42,000 from AURIC Phase 1 plus 18,000 from Hosur).
AURIC Phase 2 could add 5 lakh units/year (total 14.2 lakh); planning stage only, firmer timeline possibly within a quarter or two.
Fundraise: Rs 1,300 crore QIP completed; a further Rs 1,200 crore preference issue pending shareholder approval, total Rs 2,500 crore.
PM E-DRIVE subsidy extension awaited; about 15-20% of Q1 vehicles sold without subsidy; Q2 subsidy treatment uncertain.

Ather Community Day on 29 August 2026 in Bengaluru to unveil the EL scooter.
New store openings slowed in Q1; expected to surge once EL and AURIC are live around the festive season. Stores reportedly reach operational profitability in about 5-6 months on average.
demand_pricing: Industry e-2W penetration reported at 11%, up 44%; industry registrations up 68% YoY to 525k in Q1 FY27; Ather inquiries up 95%; over 7 lakh inquiries in Q1; Ather brand searches up about 118%.

Management estimates unrealised retail potential of 13,000-15,000 units per month above the roughly 30,000 units/month retailed; some dealers have stopped accepting preorders with waits of about 2 months.
Pricing power: ASP moved from Rs 1.5 lakh (Q4) to Rs 1.53 lakh (April and May) and Rs 1.61 lakh (June), with price hikes described as 100% margin accretive.
Customer profile reportedly unchanged; retail finance and TCO advantage cited as supporting willingness to pay higher prices.
EL launch expected to depress ASP somewhat, with launch focus on northern and rest-of-India markets and attach rate guided at least 75%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the commodity headwind be a similar 5-6% again next quarter, or stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a further 100-200 bps of hit, not 5-6%, and says commodity costs may be near the top; quarterly averages understate end-of-quarter costs.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 employee and other expense control a new baseline before AURIC capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was not exceptional, reflecting cautious spending in FY27 after a strong FY26; some AURIC costs will be capitalised initially, with P&L impact from Q4 onwards alongside volume.

qa_highlights.question: How does 60,000 EL capacity relate to Hosur's 35,000 capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: AURIC Phase 1 is dedicated to EL at 42,000/month; Hosur gives flexibility of 18,000 units/month, shared with Rizta and 450X, so total is 60,000 for EL and not additive.

qa_highlights.question: Can AURIC Phase 2 be brought forward, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 2 is in planning; the Rs 2,500 crore raise gives funding to fast-track it, with firmer timelines possibly within one to two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for non-vehicle revenue and service?
qa_highlights.answer: AtherStack Pro is the largest non-vehicle item and benefited from price increases; service revenue is about 2-3% of revenue versus 10-12% for mature peers, and is expected to compound with fleet size.

qa_highlights.question: Will Ather enter electric motorcycles soon?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is focused on EL platform products over the next year; a motorcycle launch is more than a year away, probably two years or more.

risks_watch: Commodity costs could rise a further 100-200 bps; margin recovery depends on price increases and commodity cooling, which management says is hard to predict.
PM E-DRIVE subsidy extension not yet confirmed; about 15-20% of Q1 volumes sold without subsidy.
AURIC Phase 1 ramp risk: go-live slated for later in 2026, possible slip into early FY28; supply already short of demand by about 15,000 units per month per analyst.
EL launch may lower ASP and could cannibalise Rizta; attach-rate and margin mix to be watched.
Dealer inventory at about 3 days leaves little buffer; new store additions paused until capacity arrives.

544397|2026-09.headline: Ather Energy Q2 FY27: wholesale volume up 42% YoY to 93,000 units, first positive PAT, and gross margin at 24% (H1 FY27: 23%).
544397|2026-09.overview: Management reported strong demand with preorders up about 108% and inquiries up about 109% YoY, supporting wholesale volume of 93,000 units (up 42% YoY) and registrations of about 92,500 (up nearly 60%). Average ex-showroom price rose to INR164,000 from INR150,000 in Q4 FY26, and adjusted gross margin reached 24% in Q2 FY27 versus 25.4% in Q4 FY26 after commodity headwinds. EBITDA turned positive at 4.9% (from -9.6% a year earlier) and the company reported its first positive PAT. Management is raising installed capacity to 11.4 lakh units per year by Q2 FY28 because demand exceeds supply, and Konarc launched in phases from late August.

segments.name: Zones (registrations growth)
segments.commentary: Industry registrations grew 82% YoY to about 6 lakh in Q2. Ather growth was 82% in South, 85% in Middle India and 79% in Rest of India; Rest of India was the fastest-rising zone as Konarc rolled out in northern states and sales were prioritised there.

segments.name: Konarc (new mainstream scooter)
segments.commentary: Launched 29 August 2026 with only one month of sales in Q2 and fewer than 10,000 units sold by quarter-end. Mid variants SR2 and SR3 are live, SR1 is due by Q4 FY27, and the Z variant is not yet in production.

segments.name: Non-vehicle revenue
segments.commentary: Non-vehicle revenue was 15% of total. AtherStack Pro is more than 50% of it, with accessories and servicing split roughly equally. Management indicated gross margins of about 30-40% for accessories, 40-45% for spares and 80-90% for AtherStack Pro.

guidance_outlook: Installed capacity to rise from 9.2 lakh units/year to 11.4 lakh units/year by Q2 FY28, through Hosur (+6,000 units/month, live later this quarter) and AURIC Phase 1 (base 42,000 units/month, plus 12,000 units/month incremental).

AURIC Phase 1 trial production expected in the next few weeks (Q3 FY27), with capex installation complete by Q4 FY27; full capacity realisation takes a couple of quarters, with ramp-up expected within FY28.
Dealer/experience-centre network expansion to restart from around end of Q3 FY27, with noticeable numbers from Q4 FY27; fewer than 50 experience centres were added in the last two quarters.

No further price hikes in Q3 FY27 and no planned price increases on the current portfolio for the next few quarters; Konarc's entry variants may lower average ex-showroom price without hurting gross margin.
Management expects like-to-like Konarc gross margin to be 6-7% better than Rizta in the long term; Konarc is already a few thousand rupees cheaper than Rizta on a like-to-like basis.
Commodities seen as flat in recent weeks; management says Q3 is not expected to be worse than Q2 but volatility remains high. Subsidy is broadly unchanged QoQ.
Electric motorcycle launch: no timeline given.
capex_capacity: Current manufacturing capacity averaged 33,000 units/month in Q2 FY27, up from 28,000 in Q1; Hosur is at 35,000 units/month capacity and is described as at its limit.
Hosur expansion adds 6,000 units/month, live later in Q3 FY27. Total installed capacity is about 77,000 units/month after AURIC Phase 1 base (42,000) before the additional expansion.
AURIC Phase 1 (Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar) adds 12,000 units/month of incremental capacity by Q2 FY28, taking installed capacity to 11.4 lakh units/year from 9.2 lakh units/year.
Management estimates about 20,000 units/month of unrealised retail demand at current run-rate, with demand in the 50,000-60,000 units/month range.
Ather Node (apartment EV charging) is being industrialised and will begin deployment in the next few months; Ather Bedrock 5th-gen battery packs are live across 450, Rizta and Konarc.
demand_pricing: Preorders rose about 108% YoY to about 1.8 lakh; inquiries rose about 109% YoY to over 10 lakh; Ather searches rose about 94% vs about 34% for EV searches industry-wide.
Pan-India E2W penetration crossed 10% for the first time, at about 11.2% for Q2 FY27 (industry commentary cites 11.6% as the quarterly figure).
Average ex-showroom price rose to INR164,000 from INR150,000 in Q4 FY26, helped by price hikes and SKU/incentive management. Management says part of the gain is temporary.
Commodity inflation (aluminium, copper, plastics, memory chips) hit gross margin by about 9.4%. Management says SKU management recovered 2.7pp of this, a more temporary lever.
Structural gross-margin gains of about 5.3pp over two quarters came from price hikes, VAVE and cost reduction.
Konarc early Stack Pro attach rates are said to be as strong as Rizta, but management wants at least two quarters before assuming ~90% attach for Konarc, given a more non-South-heavy mix.
Tier 2 penetration is rising fastest; Maharashtra Tier 2 penetration is about 18-19%. Company is not yet present in rural markets.

qa_highlights.question: How quickly will the new AURIC Phase 1 capacity ramp up, given it is greenfield, and when will the 6.5 lakh figure be realised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AURIC Phase 1's base 42,000 units will take about two quarters to ramp; the additional 12,000 units going live in Q2 FY28 may ramp faster. Full ramp is expected within FY28, while Hosur ramp is expected to be rapid from the end of Q3.

qa_highlights.question: How much pricing headroom remains if commodities stay elevated into next calendar year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not want to raise prices on the current portfolio for the next few quarters. Konarc's more aggressive entry portfolio gives better unit economics, so it could lower average ex-showroom price without hurting gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: How are Konarc bookings and cannibalisation trending in launched regions?
qa_highlights.answer: Konarc has only one month of sales in Q2 and fewer than 10,000 units sold by quarter-end. Inquiries, preorders and walk-ins are up several times in Rajasthan and UP, and Konarc Z demand is strong.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ASP rise driven by scooter buyers or motorcycle buyers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the buyers are still scooter buyers paying for better experience, quality and features, not motorcycle buyers. Stack Pro attach is high across the base.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 5.3% margin gain sustainable, and does the 2.7% SKU lever reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 5.3% is broadly structural (price hikes, VAVE, cost reduction). The 2.7% SKU/incentive lever is more temporary and can be reopened if supply is tight or commodities stay high, but it is not one-off.

qa_highlights.question: How are dealer network expansion and experience-centre additions planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Fewer than 50 experience centres were added in the last two quarters as dealer expansion was held back. Expansion restarts around end of Q3 FY27, with noticeable numbers from Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Konarc variant rollout sequenced with mid variants first and entry variants later?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity constraints on 450 and Rizta changed the plan. SR2 and SR3 launched first, SR1 is due by Q4 once Aurangabad capacity is available, and Z comes later. Geographic rollout started in the North.

risks_watch: Commodity costs (aluminium, copper, plastics, memory) have stayed elevated for longer than expected; management says Q3 is unlikely to be worse than Q2, but the outlook is volatile.
The 2.7pp SKU and incentive lever is temporary and may reverse if supply eases, which could weigh on gross margin.

Capacity ramp risk: AURIC Phase 1 takes about two quarters to ramp, and the 12,000 units/month add-on is due by Q2 FY28; demand is 50,000-60,000 units/month against 77,000 installed capacity after Hosur and AURIC.
Konarc ramp and attach-rate uncertainty: early Konarc attach rates are strong, but its mix is less South-heavy, and management wants at least two quarters of data.
PAT is positive for the first time but management says it can fluctuate; PAT is not the near-term focus.
Dealer network expansion has been slowed; it restarts around end of Q3 FY27, so store additions and reach may lag demand.
Electric motorcycle timeline is not guided.

Management was reluctant to give forward figures, deferring Konarc attach rates, AURIC ramp timing and motorcycle timelines.

544399|2026-03.headline: Srigee DLM FY26 revenue INR 72.31 crore, PAT INR 6.87 crore (9.06% margin); H2 PAT more than doubled to INR 5.53 crore.
544399|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue from operations of INR 72.31 crore, total income of INR 75.76 crore, EBITDA of INR 9.23 crore (12.18% margin) and PAT of INR 6.87 crore. H2 FY26 total income was INR 54.34 crore, EBITDA INR 6.89 crore and PAT INR 5.53 crore, which more than doubled YoY. The core message is that existing capacity is over 100% utilised, so growth depends on moving to a larger Greater Noida plot (R11A, 10,850 sq m) targeted for commissioning around August 15, 2026. Management set an aspirational target of about INR 100 crore turnover in FY27 and INR 200-250 crore in FY28, though it is not formal guidance.

financial_highlights.change: As cited by analyst, not confirmed by management

financial_highlights.metric: Polymer compounding revenue (FY25, manufacturing plus trading)
OEM / B2B share of revenue (ODM segment)
financial_highlights.change: Management said earlier it would be around 70%

segments.name: Plastic injection molding and assembly
segments.commentary: Core business serving Symphony, Havells, LG, Yamaha, Neelkamal and Elentec; management cited cooler assembly as a major line. Existing capacity is more than 100% utilised.

segments.name: Mobile phone assembly (job work)
segments.commentary: Monthly sales rose from about INR 50 lakh to INR 1 crore this year. Management says this segment will contribute the most margin among the four verticals, though not the most sales, and that it currently holds under 10% share of Samsung's over 10 lakh phones assembled.

segments.name: Polymer compounding (Polymos brand)
segments.commentary: Started about two years ago with one twin-screw extruder producing and selling about 50 MT per month. Roughly INR 1 crore per month is being generated; the target is INR 2.5-3 crore monthly this year, with a 150 MT/month plan at the new facility. Captive use is about 35-40 MT/month, or 25-30% of raw material needs.

segments.name: Tool room and die
segments.commentary: Management called this one of two verticals whose potential is not yet fully harnessed, alongside polymer compounding. No revenue figure was given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 turnover target of about INR 100 crore, described by management as a personal target and not a formal projection; H2 FY27 sales expected to double.

FY28 (April 2027 to March 2028) aspiration of INR 200-250 crore; at peak utilisation the new facility is expected to reach about INR 200 crore on about INR 25 crore capex, and management said at least INR 350 crore at the site.
Margins expected to be positive relative to current levels, with no quantified margin guidance.
Financing: debt cost discussed at 8-9%, with bank negotiations at 8-8.25% versus the bank's 9.5% ask; bank funding was expected by end of June 2026.
capex_capacity: New Greater Noida facility R11A: 10,850 sq m plot (4x current space). Construction started; commercial production targeted August 15, 2026, with puja and move-in before Diwali (slippage possible).

Capex plan around INR 24-25 crore for FY27 by March 2027, apart from land already acquired. The overall project is described as about INR 50 crore, funded by IPO proceeds (INR 17 crore), bank debt and sale of smaller units and land.
Ecotech 10 (2,000 sq m plot) put on hold; funds shifted to the larger plot.
Current FAR is 1.50 against a permissible 4, giving room for vertical expansion.
IPO proceeds: 50% utilised by March 31, 2026; balance to be used in the current and next quarter.
demand_pricing: Management said customer pricing is set quarterly, so the March 2026 polymer price spike (around 3x) was absorbed in margins; the company stocked up polymers in March 2026 to offset the war impact.
New PO pricing now reflects current market rates (polymer from about INR 100 to INR 140-150 per Reliance price list).

ODM pipeline: talks with three new customers, two of which have visited the site and informally confirmed business; Havells has indicated possible work. No formal LOI received. Product areas are hand blenders, juicer-mixer-grinders and home appliances.
Cooler demand is seasonal, with June to August typically slow. Management said mobile phone demand is strong.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue is expected from polymer compounding over the next few years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 3x expansion; current run-rate about INR 1 crore per month, with INR 2.5-3 crore per month targeted this year and 150 MT/month capacity at the new facility.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is H2 FY26 growth, and what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is sustainable and will expand, citing over 100% utilisation, the mobile assembly line adding margin, and rent savings after the move. Q1 sales were affected.

qa_highlights.question: Ecotech 10 status and commercial production timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Ecotech 10 is on hold. The focus is R11A (10,850 sq m); commercial production is targeted for August 15, 2026, with possible slippage to before Diwali.

qa_highlights.question: How much ODM revenue and what share is OEM?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said above 70%, and later gave 76% as the OEM/B2B share, with modelling sales being 100% OEM.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the war and polymer prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the major impact falls on polymers, which are a crude derivative. The company bought heavily in March 2026 when prices were about 3x higher and absorbed the cost because customer pricing was fixed for the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of debt for the new capex?
qa_highlights.answer: About 8-9%. Bank's regional manager initially discussed 8-8.25% against the bank's 9.5% ask; negotiations are ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue at peak utilisation for the INR 25 crore capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR 200 crore turnover at peak utilisation, and later at least INR 350 crore at the new site with a long-term aim of INR 1,000 crore.

risks_watch: Space constraint: at 100%+ utilisation, new customers cannot be onboarded until R11A is commissioned; any delay past August 15, 2026 (or Diwali) would push out the FY27 target.
Funding: the balance of the ~INR 50 crore project depends on bank debt (not yet sanctioned at call time), sale of smaller units and land, and the debt cost being negotiated at 8-9.5%.
Customer concentration: top-10 customers still account for 91% of revenue.
Polymer price volatility from the war; pricing is reset quarterly, so cost spikes can hit margins before they are passed on.
Targets (INR 100 crore FY27, INR 200-250 crore FY28) are management aspirations with no formal guidance. Audit and qualification of the new plant by ODM customers is still pending.
