544408|2026-03.headline: Leela Palaces Q4 FY26: operating revenue up 12% to INR 484 crores and EBITDA up 13% to INR 266 crores, with ADR up 15% offsetting a March occupancy hit.
544408|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 operating revenue rose 12% YoY to INR 484 crores and operating EBITDA rose 13% to INR 266 crores, at a 55% margin, while PAT increased to INR 172 crores from INR 117 crores. Growth was driven by ADR, which rose about 15% to around INR 32,000, while RevPAR grew only 6% as occupancy fell from 78% to 72% after the West Asia conflict disrupted international travel in March. For FY26, operating revenue grew 15% to INR 1,527 crores, EBITDA grew 19% to INR 743 crores at a 49% margin, and PAT reached a record INR 403 crores. Management said April occupancy had recovered to last year's level, with high single-digit to early double-digit RevPAR growth expected for April.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 117 crores in Q4 FY25

segments.name: City hotels
segments.commentary: Occupancy fell in March on the international, US and UK source-market disruption; management expects city occupancy in mid-70s in FY27. Non-resident covers at city hotels were 54% of the cover mix.

segments.name: Resorts
segments.commentary: Described as insulated from the war; management expects a strong rebound in May and June. Resort occupancy guided to mid-60s to late-60s for FY27.

segments.name: F&B
segments.commentary: F&B revenue grew 15% in FY26 and close to double digits in Q4; banqueting grew more than 10%. Non-resident covers rose about 9-10% in Q4 and about 12% for FY26.

segments.name: Managed hotels / HMA fees
segments.commentary: HMA fees grew double digits in Q4, helped by Hyderabad ramp-up to about 62% occupancy and ADR about 1.24x peer set, plus additional HMA fees from contract terms. FY27 management fees guided to grow double digits.

segments.name: ARQ by The Leela
segments.commentary: Invite-only ultra-luxury club; first club in Bengaluru in FY26, with New Delhi in Q1 FY27, Chennai in Q2 FY27 and Mumbai later in FY27. Initiation fee is INR 45 lakh plus GST; stabilised target is 2,000 members.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q1 FY27 RevPAR growth of high single digit to early double digit in April, and May and June to be very strong; Q1 revenue and EBITDA guided to grow double digit.
FY27 occupancy: city hotels mid-70s, resorts mid-60s to late-60s, blended early 70s.
Net debt to EBITDA to stay around 1.6x in FY27, then fall toward 1.4x and near 1x as new assets ramp; acquisitions could push it slightly higher.
Depreciation to stay around INR 100 crores for the next two to three years, rising only when new hotels open.

Coorg (The Leela Forest Sanctuary): first-year revenue of INR 65-70 crores at about 40% occupancy, with stabilised EBITDA margin of 50-55%; stabilised revenue of INR 165-175 crores in year four including 19 additional villas (capex about INR 38 crores). Rebrand expected end-Q1 or early Q2 FY27.

Jaisalmer and The Leela Luxury Residences Mumbai to open in FY27. Ayodhya, Agra and Ranthambore now slated for CY28 (previously FY28), with approvals and funding in place and capex unchanged; Dubai refurbishment to start by end of CY26, handover 1 January 2027 and rebrand 1 January 2028.
capex_capacity: Total portfolio is over 5,200 luxury keys across 24 properties: 15 operational hotels and nine in the pipeline. FY26 keys grew 23% with 966 keys added across Mumbai BKC, Dubai, Jaisalmer and Coorg.
Coorg acquired on 18 March 2026: 71-key all-villa resort on 76 acres, with 25 rooms having heated pools; only about 20 of the 76 acres used so far.
Greenfield projects under construction: Bandhavgarh, Srinagar, Sikkim, Agra, Ayodhya and Ranthambore (design, demolition, excavation, piling and structural work underway).
Asset enhancement initiatives (F&B refurbishments, retail, spa, kids club, villa conversions) targeted at about 25% projected yield on cost.
Solar capacity of 2.25 MW commissioned at The Leela Palace Chennai; green energy now 67% of consumption, and power and fuel cost fell to 3% of operating revenue from 3.3% in FY25.
demand_pricing: West Asia conflict cut international inbound and outbound travel in March; the international business is roughly 50:50 with domestic in FY26 and has shifted to about 40:60 international to domestic in Q4.
Domestic demand was unaffected; management said April occupancy recovered to last year's levels.
MICE cancellations in March were given credit notes and deferred over six to nine months; management expects a high share to return in coming quarters.
Three weddings originally planned in the Middle East were moved to Leela hotels in March, with more enquiries for April and May.
Expedia and Agoda moved to charging on a gross basis rather than net, which raised sales and marketing and commission costs.
Dubai: asset is 25% owned, with Brookfield holding 75%; management said there is no change in plans and it is focused on operational break-even.

qa_highlights.question: Were March trends sharply weaker and what are April and May trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said occupancy fell on US and UK source markets while ADR held; April occupancy returned to last year's level, with high single-digit to early double-digit RevPAR growth expected, and May and June strong.

qa_highlights.question: Were there MICE cancellations, and are they deferred or lost?
qa_highlights.answer: Cancellations occurred in March; they were converted to credit notes and deferred over six to nine months, with a high share expected back in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Did Ayodhya, Agra and Ranthambore slip, and has capex changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Timing moved from FY28 to CY28 because of approval-linked construction risk; approvals and funding are in place, and capex is unchanged with no cost escalation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Dubai write-off risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not see a write-off possibility, that the asset was underwritten on conservative real estate pricing, and that it is evaluating daily.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee and other costs rise as a percentage of revenue in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise mainly to a one-time accrual for new labour code leave encashment and gratuity, plus hiring of value-driver staff; excluding this, payroll rose 8-8.5%, and management expects the ratio to decline.

qa_highlights.question: How will net debt to EBITDA trend in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 1.6x in FY27, falling toward 1.4x and then near 1x as new assets generate EBITDA; acquisitions could push it higher temporarily.

risks_watch: Recovery of international inbound demand from US and UK source markets, which is the segment hit by the West Asia conflict.
Q1 FY27 delivery against the guided high single-digit to early double-digit April RevPAR growth and double-digit May-June performance.
Dubai: a possible impairment if the market stays weak, plus the refurbishment and handover timeline (1 January 2027 handover; 1 January 2028 rebrand).
Q4 cost ratios (employee cost 16.6% of revenue vs 15.9%; other costs up 70 bps), with management expecting them to fall; management did not give exact room, F&B and HMA revenue figures for Q4.
Coorg ramp-up and rebranding, plus ARQ club openings in New Delhi, Chennai and Mumbai.
Depreciation guided flat at about INR 100 crores until new hotels open.

Management was less specific on Q4 line-item detail (room, F&B and HMA revenue) and on city-level data, deferring those to follow-up calls.
key_quotes: Our domestic business has not been impacted at all, and whilst some part of our international business has been impacted from a key source market.
The only sub -segment of demand that got impacted because of the war was our international business from our key source markets.

We are looking at an overall stabilized number of 2,000 members, because at that number we feel is the right fit where we can serve them, take care of them, and give them that kind of a luxury experience they have paid for.
The plan remains the same and there is no cost overrun on that front.

rows.why: First-year revenue guided at INR 65-70 crores at about 40% occupancy with a 50-55% stabilised EBITDA margin, and stabilised revenue of INR 165-175 crores in year four after 19 additional villas (capex about INR 38 crores).

544408|2026-06.headline: Leela Palaces Q1 FY27: operating revenue up 28% to INR3,520 mn and operating EBITDA up 41% to INR1,434 mn, margin 41%.
544408|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was driven by domestic demand, which offset a weak international start to the quarter caused by West Asia travel disruption. Six owned hotels (including Coorg) posted occupancy of 67.5% (vs 63.6%), RevPAR up 17% and ADR up 10%, with same-store RevPAR up 15%. Operating EBITDA margin expanded 383 bps to 41%, and consolidated PAT rose five-fold to INR488 mn despite a INR156 mn share-of-loss from the Dubai JV. Management reiterated double-digit RevPAR growth and mid-to-high teens EBITDA growth for FY27.

segments.commentary: RevPAR up 14% YoY. Bengaluru and Chennai are GDS and corporate heavy; Delhi and Jaipur called out as strong performers.

segments.name: Resorts

segments.name: Dubai JV (25% stake, Brookfield sponsor)
segments.commentary: Operationally break-even but recorded an accounting loss at SPV level (interest and depreciation), flowing through as INR156 mn share of JV loss. Leela takes over operations in CY27, followed by about a year of renovation.

segments.commentary: HMA fees INR262 mn (+86%); other operational service revenue +26%. Management said fees are partly performance-linked and key-money-linked, so quarterly growth may vary.

Second half expected to be strong as international arrivals, incentives and conferences return; Oct-Mar cited as the peak international months.

FY30 target of INR20 bn EBITDA reiterated; ROCE to move from double-digit to mid-to-high teens over the coming years as new hotels stabilise.
Leverage comfort level of around 2.5x average net debt/EBITDA, with variation across quarters.

Tadoba (Maharashtra) concession signed with MTDC: 30 luxury keys on 62 acres, INR1,200 mn project, 60-year concession extendable by 30 years, targeted CY30; management cites 15-17% yield on cost.
Ranthambore: 400-year-old fortress wall stabilisation has delayed the project by about two quarters; management expects to catch up once complete.
Mumbai Residences: 63 keys; show-arounds from end-CY26, residents expected early CY27.

Bandhavgarh villa construction started; Srinagar walling and landscaping in progress; Agra piling under way; Ayodhya main piling to start mid-to-late August after test piling; Sikkim main block civil work started.
Coorg 19-key brownfield expansion to follow stabilisation of the operating asset.
Renewable energy share about 67%, targeted at 75%; renewable project planned at Coorg and Chennai to reduce fixed costs.
demand_pricing: International room revenue at the five owned palace hotels moved from a 10% YoY decline in March to a 1% YoY increase in June.
Domestic room revenue up 25% YoY at the five palace hotels; retail segment up more than 20%.
Leela website share of bookings is 16% (about 64% direct overall); management says direct acquisition costs about one-third of OTA cost.
Management said the international/domestic mix is roughly 50:50 and expects international to recover further in H2 FY27.
Occupancy of existing five palace hotels close to 70%.

qa_highlights.question: Are occupancies on track for mid-70s in FY27, given Q1 occupancy of 67%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give an FY occupancy target. It pointed to balanced growth across city hotels (+14%) and resorts (+24%), and expects H2 international demand to add compression.

qa_highlights.question: Tadoba: underwritten ARR, occupancy and IRR? Could it open before CY30? Leverage cap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Tadoba is a value-accretive deal with 15-17% yield on cost, and the timeline reflects approvals and design for a wildlife trail. Net debt/LTM EBITDA is 1.6x, with an average comfort level of 2.5x.

qa_highlights.question: Expansion timelines: have Bandhavgarh, Srinagar, Ayodhya and Agra slipped?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the slippage is about one quarter. Srinagar and Bandhavgarh are for CY27 (Oct-Dec for the latter), Jaisalmer and Leela Residences by year-end, and Ranthambore is delayed by about two quarters due to wall stabilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the HMA fee growth sustainable (run-rate around INR100 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said HMA fees depend on performance, key-money-linked structures and ramp-up of new hotels, so quarterly growth will vary, but the trajectory is expected to continue.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 24% resort RevPAR growth beyond base effects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to FIT share gains, repositioning (kids clubs, F&B, spa, Amber Terrace), and multi-generational and drive-to demand, with high double-digit growth in both Rajasthan resorts.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainability of the EBITDA margin, and is it one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited renegotiated AMC and central procurement rates, revenue growth and renewable energy share. It guided to around 41% for the summer quarter, with about 50% for the full year.

risks_watch: International demand recovery: international room revenue at five palace hotels moved from -10% YoY in March to +1% in June; management expects H2 (Oct-Mar) to add compression, but West Asia conflict is not fully normalised.

So HMA is an ongoing business for us. The HMA contracts have various fee structures, incentive linked to performance and past key money commitments.
And you are right, that's got delayed by a couple of quarters, but we have now stabilized the wall and this is work in progress, but this is a one-time activity when we are building in Ranthambore.
Plus our renewable share of energy is around 67%, which we intend to take it to 75%.

544408|2026-09.headline: Leela Palaces Q2 FY27 operating EBITDA rose 36% to INR 1,877 million on 33% revenue growth; FY27 guidance kept at mid-to-high teens for H2.
544408|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 operating revenue rose 33% YoY to INR 4,119 million, with every revenue stream growing above 20%. Operating EBITDA grew 36% to INR 1,877 million at a 46% margin (up 118 bps), and PAT rose 27% to INR 946 million. RevPAR grew 30% and the company said it outperformed the India luxury market (17% vs 13% for April to August). Management reiterated mid-to-high teens EBITDA growth for H2 despite H1 running well ahead of guidance, and said the Mumbai BKC project needs incremental equity to buy the full FSI.

financial_highlights.change: from 1.6x in Mar 2026 and 3.7x in Mar 2025

segments.name: City hotels (H1)
segments.commentary: RevPAR grew 26% in H1 FY27; record H1 city occupancy of 74% vs 69% last year. Bengaluru, Chennai, Jaipur and Udaipur each grew at high double digits.

segments.name: Resorts (H1)
segments.commentary: RevPAR grew 18% in H1 FY27; same-store resort occupancy near 60%, with mid-50s blended including Coorg. Jaipur H1 occupancy above 60%.

segments.name: Owned domestic hotels (Q2)
segments.commentary: RevPAR up 30% with ADR up 30% to INR 25,046 and India headline occupancy of 69%. Domestic revenue at owned hotels grew more than 30%, and growth excluding Coorg was similar.

segments.name: Management fees
segments.commentary: Fees up 76% to INR 289 million; share of revenue rising from about 5% to 7%. Management said 85-90% of new managed-fee revenue flows to EBITDA.

544410|2026-03.headline: Prostarm Q4 FY26 operating revenue rose 27% YoY to INR105 crore but fell 35% QoQ, with FY26 revenue at INR386 crore (+10%) as March billings slipped into Q1 FY27.
544410|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue of about INR105 crore grew 27% YoY but fell 35% QoQ, as project executions scheduled for March were deferred to Q1 FY27 due to West Asia-linked supply chain and gas-availability disruptions. EBITDA was about INR11 crore (down ~3% YoY) at a 10.43% margin, and PAT was about INR8 crore (up ~16% YoY) at a 7.56% margin. For FY26, revenue was INR386 crore (+10%), EBITDA margin fell 98 bps to 12%, and PAT was about INR33 crore (+14%). Working capital days rose to 185 from 68 as receivables reached about INR254 crore, mostly from one large project, and management guided to FY27 operating cash flow turning positive and FY27 revenue growth of at least 25%.

segments.name: UPS and power conditioning
segments.commentary: Core product made in two Pune facilities; Gujarat plant (1 kVA to 600 kVA UPS) now expected operational by Q2 FY27, delayed from Q1 FY27 by supply chain issues. Management expects UPS growth above 30-40% over the next two years.

BESS developer projects (rental model, about INR63 crore rental per year) are being sought for hive-off, with Bihar EPC targeted for FY27 and Karnataka subject to legal issues.

segments.commentary: Management cites channel business of about INR100 crore per year (FY26: about INR107 crore). Services include installation, AMCs and rentals; EPC is executed for solar and BESS projects.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue: management cites at least 25% growth; visible base of about INR430 crore (INR336 crore order book excluding BESS developer projects plus about INR100 crore channel business), with minimum-revenue framing and additional orders excluded.
Q1 and Q2 FY27: expected to carry the deferred billings; Q1 FY27 revenue is expected to grow YoY.

Q1 and Q2 FY27 margin target: EBITDA 12-13%, PAT 8.5-9.5%.
Operating cash flow: still expected to turn positive for FY27 as a whole, with improvement visible from Q3 FY27; receivable days targeted at 120-150 days exiting FY27.
Jhajjar BESS plant utilisation: 25-40% in FY27 and about 70% in FY28 (per management, assuming operations from around July 2026).
Working capital: no equity dilution planned; requirements to be met from bank borrowings and internal accruals. Promoter holding about 73%.
capex_capacity: Jhajjar, Haryana: 1.20 GWh BESS assembly plant, capex about INR25 crore, revenue potential about INR1,000 crore at full utilisation; machines largely installed, expected fully operational in Q1 FY27.

Gujarat UPS plant (1 kVA to 600 kVA): project cost not more than INR5-6 crore per management; capacity of 3,000-5,000 units per day (about 9 lakh units per year), revenue potential INR500-600 crore; now expected Q2 FY27, delayed from Q1 FY27 by supply chain issues.
Three facilities currently operational: two in Pune (UPS and power conditioning) and one lithium battery pack facility in Navi Mumbai; 100 MWh lithium expansion cost about INR3.5-4 crore.
Management says capacity is not constrained: imports from China are customised, and servo units, isolation transformers and some UPS are sourced from job workers and subcontractors.
Management estimates total potential revenue of about INR1,700-1,800 crore from all facilities at 100% localised manufacturing, excluding imports.
demand_pricing: Order book: executable order in hand approx. INR1,106 crore plus L1 approx. INR96 crore (total approx. INR1,202 crore) at end FY26; bids of approx. INR257 crore under evaluation.

Customers include Adani, Karnataka Power, Bihar Power, L&T, West Bengal Medical, South Central Railway, SAIL and India One. Government share of revenue is 43%; private is the rest, with the same payment cycle.
Q4 shortfall: a single Adani order of about INR40-43 crore was deferred from Q4 to Q1 FY27; management says Q4 revenue would otherwise have been about INR430 crore-plus.

Cost pressures: freight costs more than doubled in Q4 versus earlier; the USD rose more than 10% over three to four months; China removed BESS export incentives from April 1, 2026, raising costs on orders placed earlier. Management says Q1 onward pricing reflects these costs.
Gross margin pressure: cost of production rose to 72.78% from 72.2%. Management cites order-to-order margin mix and says EBITDA by segment is not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables jump and when will they be collected?

qa_highlights.question: Is operating cash flow still expected positive in FY27 and is equity dilution planned?

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 margins fall and what is the outlook?

544410|2026-06.headline: Prostarm Q1 FY27 revenue rose 38% YoY to INR 76 crore, PAT up 156% to INR 5 crore, with a 25% minimum FY27 growth target reiterated.

EBITDA was INR 7 crore at an 8.55% margin (up 126 bps YoY) and PAT was INR 5 crore at a 6.05% margin. Management said the 12-13% margin guidance still holds on a full-year basis, while also guiding FY27 PAT margin to 8.5-9%. Order book stood at about INR 1,085 crore plus INR 5 crore L1, and working capital days fell from 185 to 168.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 revenue fall 27% QoQ, and is the margin guidance still valid?

qa_highlights.question: What are the working capital days targets and cash flow expectations?

rows.why: Trade receivables fell from INR 254 crore to INR 231 crore in Q1 with about half expected collected by end-Q2 and a large CCTNS amount due by end-August; government-funded, so realisation risk is low.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 25% growth, 12-13% EBITDA and positive OCF targets, but cautious and evasive on utility BESS pricing and Jhajjar FY27 utilisation (20-25%); analysts pressed on margin ramp, receivables and dilution.

544410|2026-09.headline: Prostarm H1 FY27 revenue rose 62.3% YoY to INR 196 crore, but Q2 EBITDA margin fell to 7.83% as costs and low-margin third-party sales weighed.
544410|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew about 82% YoY to INR 120 crore, but EBITDA fell 17% YoY to INR 9 crore with margin at 7.83%, and PAT fell about 27% to INR 6 crore (5.08% margin). Management attributed margin compression to low-margin third-party power and other product sales, higher freight (said to have almost doubled), forex impact on fixed-price contracts, higher employee and overhead costs, and start-up costs of the Bhachau and Bakrol plants. Order book stood at about INR 1,121 crore across 97 projects at 30 September 2026, with 78% government. Working capital cycle lengthened to 192 days from 185 days, mainly on receivables and inventory build, and operating cash flow remained negative.

financial_highlights.value: Net cash of about INR 97 crore cited versus about INR 105 crore borrowings-linked figure as stated; unclear on transcript

segments.name: Solar EPC
segments.commentary: About INR 178 crore of the order book (about 16%); selective, high-value solar EPC work is being taken, with volumes elevated in FY27 but expected to moderate in FY28 unless high-value orders are won.

segments.name: Developer / BESS projects
segments.commentary: Developer projects of about INR 854 crore (government, 12-year annual rental of about INR 62 crore) and total VSS/EPC/developer book of about INR 999 crore (about 81%). Management is in talks to downsell two developer projects to a buyer.

segments.name: Manufactured power solutions (UPS)
segments.commentary: Order book about INR 26 crore; Bakrol UPS plant (about 3,000 pieces per day, 1 kVA to 600 kVA) can generate about INR 500-600 crore revenue per year at full utilisation.

segments.name: Third-party power and other products
segments.commentary: Low-margin third-party sales contributed to margin dilution in Q2 FY27; management said one third-party billing was executed in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of about INR 500 crore, based on about INR 266 crore order in hand plus about INR 20-25 crore of monthly billing additions.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided to remain above 11%, lower than the earlier 13-14% range; management described it as a moderation with FY27 revenue growth expected to be strong.

FY28 guidance: revenue growth of about 25% described as a minimum expectation; EBITDA margin expected to recover toward 12-13% and later about 18%; BESS-led margin of 8.5-9% described as achievable if BESS volumes come through.
Operating cash flow expected to turn positive by year-end FY27; management described this as a target rather than a commitment.

Bhachau BESS plant (1.2 GWh, single shift, scalable to 3 GWh on three shifts) expected to contribute from FY28; BESS capacity utilisation expected at 25-30% in FY28, with peak utilisation in about three years.
capex_capacity: Bhachau, Gujarat: 1.2 GWh BESS assembly plant, single shift, scalable to 3 GWh on three shifts; about INR 1,000 crore potential revenue per year at full utilisation.
Bakrol, Gujarat: UPS assembly facility with lithium integration, about 3,000 pieces per day; potential INR 500-600 crore per year.
Both facilities commenced operations on 25 September 2026; Bakrol expands UPS capacity across the 1 kVA to 600 kVA range.
Inventory rose to about INR 120 crore from about INR 77 crore to support new plant output and lead times (BESS lead time over three months).
Lithium cells will still be imported; BESS assembly is in-house but no backward integration yet.
demand_pricing: Order book about INR 1,121 crore across 97 ongoing projects at 30 September 2026; 78% government, 22% private.
Management cited India BESS market growth of more than 8x between FY25 and FY34 and data centre capacity rising from about 1,150 MW (December 2024) to about 3,200 MW by FY30.
Government VGS scheme (about INR 14,500 crore, 30 GWh) with about 40% local content requirement, and a PLI of 10 GWh, cited as support for domestic BESS manufacturing.
Management says pricing pressure is high from new entrants in BESS and UPS; it is shifting to selective tenders with high ticket size and private/channel business.
Average BESS order ticket about INR 40-50 lakh; utility-scale solar pricing pressure described as continuing.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 13-14% FY27 EBITDA margin still achievable, and what is the H2 margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 margin would be above 11% and H2 would see moderation in costs; freight roughly doubled and forex hit fixed-price contracts. It has about INR 266 crore order in hand for FY27 revenue of about INR 500 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin decline temporary or structural, and how will working capital and receivables evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it temporary, linked to low-margin third-party sales and start-up costs at new plants. Average receivable days were about 100 (about 178 excluding one large September billing of about INR 86-90 crore). Receivables fell from INR 257 crore at H1 to INR 201 crore in October 2026 after about INR 73-75 crore of collections.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company looking to downsell its developer projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is in discussions with about six to seven industry players to sell down its two developer projects; no timing given beyond possibly this or next quarter. Equity IRR on these projects was said to be above 12% before margin erosion from lithium and dollar costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS capacity ramp and when will scale benefits show?
qa_highlights.answer: Bhachau plant (1.2 GWh single shift) is expected to contribute from FY28 with 25-30% utilisation next year; peak utilisation expected in about three years. Export samples of about 16 kWh units shipped to an overseas customer, with volume expected next financial year if approved.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company differentiate as BESS and solar become more commoditised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it focuses on local content, technical solutions, and OEM/technology partner positioning rather than a typical EPC; it is targeting selective tenders above INR 5 crore and private sector channel partners.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on FY28 BESS volume ramp and cost normalisation (freight, forex, lithium); management's margin guidance has been revised down from 13-14% to above 11% for FY27.
Working capital cycle at 192 days and negative operating cash flow (about INR -17 crore at September 2026 per management) remain key watch items.
Possible sale of two developer projects (INR 854 crore book) may create margin depletion and changes to the order book.
Competitive pricing pressure from new entrants and rising input costs in BESS and UPS.
Collection of about INR 201 crore receivables, including two large parties expected by December 2026.

Answers on working capital and cash flow were detailed but partly qualitative, and the company declined to give long-term margin targets or name export customers.
key_quotes: Our focus was on delivering numbers. Even if the margin is on the lower side, important for us to have the regular billing done on the books.
We would try to maintain Paras G, but still it should be above 11 percent.
So 25% is a minimum expectation that we are keeping an eye on a financial year.

rows.why: Management is in talks with six to seven industry players to sell down the two developer projects, which could reduce the INR 999 crore VSS/EPC/developer book (about 81% of orders) and may deplete margin.

544411|2026-03.headline: Scoda Tubes FY26 revenue rose 7% to INR518.7 crore and PAT 22% to INR38.8 crore, while Q4 revenue was flat at INR123.6 crore after a March gas shutdown.
544411|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a transition year with revenue up 7% to INR518.7 crore, EBITDA of INR76.2 crore and margin down to 14.7% from 16.1%. Q4 FY26 revenue was flat at INR123.6 crore, EBITDA margin 13.5% and PAT down 7% YoY to INR6.3 crore, as a 15-17 day PNG gas-driven plant shutdown in March cut production by about 40% for the month. Management guides FY27 revenue growth of about 25% with 14-15% EBITDA margin, backed by a 8,000 MTPA welded expansion (INR40 crore) on top of the 13,000 MTPA welded line funded from IPO proceeds. Capex was INR110 crore in FY26 and about INR100 crore is planned for FY27.

financial_highlights.value: around INR175 crore, executable in 3-4 months

segments.name: Seamless (piercing mill)
segments.commentary: Seamless capacity raised to 20,000 MTPA, total capacity 21,000 MTPA in FY26; piercing plant was shut for about 15-17 days in March on gas shortage and resumed in April. Seamless utilisation expected around 70% in FY27 and optimum in FY28.

segments.name: Welded
segments.commentary: New welded facility targeted to be operational in H2 FY27 with trial runs by end-Q2 FY27; 13,000 MTPA line funded from IPO, plus 8,000 MTPA (INR40 crore) from internal accruals, taking welded capacity to 21,150 MTPA by H1 FY28. Welded utilisation expected around 25% in FY27; optimum FY29.

segments.name: Geography (FY26 revenue)
segments.commentary: India INR339 crore, Europe INR137.8 crore, Americas INR30.7 crore, others INR8.9 crore. Management cited domestic INR344 crore and export INR174 crore on the analyst's summation.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 25%, with domestic about 20% and export about 25%; management called this conservative and will revisit in H1 FY27.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 14-15%.
Target FY27 revenue mix of roughly 40% export and 60% domestic.
Inventory days expected to fall from 217 days to about 160 days in FY27 and remain 160-170 days thereafter.
Peak debt expected to rise by about INR50 crore to about INR250 crore in FY27; debt to decline once new capacity is fully utilised.

Solar project (8.79 MWdc: 4.99 MW seamless, 3.8 MW welded) expected to generate about 137 lakh kWh a year and save about INR8-8.63 crore a year in power cost.

Management said operations are fully normalised for Q1 FY27 with a higher cost base, and the plant is running at full capacity.

IPO proceeds of INR220 crore: about INR27 crore spent on capex and INR50 crore on working capital; about INR74.2 crore remaining in bank.
FY27 capex planned at about INR100 crore. Mother hollow mill supplies 70% captive consumption, targeting full captive by FY28.
demand_pricing: Raw material is stainless steel round bar made from imported scrap; base-material prices up 25-30% due to the war. Management said these are passed through to customers at order booking or dispatch.
LPG and gas prices remain elevated; cost pressure passed to customers with a lag. Management said demand is intact and only pricing is affected.
Export end-use: about 50% oil and gas, the rest engineering, automotive, power, and cooling industries. Europe pending Rina marine approval for Italian market, expected within 3-4 weeks.

Domestic power demand hinges on a BHEL tender now expected June-July 2026 (earlier slipped from Nov-Dec 2025 and Mar-Apr 2026); Scoda is BHEL- and NTPC-approved and works with BARC. Power sector demand is for seamless tubes.
Data centre, HVAC, cooling and water-treatment demand targeted through welded pipes; no data-centre order book yet, with inquiries on hand and orders expected around Q4 FY27.
Receivable days rose sharply (receivables up 36% vs revenue up 7%), attributed to industry-wide supply chain disruption and longer payment cycles.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the high-diameter welded pipe capex delayed from Q3 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed geopolitical shortages, higher logistics and energy costs, and container and shipping constraints for machines from China. Delivery now expected July-August, against a prior plan of Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 weakness and was it one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the March gas shutdown (about 15-17 days, roughly 7-8 March to 21-22 March) was the largest headwind; without it, Q4 revenue could have been about INR140 crore. Demand is intact, and gas availability has normalised.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the planned acquisition withdrawn?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited cross-border remittance, regulatory, banking and forex constraints, plus the EU safeguard duty rising from 25% to 50% and a tariff-rate quota cut of 50% from 1 July, which removed the benefit of a European entity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the basis for FY27 guidance and domestic/export split?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is conservative: domestic about 20% and export about 25% growth, with the mix targeted at 40% export and 60% domestic. Upside is seen from a BHEL win and data-centre welded demand.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the shift from 8-inch to 16-inch welded pipe made?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers in data centre, HVAC, cooling and water-treatment packages prefer one supplier covering up to 16 inches, so Scoda extended its welded range beyond 8 inches. Above 16 inches needs a different A358 technology.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost rise despite lower borrowings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to borrowings for ongoing capex, the solar project and higher working-capital use, plus interest on delayed income tax payments.

risks_watch: Gas and LPG cost inflation and supply continuity; a repeat of March-type shutdown would hit volumes again.
Raw material (imported scrap-based stainless round bar) volatility, with a 25-30% rise to be passed through on order booking; lag risk on margins.
Delays in welded equipment delivery (July-August) could push welded commissioning beyond H2 FY27.
Receivable days and inventory days (217 days, target 160-170) affect working capital and debt, with peak debt near INR250 crore.
Order book of INR175 crore covers only 3-4 months; large export and BHEL tender timing (June-July) is uncertain.
Management withheld volumes, utilisation by segment, realisation per ton, EBITDA per ton and order-book split, limiting transparency.
Q4 FY26 PAT fell 7% and the company says the Q4 margin was hit by under-absorbed fixed costs; benchmarking against peer margins was declined.
Management agreed to consider quarterly calls and disclosure of new orders, as requested by an analyst, with no commitment.

So, for now, we don't have any plan for diluting any more equity.
Yes, sir. Everything is smooth now. Everything is normalized, just a little bit higher cost.

544413|2026-03.headline: Digitide Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9.2% YoY to INR 800 crores, but adjusted PAT fell to INR 11 crores on wage code and accounting charges.
544413|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue reached INR 800 crores, up 2.5% QoQ and 9.2% YoY, with Tech and Digital at 31.1% of mix and international at 38.1%. EBITDA was INR 88 crores (11% margin), absorbing about INR 4 crores of one-time wage code impact. Adjusted PAT fell to INR 11 crores from INR 24 crores in Q3, mainly due to lease-accounting finance cost and a residual value policy change raising depreciation; reported PAT was INR (-5) crores after a INR 16 crores exceptional wage code charge. Management guided to 100 bps operating EBITDA margin expansion by exit FY27 and double-digit revenue growth, with early-to-mid teens cited.

segments.name: BPM
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR 551 crores (+1.1% QoQ, +2.6% YoY); FY26 INR 2,170 crores, about 70% of revenue. EBITDA margin 16.3%, up 187 bps YoY.

segments.name: Tech and Digital
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR 249 crores (+27.2% YoY); FY26 INR 910 crores, 29.6% of revenue (up 280 bps from 26.8%). EBITDA margin 12.1%, up 289 bps YoY.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR 304 crores (+16.4% YoY), 38.1% of mix; FY26 mix 37.3%, up 180 bps. Healthcare (US) revenue crossed about USD 25 million in FY26.

guidance_outlook: Double-digit revenue growth in FY27-28; management quantified as early to mid-teens.
100 bps operating EBITDA margin expansion by exit of FY27 (Q4 FY27); mix (Tech and Digital and international) expected to contribute about 40% each, with operational efficiencies the rest.
FY31 target of INR 8,400 crores (USD 1 billion), of which about INR 1,700 crores inorganic; implies about 14-15% organic CAGR.
Healthcare expected at 12-15% of revenue by FY31 (USD 120-150 million); Tech and Digital at 40% and international at 50% of revenue by FY31.

Cash conversion baseline of about 70% of EBITDA; steady-state lease depreciation about INR 38-40 crores and PPE depreciation about INR 20 crores per year; management said at least one acquisition likely this year, with six targets evaluated and two at advanced stage.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex INR 105 crores, mainly technology platforms, AI capabilities and IT and leasehold infrastructure.

Annual cash deployment roughly INR 100 crores: maintenance capex INR 70-80 crores, plus INR 15-20 crores for two large leasehold premises moving in FY26-27; balance accrues for internal growth and inorganic deals.
AI centres of excellence set up in Bengaluru and Coimbatore for a global P&C insurance client, with the deal running on Azure.
Management stated no plans to monetise physical assets; premises are largely leased, with one owned premises.
demand_pricing: Q4 TCV INR 620 crores, second consecutive quarter above INR 600 crores; FY26 TCV INR 2,355 crores.
About 15% of pipeline is hyperscaler-led (AWS, GCP, Microsoft); management linked part of the 27% Tech and Digital growth to hyperscaler deal conversion.
Top-10 customer revenue concentration fell about 200 bps; of FY26 incremental revenue of about INR 205 crores, about 45% came from new customers.
Healthcare: two new US provider-side deals won in Q1 FY27 (per management); positioned as revenue cycle management, revenue enablement and CX partner; compared with Sagility as not like-for-like.
Revenue per FTE up 11.4% YoY to INR 584k, supported by AI-led delivery and pyramid optimisation.

qa_highlights.question: What was FY26 growth in USD terms, and how much came from existing versus new clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Constant-currency growth was 5.2%. About INR 205 crores of incremental revenue was added, with roughly 45% from new customers and the rest from existing clients.

qa_highlights.question: Is the standalone Digitide business loss-making once Alldigi profits are excluded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no; corporate costs sit in Digitide, including US and Canada sales leadership, and cost transfer pricing is applied, so standalone-versus-consolidated comparison is not like-for-like.

qa_highlights.question: What is sustainable OCF conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 70% of EBITDA is the baseline; FY26's 77% was boosted by novation catch-up after the demerger, with Q1 FY26 at -36%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the pipeline is hyperscaler-led and is it converting?
qa_highlights.answer: About 15% of the pipeline is hyperscaler-led and contributions are now flowing through partners, with the Azure-based AI CoE deal cited.

qa_highlights.question: Will PulseNerve become a recurring platform or IP revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: PulseNerve is an orchestration layer enabling large AI service deals rather than a standalone platform; DocuSense, SmartPay and DigiCollect were cited as IP assets with non-linear revenue potential.

qa_highlights.question: What is the depreciation run-rate and what does EBIT look like after the Q4 changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the one-time PPE depreciation charge is about INR 4 crores; steady-state lease depreciation is about INR 38-40 crores, with total depreciation around INR 60-62 crores, and the 100 bps margin guidance was reiterated. Net margin guidance was declined, with management pointing to an FY26 adjusted PAT margin of 2.3% as baseline.

risks_watch: Adjusted PAT fell to INR 11 crores in Q4 from INR 24 crores in Q3; management attributes this to lease and depreciation accounting, but the step-up in depreciation (Q4 INR 66 crores vs INR 49 crores a year earlier) and finance cost weigh on earnings.
Q4 EBITDA margin was flat at 11%, and management has pushed margin expansion timeline out; 100 bps expansion is now targeted by exit of FY27.
FY31 USD 1 billion target needs about 14-15% organic CAGR plus about INR 1,700 crores inorganic; inorganic progress and acquisition timing remain open.
Management declined to give a steady-state net profit margin, so analysts must derive it; reported PAT was INR (-5) crores in Q4 and INR 6 crores for FY26.
Watch whether DSO stays near 75 days and OCF conversion holds near 70% of EBITDA; watch hyperscaler pipeline conversion and healthcare wins.

Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 20%+ presales growth, 20%+ revenue growth, 17-19% EBITDA margin and 20%+ ROCE. qa_highlights.answer: Focus remains MMR and Maharashtra; Pune studied but returns did not meet criteria. Company insists on 100% development control in JDAs with step-in rights.

544420|2026-09.headline: Raymond Realty Q2 FY27 total income rose 7% YoY to INR757 crore, EBITDA margin 15%, booking value up 111% YoY in H1 to INR1,602 crore.

Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 20% pre-sales growth, 17-19% EBITDA margin, 20% ROCE and 9-10% PAT margin, and dropped explicit revenue growth guidance. An ICICI Prudential AIF subsidiary investment of INR210 crore for the Mahim project and a INR400 crore promoter equity infusion were announced, with debt held near INR1,200 crore.

544421|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 28% YoY to ₹1,143 mn, but consolidated EBITDA margin fell to ~36% from 39% on freight and employee costs.
544421|2026-09.overview: Revenue from operations was ₹1,143 mn, up 28% YoY and 16% QoQ, with H1 FY27 revenue at ₹2,130 mn (+23%). Core gases segment margin improved to ~39% from 38%. The 325 TPD Durgapur on-site plant was commissioned in September 2026, and a ₹480 crore BHEL EPC contract for a 1,200 TPD air separation unit in Odisha was won, with commissioning expected in FY29.

rows.why: Thane H1 FY27 pre-sales about INR 420 crore vs INR 167 crore in H1 FY26 (up about 130%); management expects over 3,000 families on site by FY28 from about 2,000 now.

rows.label: Net debt flat at FY27 year-end
rows.why: Net debt was INR 8,323 crore at 30 Sep 2026 (2.1x net debt-to-equity), and guidance is flat vs FY26, so deleveraging depends on H2 completions and collections.

rows.label: Price increases of 3% to 5% across projects
rows.why: Price increases of 3% to 5% have been taken across projects to cover current inflation and cost increases, with no further headroom quantified.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand breadth, Thane and the completion target, and the guidance was held; analysts pressed on the H1-to-H2 bridge to INR 6,500 crore, launch approvals and price headroom, and several answers stayed qualitative, such as Kalpataru One.

544424|2026-06.headline: Globe Civil Q1 FY27 revenue (total income) rose 37.26% YoY to INR929.23 million; PAT up 40.42% to INR7.09 crore.
544424|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income for Q1 FY27 was INR929.23 million versus INR676.98 million a year earlier, up 37.26% YoY. EBITDA rose 33.03% to INR15.80 crore with a stated margin of 17.01%, and PAT rose 40.42% to INR7.09 crore (net margin 7.63%). Management attributed growth to projects won after the IPO (Central University Bathinda, Haryana Cricket Association stadium, Kanpur) and said working capital was elevated by pre-final/final bills and early material procurement. Management guided to 10-15% growth in FY27 on the existing order book, with order book targeted to reach INR1,200-1,500 crore.

segments.name: Institutional / education
segments.commentary: Management called education its main focus, citing IITs, IITs/IIMs/NITs as major revenue sources; recent bids include Central University Tamil Nadu and IIM Visakhapatnam. IIT Delhi and an INR100 crore IIT order were mentioned.

segments.name: Sports infrastructure
segments.commentary: Two small sports projects of about INR50 crore each done, and a ~INR200 crore stadium (Jhajjar) under execution, with management aiming to build eligibility for bigger sports projects. Stadium revenue to date was about INR30-35 crore, and completion is targeted in about 15 months.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 10-15% from the existing order book, excluding any new project wins.
Expected FY27 execution of about INR300-350 crore from the ~INR700 crore order book, with the largest revenue in the last quarter.
EBITDA margin expected to be maintained at around 17% (similar margins), and management said margins are sustainable for the next one to two years.
Target to add at least INR500 crore of new orders within 3-12 months, taking the order book to about INR1,200-1,300 crore; next milestone INR1,500 crore by year-end.
Management says it wants order book at least 3x annual turnover.
capex_capacity: Management said it can handle 10-15 projects simultaneously; 11-12 projects are currently running.
Single-project eligibility is INR500-650 crore in normal projects; larger projects possible via joint ventures.
Existing setup could support revenue of INR500-600 crore without a major increase in fixed cost.
Inventory rose about INR162 crore, partly from early procurement of material (e.g., tiles) in Feb-Mar 2026 ahead of price rises for the Bathinda project.
Mobilisation advance (up to ~10% of contract value against bank guarantee) available but not availed on Bathinda or the recent IIT project.
demand_pricing: About four to five tenders (~INR800 crore) were pending opening; bids placed at two to three per month, including Bihar, Tamil Nadu, Visakhapatnam and Nagpur.
Selective bidding favoured central government and funded projects; competition cited as 5-6 bidders versus 10-15 on NHAI tenders.
Management described competition as healthy with decent margins, not heavy under-bidding.
Top 5 projects contribute about 70% of turnover; one private client (DPS) and one cricket stadium are the main private projects, the rest are government.
Repeat clients include CPWD (about 20 years), NBCC (fifth or sixth project) and DPS (three projects in total).

qa_highlights.question: What drove Q1 revenue growth and what share of revenue came from which projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Post-IPO wins (Central University Bathinda, Haryana Cricket Association, Kanpur) drove growth; Bathinda structure work and NBCC project contributed most. A new project typically takes 6-8 months to reach full revenue flow.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the order book and what pipeline exists?
qa_highlights.answer: Current order book about INR700 crore; four tenders (~INR800 crore) awaiting opening; target at least INR500 crore new orders in 3-12 months, taking book to INR1,200-1,300 crore; next milestone INR1,500 crore by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables and inventory rise, and what is being done on cash conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables rose on Q4 final and pre-final bills (Aligarh NBCC billing expected to close by 15 September; Telecommunications India Limited by 30 September). Inventory rose on material bought in Feb-Mar 2026 ahead of price increases. Routine government and DPS bills take 30-40 days to realise.

qa_highlights.question: Why were some projects delayed and what is the stadium contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Stadium start was delayed by statutory approvals; it started scaling from March. Stadium revenue to date is about INR30-35 crore. Management said approvals for government projects now sit within EPC scope, making them faster.

qa_highlights.question: Will the current margins be sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident the current margins (about 17% EBITDA) are sustainable for the next one to two years.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR700 crore order book will be executed in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects INR300-350 crore of execution in FY27, based on current monthly run-rate of INR30-40 crore.

risks_watch: Receivable days elevated: final bills pending on NBCC Aligarh and Telecommunications India Limited; collection timing is key to cash flow.
Inventory and working capital rose faster than revenue; watch whether it normalises as orders scale.
Order inflow needed to reach INR1,200-1,500 crore target; four tenders (~INR800 crore) pending with no guaranteed wins.
Project start delays from statutory approvals (Bathinda, cricket stadium) can push revenue recognition out by 6-8 months.
Heavy reliance on government clients and top 5 projects (~70% of turnover).
544424|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on execution and margins, but guidance is conditional on new order wins. Management was candid about delays, receivable timing and the number of pending tenders. Several answers were vague or repetitive on order targets and FY27 growth.
key_quotes: We always believe that we should have at least 3 the turnover -- 3x order book of the turnover.
Yes. We're confident that this margin are sustainable for the next couple of years.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides EBITDA margin held at around 17% (Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 17.01%, up from ~17.5% implied last year on INR15.80 cr EBITDA vs INR929 mn income) and calls it sustainable for 1-2 years, but this is maintenance rather than expansion.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex not discussed; existing setup can support INR500-600 crore revenue without major fixed-cost increase, so there is no capacity pressure forcing an announcement, and the asset-light EPC model needs little fixed capex.

rows.why: Upside depends on winning the target INR500 crore of new orders within 3-12 months (four tenders worth ~INR800 crore pending, bids at 2-3 per month), with no guaranteed wins and Q1 growth of 37.26% against 10-15% FY27 guide.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Guidance is conditional on new order wins; receivables elevated on NBCC Aligarh and Telecommunications India Limited final bills, inventory up about INR162 crore, and statutory approval delays (Bathinda, stadium) can push revenue out 6-8 months.

rows.why: No new products, brands or molecules discussed; company is a civil construction contractor.

rows.label: INR500 crore new orders to reach INR1,200-1,300 crore book
rows.when: within 3-12 months; INR1,500 crore by year-end

rows.why: Final bills on NBCC Aligarh (by 15 Sep) and Telecommunications India Limited (by 30 Sep) should close, but inventory rose about INR162 crore on Feb-Mar 2026 tile buying, and routine government bills take 30-40 days to realise.

rows.why: Up to ~10% of contract value advance (against bank guarantee) is available but not availed on Bathinda or the recent IIT project, which could ease working capital if taken.

544425|2026-06.headline: AJC Jewel Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 124.69% YoY to Rs 101.38 crore; EBITDA margin 4.58% and PAT margin 2.35%.
544425|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue reached Rs 101.38 crore versus Rs 45.12 crore in Q1 FY26, with EBITDA of Rs 4.64 crore (from Rs 1.58 crore) and PAT of Rs 2.38 crore (from Rs 0.57 crore). Margins expanded, with EBITDA margin at 4.58% (from 3.5%) and PAT margin at 2.35% (from 1.26%). Management announced a proposed 80% stake acquisition in AJC Jewel Manufacturers FZC, Sharjah, via a non-cash share swap valued at up to Rs 9.6 crore, though the Sharjah entity is not consolidated in Q1. Management guided FY27 standalone India revenue of Rs 450 crore and 50% CAGR for three years, on a volume basis. Many answers on utilisation, Esthara economics and FY28 targets were deferred to H1 results.

segments.name: India gold jewellery (core B2B, casting)
segments.commentary: Capacity 5 kg/day; utilisation about 25% (about 1.2 kg/day). Kerala accounts for 90-95% of revenue. Top 10 customers are about 50% of revenue; about 200 other customers make up the rest.

segments.name: Sharjah UAE (AJC Jewel Manufacturers FZC)
segments.commentary: Gold jewellery capacity 3 kg/day at about 800 g/day (about 27% utilisation). Management cited PAT margin of about 4% and EBITDA margin of about 5%, in a tax-exempt free zone. Not consolidated in Q1; expected consolidation from Q3.

segments.name: Esthara Jewels (silver DTC)
segments.commentary: Three stores operational in Kerala; two more under fit-out, expected to open by end of next month. Silver capacity 8 kg/day with about 1 kg/day production. Management targets about Rs 20 lakh revenue per store per month; first store reportedly about Rs 15 lakh per month. Capex about Rs 4,000 per sq ft; opex about Rs 5-6 lakh per store; breakeven targeted within one year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone India revenue target of Rs 450 crore (management reiterated it is standalone India only; Sharjah additional).
Revenue growth of about 50% CAGR for the next three years, stated as based on volume growth; management said price effects would be added only if gold prices rise.
Current PAT margin of about 2.5% cited for the year.
Sharjah full-year contribution to be updated after H1 results; acquisition completion expected in 3-6 months subject to BSE and regulatory approvals.
Dilution to existing shareholders from the share swap estimated at about 7-8%, per management (uncertain).
Store count and three-year store plans to be updated post H1 results.
Q1 and Q2 seasonally moderate; Q3 and Q4 stronger on festivals and weddings.
capex_capacity: India: 5 kg/day gold casting capacity, upgraded from IPO proceeds to 120% expansion (cited as 5 kg Kerala, 8 kg silver), with about 25% utilisation today.
Silver jewellery production started in India; capacity up to 8 kg/day, currently about 1 kg/day.
Sharjah: 3 kg/day installed gold capacity at about 800 g/day.
At 100% utilisation management cited India about Rs 7 crore/day (about Rs 2,500 crore/yr at 5 kg/day) and Sharjah about Rs 3.6 crore/day; these are indicative and not guidance.
Additional working capital needed to reach peak utilisation; to be funded via internal accruals, debt and possibly equity, gradually.
Design and innovation centre set up; about 20 in-house design staff; library of about 2.5 lakh designs on B2B portal.
demand_pricing: Added 12 independent jewellers in Q1, mainly mid and small Kerala retailers; no new corporate clients after Kalyan.
Management is targeting expansion beyond Kerala, with a marketing team in Chennai; international orders to be served via Sharjah.
Management said gold price moves will not affect margins because it hedges with suppliers and on MCX.
Launched 9-karat and 18-karat products; 18-karat is served to some customers for higher margin at lower caratage. Early response described as encouraging.
Management said no gold metal loan or advance gold loan business; no bullion trading in consolidated revenue.
Receivables growth well ahead of sales (3-year receivables CAGR about 51% vs sales 16%), attributed to recent corporate clients with longer credit periods.

qa_highlights.question: What is the total value and rationale of the Sharjah acquisition, and what margins does it earn?
qa_highlights.answer: 80% stake via share swap, valued at up to Rs 9.6 crore; Sharjah earns about 4% PAT and about 5% EBITDA, aided by free-zone tax exemption. Completion expected in 3-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 50% growth guidance based on, volume or price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume only; price changes would be added only if gold prices rise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected utilisation for FY27/FY28 and revenue at 100% utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: No utilisation guidance given. Indicative values at 100%: India about Rs 7 crore/day and Sharjah about Rs 3.6 crore/day. FY27 India target is Rs 450 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why is receivables growth far ahead of sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to recent corporate clients with longer credit periods, and said it will try to reduce debtors.

qa_highlights.question: Cash flow from operations has been negative for six years; when does it turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will try to make it positive in coming years, without a specific timeline; focus is on sales volume and growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a demand impact from the duty change talk and what is the Q2/Q3 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said duty changes have not affected the business historically; Q1 and Q2 are moderate, Q3 and Q4 stronger. No specific Q3 numbers given.

risks_watch: Sharjah acquisition (80% via share swap, up to Rs 9.6 crore) completion in 3-6 months subject to BSE and regulatory approvals; full-year Sharjah contribution and consolidation from Q3 to be confirmed post H1.
Receivables growing far faster than sales (3-year receivables CAGR about 51% vs sales 16%); management said it will try to reduce debtors. Watch debtor days and corporate client credit terms.
Cash flow from operations negative for six years, with no timeline given for turning positive; working capital needed for peak utilisation to come from internal accruals, debt and possibly equity.
Utilisation (India about 25%, Sharjah about 27%) and FY27/FY28 utilisation targets not given; FY27 Rs 450 crore India target and 50% CAGR are volume-based and need checking against H1 numbers.
Concentration: top 10 customers about 50% of revenue, Kerala 90-95% of revenue; only 12 independent jewellers added in Q1 and no new corporate clients after Kalyan.

Esthara store economics (Rs 15 lakh per month first store, breakeven within one year) and store count plans to be updated post H1; promoter remuneration about 10-15% of FY26 PAT to be aligned with PAT going forward.
key_quotes: Definitely by volume growth. Because we are getting higher volume, volume from our existing customers and also we added more customers also
No, no. It will not affect us.
We have not given any guidance regarding this utilization now. So we have the guidance that we can do 450 crore this year.
Yes, we need capital gradually, not in a single, single time. We need it in, we need it gradually.
544425|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident on headline growth and the Sharjah deal, but cautious and often vague on forward numbers. It repeatedly deferred utilisation, Sharjah full-year contribution, Esthara store plans and FY28 targets to H1 results, and gave no specific timeline for positive operating cash flow.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose to 4.58% from 3.5% and PAT margin to 2.35% from 1.26%, with management citing a current PAT margin of about 2.5%, but Sharjah (about 5% EBITDA, about 4% PAT) only consolidates from Q3 and Q1/Q2 are seasonally moderate.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Two more Esthara silver stores are under fit-out and expected to open by end of next month, and Sharjah consolidation/acquisition completion is expected in 3-6 months, though India gold capacity is already 5 kg/day at only about 25% utilisation.

rows.why: Management targets Rs 450 crore India revenue in FY27 and 50% volume CAGR for three years, but India utilisation is only about 25% (about 1.2 kg/day of 5 kg/day), with 12 new independent jewellers added in Q1 and no new corporate clients since Kalyan.

rows.why: Utilisation is only about 25% in India and about 27% in Sharjah, so no new gold capex is needed near term; management said additional working capital for peak utilisation will be funded by accruals, debt and possibly equity, with store plans and utilisation targets deferred to H1.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated the Rs 450 crore FY27 India target and 50% volume CAGR without new upside, while H1 numbers are needed to validate a run-rate of about Rs 101 crore per quarter against the target.

rows.why: 9-karat and 18-karat products were launched with an encouraging early response, and 18-karat is being served to some customers for higher margin, while Esthara's two additional silver stores open by end of next month.

rows.when: Q3 FY27 consolidation, completion in 3-6 months
rows.why: 80% stake via share swap valued at up to Rs 9.6 crore; Sharjah generated Rs 72.46 crore revenue in Jan-Jun 2026 at about 27% utilisation, adding revenue and about 5% EBITDA margin once consolidated, subject to BSE and regulatory approvals.

rows.label: Receivables growth ahead of sales
rows.why: Receivables 3-year CAGR of about 51% versus sales 16%, with management saying it will try to reduce debtors, so working capital strain may persist without a stated timeline.

rows.label: Operating cash flow turning positive
rows.why: Cash flow from operations has been negative for six years and management gave no timeline, with peak-utilisation working capital to be funded by accruals, debt and possibly equity.

tone.note: Management was confident on headline growth, margins and the Sharjah deal but deferred utilisation, Sharjah full-year contribution, Esthara store plans and FY28 targets to H1 results; analysts pressed on receivables, negative operating cash flow and volume-based guidance.

544429|2026-03.headline: HDB Financial Q4 FY26: PAT rose 16.6% QoQ to ₹751 crore, NIM expanded to 8.23% and Gross Stage 3 fell to 2.44%.
544429|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 showed sequential improvement on profitability, margins and asset quality. Disbursements hit a record ₹19,922 crore (up 11.2% QoQ), but gross loan book growth was only 3.4% QoQ and 10.9% YoY. NIM rose 16 bps QoQ to 8.23%, helped by lower borrowing costs, while yield dipped 7-8 bps on product mix. Management said March went well and it has not yet seen level 2/3 impact from the West Asia conflict, which it flagged as a key monitorable.

financial_highlights.change: vs 8.09% in Q3 FY26, 7.55% in Q4 FY25
vs 41.6% in Q3 FY26, 42.9% in Q4 FY25
vs 2.81% at Dec 31, 2025 and at Mar 31, 2025 per Q&A

segments.name: Enterprise lending
segments.commentary: Q4 disbursements grew ~27.9% QoQ and ~15.4% YoY. LAP+EBL book grew 3.8% QoQ on ~36% disbursement growth. Enterprise lending Stage 3 fell to 1.58% from 1.82% in Q3 and 1.79% a year ago.

segments.name: Asset finance (CV/CE)
segments.commentary: Book showed moderate growth in Q4. Gross Stage 3 moved 3.14% (Q4 FY25) to 4.3% (Q3 FY26) to 3.79% (Q4 FY26). FY26 disbursements declined ~3% per analyst; management is pushing used vehicles, with a 50:50 new/used target over four years.

segments.name: Consumer finance
segments.commentary: Book grew 5.3% QoQ and 19.4% YoY, led by consumer durables then auto loans. Stage 3 rose to 2.44% from 2.26% a year ago, but improved from Q3.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book doubled in FY26; disbursements grew 58.7% QoQ.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term growth target: nominal GDP + 6-7% CAGR, with the three-year agenda; management declined to give specific numbers.
Credit cost to moderate to around 2.3% (+/- ) and be sustainable at that level over the medium term.
NIM to be maintained at 8% or above, described as non-negotiable in 2/3/5-year plans; Q4 was 8.23%.
FY27 opex-to-gross loan book expected around 3.7% (FY26 was ~3.8%); cost-to-income guided to a similar range.
Cost of borrowings expected to hold for at least the current quarter; the CP mix is low and bank loans are below 50% of borrowings.
Expects Q1 to be seasonally slower; comparisons should be made Q1 vs Q1, not Q1 vs Q4. Ambition is YoY disbursement growth of 18-20%, described as hopeful, not committed.
capex_capacity: Branch count at 1,730 across 1,161 towns and cities; 20-30 branches may be added or relocated, with consolidation into larger formats (600-800 sq ft to up to 4,000 sq ft).
Management said no square footage has been reduced in the last three quarters as a listed company.
DIY digital sourcing grew ~2.2x in FY26; management expects it to grow further (2x to 5x cited).
App downloads at 1.41 crore; 4.76 lakh daily active users.
Five large AI-powered initiatives underway; bot-based collections nudging covered over 50% of early-bucket customers needing a nudge in Q4, improving early-bucket collection efficiency by ~25 bps.
demand_pricing: Management says all product yields were held in Q4; the 7-8 bps yield decline was from product mix, with unsecured disbursement growth lagging. Yield should return with unsecured growth, staying within the 14%+ range.
Q2, Q3 and Q4 FY26 disbursements were ₹15,599 crore, ₹17,917 crore and ₹19,922 crore respectively.
Secured share of gross loans is 74%, up from the 72% level management has held historically.
Borrowing costs have risen across the market over the past month, per management; the company has no low-cost borrowings left to reset after the last tranche in Oct-Nov 2025.
Average exposure per customer is ~₹1.66 lakh; the retail book is 100% of the portfolio.
AUM mix is 38:38:24 (enterprise lending : asset finance : consumer finance), expected to move to roughly 38:37:25 in the short term.

qa_highlights.question: What changed in March and early April on the West Asia conflict, supply chains and CV operators?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said March went well and is reflected in the results; no level 2/3 impact seen so far. It remains a key monitorable, with a 15-20 day watch period.

qa_highlights.question: Were contingency or buffer provisions considered for MSME/SME stress?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific level 2/3 impact seen yet. Management said LAP and MSME challenges were resolved by the March quarter and the focus is now growth.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 35 bps QoQ fall in cost of funds and can it be sustained given market rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it held lending rates and worked on borrowing strategies; no low-cost borrowings remain to reset. Cost of funds should hold for the current quarter, though market rates have risen.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Stage 1 PCR rise by 30 bps, and why did enterprise lending PCR fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Provisioning is refreshed quarterly on an automated ECL basis (fully automated this quarter) using PD, LGD and product mix. Management said there is no one-time item.

qa_highlights.question: Why did asset finance Stage 3 recover so quickly?
qa_highlights.answer: Recovery has been K-shaped: accounts challenged in Q1 recovered slowly, while newer slippages are recovering faster. Management pushed recoveries and flow-forward reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Will NIM be sustained at 8%+ and what about branch additions?
qa_highlights.answer: 8%+ NIM is non-negotiable in internal plans; Q4 was 8.23%. Branch count will change by 20-30 sites through consolidation and upsizing, with digital channels driving growth.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict, supply chain disruption and El Nino impact on CV and MSME repayments; management says it is too early to call second- and third-order effects.
Rising market borrowing costs (CP mix low, bank loans below 50%), which could pressure the 8%+ NIM.
Disbursement-to-book conversion: book growth of 3.4% QoQ and 10.9% YoY is still below the nominal GDP + 6-7% aspiration.
Asset finance Stage 3 at 3.79% and consumer finance Stage 3 at 2.44%; sustainability of the recovery and the used-vehicle push.
Write-off quantum for FY26 and Q4 was not disclosed on the call; to be provided offline.
Yield dilution from product mix until unsecured business loans regain growth.
544429|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on operations and asset quality, with repeated emphasis on growth and NIM discipline. Cautious and evasive on the West Asia conflict, borrowing-cost outlook and forward growth numbers, which were framed as hopes rather than targets.
key_quotes: Gross NPA, which we also report as Gross Stage 3 – we don't report two different numbers – reduced to 2.44% as at March 31, 2026 vs 2.81% as at December 31, 2025.
But an 8 %+ is a non-negotiable the way we treat it internally today.
So, we haven't seen any major disruption is the way I would put it.
I would like to think at least for the current quarter we're good, right?

rows.label: Record disbursement momentum into Q1 FY27

544429|2026-06.headline: HDB Financial Q1 FY27 PAT rose 38.3% YoY to ₹785 crores, a record, with Stage 3 down to 2.34% and NIM at 8.35%.
544429|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 delivered record quarterly profit of ₹785 crores (up 38.3% YoY, 4.6% QoQ) with ROA of 2.5% and ROE of 15%. Gross Stage 3 improved to 2.34% from 2.44% in March 2026 and 2.56% a year earlier, and credit cost held at 2.32% versus 2.35% in Q4. Loan book grew 11.3% YoY to ₹1,21,846 crores but only 2.8% QoQ, with Asset Finance and Business Loans still lagging. Management pushed growth recovery into Q2–Q3 and kept the 2.3% steady-state credit cost and 8%+ NIM framing without formal annual guidance.

segments.commentary: Q1 disbursements grew 14% YoY; LAP (LAP+ EBL) book grew 13.2% YoY but LAP growth is steadying at about 3–4%. Gold loan book doubled YoY, with about 500 branches enabled; Unsecured Business Loans disbursements began accelerating late in the quarter, while the book shrank marginally QoQ.

segments.name: Asset Finance
segments.commentary: Commercial vehicle book grew 10% YoY and construction equipment 8% YoY; disbursements remain the laggard. Management reduced high-value, low-return products (tractor trailers, high-end HCVs), and says Stage 3 improved sequentially.

segments.name: Consumer Finance
segments.commentary: Book grew 7.5% QoQ and 21% YoY; consumer durables grew over 50% YoY on compressor season demand, and auto loans grew 21% YoY. Auto is flagged as the area needing more growth.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give formal guidance; steady-state credit cost viewed at about 2.3%, with a possible decline only if the economy improves.
NIM expected to hold at 8%+ and focus remains 2.5% ROA on a consistent basis.
Business Loans book expected to turn positive QoQ from Q2 and show YoY growth from Q3; Q2 expected to be positive in direction.
Cost of funds expected to be range-bound in Q2; Q3 view deferred. Current ratio about 1.3x and CP book under 2%.
Asset Finance growth expected to pick up over the next three to four quarters, with July run rate improving if the trend holds.
Viral Shah's 18% growth question was not answered; management said it would revert closer to dates.
capex_capacity: Gold loans: about 500+ branches enabled; management says the existing network could roughly double gold loans over time, with the timing still under internal work.
Distribution footprint of about 1.6 lakh+ retail touchpoints across about 1,200 cities; relationships with 150+ consumer durable manufacturers.
Rural micro-finance run through a couple of hundred branches as a small pilot; management declined to say whether it would be shut down.
Customer franchise 23.9 million, up 18.6% YoY and 4.1% QoQ.
demand_pricing: Q1 disbursements ₹17,629 crores, up 16.2% YoY; gross loan book ₹1,21,846 crores, up 11.3% YoY and 2.8% QoQ; secured loans 73.9% of book.
May 2026 was the highest-ever volume for a large number of Asset Finance products management wants to grow.
Yields described as fairly constant; Q1 yield uptick attributed to product mix (consumer durables seasonality), not to pricing.
Competition: management declined to name who is taking up the Asset Finance segments it is vacating.
Fuel price increases of about 8–9% reportedly passed on in small doses; freight rates described as stable for its customer base.
ECLGS uptake described as work in progress and modest; eligibility requires working capital end-use.
Top 20 customers are about 0.3% of AUM, so the book is retail-weighted.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Asset Finance disbursement lagging and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Used CV build-out and product reprioritisation are largely done, and growth should show over the next few quarters; July run rate improvement was expected but not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full-year credit cost guidance for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not guide; 2.3% is the steady-state view, with a possible decline only if economic conditions improve. Current metrics are comfortable, and check bounce for June–July was described as fine.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Business Loans, MFI and two-wheeler books shrinking QoQ?

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Asset Finance Stage 3 level and can it fall toward 3%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline is on a flat book; Stage 3 should fall as the book grows and as the economy improves, and it was steady so far in June-July.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a cost-of-funds outlook and liquidity strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of funds expected to be range-bound in Q2; liquidity is supported by a current ratio of about 1.3x and CP under 2%, and Q3 guidance is deferred.

qa_highlights.question: Is the yield uptick in Q1 seasonal?
qa_highlights.answer: The uptick is purely product mix, driven by the consumer durables compressor season; yields are otherwise stable, and the next peak is Dussehra-Diwali.

544429|2026-09.headline: HDB Financial Q2 FY27 PAT rose 34% YoY to ₹780 crore, NIM 8.23%, Stage 3 down to 2.43%, with management guiding to a near-term 8.2%+ NIM.
544429|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 showed disbursements up 18.7% YoY to ₹18,522 crore and PAT up 34% YoY to ₹780 crore, with Stage 3 improving YoY to 2.43%. Gross loan book grew 11.7% YoY to ₹1,24,469 crore, which management described as slow relative to disbursements because of high repayments. Sequentially, NIM was 8.23% versus 8.35% in Q1, and credit cost rose to 2.37%, with Stage 2 build-up in Asset Finance (mainly used/new CV) flagged as seasonal. The 25 bps repo hike on October 7, 2026 is the main near-term margin variable; management expects a minor impact in Q3 and aims to hold NIM at 8.2%+ in the near term.

financial_highlights.change: vs 7.95% in Q2FY26 and 8.35% in Q1FY27
vs 40.7% in Q2FY26 and 39.9% in Q1FY27

segments.name: Enterprise Lending
segments.commentary: Disbursements grew 25.5% YoY; LAP+EBL (mortgage) disbursements up 30% YoY, LAP growing about 3-3.5% QoQ. Gold loan disbursements up over 60% YoY, unsecured business loans turned slightly positive QoQ (+0.2%) after six quarters.

segments.name: Asset Finance
segments.commentary: Commercial vehicle book up 8% YoY and construction equipment up 12% YoY. New CV is hitting budget, while used CV growth is weak and is being addressed through internal actions; CV and CE drove the Stage 2 build-up.

segments.name: Consumer Finance
segments.commentary: Disbursements up over 25% YoY and book up 22% YoY. Consumer durables book up 49% YoY, auto loans up 22%, relationship personal loans up 16%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects NIM to hold in a narrow range, targeting at least 8.2%+ in the near term and 8%+ over the long term; minor impact expected in Q3 from the 25 bps repo hike.
Disbursement trajectory expected to rise, with Q3 better than Q2 and Q4 better than Q3; management hopes Q4 shows growth in the 17-18% range, though it did not commit to a number.
Medium-term credit cost target of 2.3% +/- range; Q2 credit cost of 2.37% described as a 5 bps uptick expected to reverse.
ROA target of 2.5%+ on an annualised basis in the short to medium term.

AI-led customer onboarding started in consumer finance; over 1 in 5 early-bucket collection calls now handled by an AI bot.

qa_highlights.question: Why did asset yields moderate QoQ despite strong consumer finance growth, and how will cost of funds and NIM trend if repo rises 75-100 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 is seasonally about 10-12 bps higher on NIM. Management said NIM came in 1-2 bps above plan, excluding an extra day in Q2, and expects only a minor Q3 impact, with LAP floating-rate pass-through and Q3 product mix as offsets.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Asset Finance growth weak, is the problem in new or used CV?
qa_highlights.answer: New CV is hitting budget; used CV is the issue, with a combination of internal challenges and weak market demand. Delinquencies in the older book have not yet come off.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the Stage 2 build-up in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to CV, and slightly to CE, as seasonal and expected to revert in the coming quarter. Management said the rise was 9 bps QoQ and that faster book growth would have shown about 2 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Will drought and macro conditions in key states affect Asset Finance and the credit cost guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is monitoring impacts, with a small tractor exposure in drought-declared areas. Credit cost is managed within 2.3% +/-, and it could fall about 5 bps next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for Asset Finance growth and FY28 growth, and the risk to NIM plus fee income from the insurance commission proposal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management believes growth will return to the industry median, citing capacity and network readiness; FY26 disbursement growth was 3%. On fees, the company is still assessing the proposal, with ₹455 crore of insurance-related income at stake.

544430|2026-03.headline: Sambhv Steel Tubes Q4 FY26 revenue rose 38% to INR685 crores and EBITDA 91% to INR92 crores, with record quarterly profit.
544430|2026-03.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue, EBITDA and PAT for Q4 FY26, with EBITDA per ton at INR9,500 excluding sponge iron sales, helped by raw-material lag and firm HR coil prices. For FY26, sales volume rose 37% to 3,96,000 tons, revenue 60% to INR2,413 crores and PAT more than doubled to INR143 crores. Capex was raised: the Kesda stainless steel Phase 1 (3,60,000 tpa) is on track for Q4 FY27, plus an additional INR200 crores of brownfield and power/DFT projects. Management guided Q1 FY27 EBITDA per ton to INR7,500-8,000 and FY27 average to INR7,000-8,000.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 EBITDA per ton so high, and what is sustainable?

qa_highlights.question: Is the stainless steel production versus sales gap explained?

The Kuthrel stainless CR coil debottlenecking doubled capacity to 116,000 tpa, and the Kesda greenfield project is guided for Q4 FY27 commissioning.
