FY27 revenue and EBITDA growth of 10-15% over FY26; FY26 operating EBITDA base cited as about INR270 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What will peak debt, finance cost and cost of debt look like after Kesda?

qa_highlights.question: Is the Kesda Q4 FY27 timeline achievable through monsoon?

qa_highlights.question: Rationale for the INR100 crore warrant issue?

qa_highlights.question: Why co-branding for stainless pipes instead of direct sales?

qa_highlights.question: Stainless CR coil margin and HR coil margin?

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 EBITDA growth guided at only 10-15% given the stainless ramp?

qa_highlights.question: Working capital needs and capex schedule?

MS pipe prices guided to fall a further 3-5% this financial year; Q2 FY27 realisations guided lower for MS pipe (about INR58,000/ton from INR60,000) and GP pipe, with monsoon softness flagged.

544430|2026-09.headline: Sambhv Q2 FY27 revenue INR840 crore, EBITDA INR105 crore (>12% margin), PAT INR61 crore; FY27 EBITDA/ton guided at INR8,000-8,500.

EBITDA per ton fell from about INR8,800 in Q1 to about INR8,200 in Q2, attributed to monsoon-related raw material yield losses, stainless steel margin compression from Chinese 200/300 series dumping after QCO relaxation, and normalising Q1 prices. Management raised its FY27 EBITDA/ton bracket to INR8,000-8,500 and announced a seamless stainless steel pipe project (INR150 crore, 14,400 tpa, production by March 2028). Working capital days fell to 4-5, which management said is not sustainable versus a 20-25 day norm.

segments.name: Galvanised / coated products
segments.commentary: EBITDA per ton cited at about INR7,000. Q3 realisation guided at INR78-79 for GP coil and pipe, versus INR72-73 in Q2.

segments.name: Seamless stainless steel pipes (new)
segments.commentary: Planned 14,400 tpa piercing and pilgering plant, INR150 crore capex, production expected by March 2028. Management targets about 10,000 tons by FY30 and an EBITDA of INR60-70 crore at steady state.

FY27 EBITDA per ton bracket raised to INR8,000-8,500.
FY27 total sales including Kesda about 5.5 lakh tons; EBITDA upward of INR550 crore. FY28 about 7 lakh tons and EBITDA upward of INR750 crore (volume and EBITDA targets as stated on the call).
Stainless steel Kesda plant (360,000 tpa, with 25 MW power) to be live by March 2027; first-year utilisation 30-35%, 60-65% by FY29.

Stainless steel operating at about 60% utilisation currently; mostly thinner-gauge output below 0.9 mm.
demand_pricing: Q2 MS pipe realisation about INR60-61; Q3 guided at INR63-64 as coil prices are elevated.
Q2 GP coil and pipe realisation about INR72-73; Q3 guided at INR78-79.
Stainless steel prices stable in Q3 per management, with 200 series price flat and 300 series price flat.
Chinese 200 and 300 series imports dumped below cost after QCO relaxation; management expects government action (minimum import price, anti-dumping) possibly by March 2027.
Seamless: domestic 2-3 lakh tpa documented demand; above 6-inch seamless about 90% imported; PLI 1.2 MoU signed with about 13% of revenue expected as incentive.
Stainless steel distributors and traders destocked in Q2 ahead of price rises; management said Q2 volume was partly pulled forward and Q3 volume will be capped at Q1 levels.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EBITDA/ton fall from Q1 to Q2 came from mix versus price and cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the roughly INR600/ton fall to monsoon raw material yield losses, stainless steel margin compression of 12,000-13,000 tons per annum from QCO relaxation and Chinese dumping, and normalising Q1 war-driven price spikes. Q1 was described as an outlier.

qa_highlights.question: Is the seamless plant's EBITDA per ton and return on capital sound?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 304 realisation of INR350-360/ton with INR50-55 margin and 316 realisation above INR450/ton with INR80-90 margin. It estimated about 15-16% normal EBITDA margin and INR60-70 crore EBITDA at about 10,000 tons; ROCE estimate was above 24-25%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Kesda stainless expansion be sold at a discount to imports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 10% PLI incentive lets it undercut prices and cited export premiums of 10-15% for competitors. It said first sales will be to replacement and trader markets that need no OEM approval, with OEM approvals expected within 1-2 years of production.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Q2 operating performance continue into Q3 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the stainless steel margin of INR12,000-13,000/ton is sustainable with imports already in the market. It said Q3 capacity utilisation cannot rise above Q2, and volume is capped at Q1 levels because of distributor destocking.

qa_highlights.question: Are working capital days of 4-5 sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the improvement reflected one-time destocking, faster customer recoveries and better supplier credit. She said 20-25 days is the optimum level for the company and the industry.

Raw material supply for stainless (nickel substitutes, imported high-value alloys, nickel pig iron) and Middle East-related shipping disruption, though management says supply is currently adequate.
Q3 volumes capped at Q1 levels after destocking and realisations guided up on elevated coil prices.

544439|2026-03.headline: Crizac FY26 revenue rose 22.7% to INR 10,422 mn and Q4 PAT rose 50% to INR 750 mn, but management withheld FY27 guidance until next quarter.
544439|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR 3,917 mn (up 15% YoY, up 40.6% QoQ) and FY26 EBITDA reached about INR 2,824 mn with margin up 172 bps to 27%. Q4 EBITDA grew 42.8% YoY to INR 939 mn, with margin at 24%, and management attributed part of the Q4 margin jump to favourable GBP/INR movement it called transitional. Management completed or operationalised four acquisitions/investments (StudiesPlanet, 51% of Global Tree Careers, EduMentor commitment, Medway NZ team) and the company remains debt-free with net cash of INR 4,674 mn. FY27 guidance was deferred to the next quarter citing geopolitical uncertainty, with management saying growth should be in line with the past trend and a full-year growth of 15% to 17% noted in Q&A.

544439|2026-06.headline: Crizac Q1 FY27 revenue fell 4% YoY to INR2,012 million on adverse university mix; management now guides FY27 flat versus FY26.
544439|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR2,012 million, down 4% YoY and below the INR3,917 million of Q4 FY26, consistent with Q1 being the seasonal trough. Management attributed the decline to a less favourable university mix (fewer high-fee top-ranked university bonuses and slabs), not lower platform activity, as enrolments rose 15% YoY. EBITDA fell 7.6% YoY to INR600 million, with margin at 29.8% versus 31%, while PAT grew 2.9% to INR471 million. Management moved from earlier growth expectations to a flat FY27 outlook, citing flight disruption and rupee volatility expected to hit Q2, with pent-up demand expected in Q3 and Q4. It also announced a leadership change: Chairman Christopher Nagle stepped down as UK CEO and became Non-Executive Chairman of the Indian holding company, with Eric Wijmenga taking UK and Europe operations.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue fall QoQ and what is the Q2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Constant-currency revenue fell about 4% as volume rose 15% but university mix shifted; Q2 expected weaker due to Feb-June flight cancellations and rupee volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth be 20-25% or 15-17% as earlier hinted?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management now expects FY27 flat versus FY26, with pent-up demand in Q3 and Q4 offsetting Q1 and Q2 shortfalls.

qa_highlights.question: Why is standalone PBT above consolidated PBT in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Crizac India standalone recognised some payments as revenue; investments in Crizac UK and subsidiaries should pay off in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a buyback plan given the stock trades around 11x EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company has only about 20% public float and SEBI rules do not allow a buyback at this level; the compliance team will look at the suggestion.

qa_highlights.question: Will the UK concentration fall, and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the target is to get UK share below 60% within about three years, aided by Innova (Netherlands) and other markets, though policy shifts will slow this.

qa_highlights.question: Will value-added services become material?
qa_highlights.answer: Not initially; they could add 2-5% to EBITDA and 1-1.5% of revenue over the next couple of years, with ForeignAdmits accelerating this.

qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said the DRHP commits to a minimum 40% of PAT as dividend for at least three years; FY26 is done, leaving at least two more years.

544439|2026-09.headline: Crizac Q2 FY27 operating income fell 36.7% YoY to INR 1,027 million; management guides FY27 revenue and profit in line with FY26 on deferred students.
544439|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was hit by the West Asia conflict, currency moves in a key source market, and post-grad students deferring intakes. Operating income was INR 1,027 million (down 36.7% YoY), operating EBITDA INR 330 million (down 44%), and PAT INR 369 million (down 23.7%). Management attributes the shortfall to timing, saying revenue is deferred rather than lost, with Q3 FY27 revenue guided up 10-12% YoY and FY27 revenue and profit guided in line with FY26. An interim dividend of INR 4 per share was declared, and the company reported net cash of about INR 5,984 million.

segments.name: UK (anchor market)
segments.commentary: Management says UK-sponsored study visas fell 20% between FY24 and FY26 while Crizac students grew 53%. Three universities accounted for 44% of revenue. The UK budget of 28 October proposed a 2-year graduate visa for high-compliance universities versus 18 months for others from January 2027; qualifying universities are yet to be defined.

segments.name: Non-UK destinations
segments.commentary: Non-UK destinations were about 9.5% of H1 applications versus 4.7% in H1 FY26, but contributed only 1.4% of revenue as of today. Management targets 30% of revenue from outside the UK by FY30.

FY27 revenue and profit guided in line with FY26, barring any black swan event; management says a large share of Q4 applications is already received and being processed.
Interim dividend INR 4 per share declared; total FY27 dividend including final expected at INR 8-10 per share.
Steady-state EBITDA margin guided at 25-26%, same as last year; salary cost expected at 3-4% of revenue in the medium to long term.
No FY28 guidance yet; management says it will be in a better position to guide next quarter. FY28 is subject to market reaction and US mid-term election outcomes.

Asset-light model: accommodation and student loans are distributed as a DSA for third parties; no real estate acquisition planned.

demand_pricing: Applications fell about 3% YoY in Q2, but revenue fell about 37%. Management attributes the gap to deferral timing, not lower revenue per student or mix.
Market share rose from 3.5% to 6% globally (FY24 to FY26). Share of Indian students rose from 9% to 13.9%, while visas to Indian students fell 22% over the same period.

Students deferred to the November and January intakes. Management says the Q2 shortfall should be recovered in Q3 and Q4.
Gross margin was about 54% in Q2 versus about 70% last year. Management says this reflects the H1 mix: 30% retained and 70% paid to the accounting partner, with full-year margin expected at 65-70%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q2 revenue gap came from post-August deferrals, and what gives confidence deferrals will convert rather than cancel?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not quantify deferrals by student count, since they span September, November and January intakes. It cited pipeline evidence (applications, deposits, visas) supporting 10-12% Q3 growth, and said many students have deferred to the January intake.

qa_highlights.question: Is the applications-to-revenue gap purely timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said it was mainly students deferring, all timing-related, with no change in revenue per student.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 M&A or capital deployment be pursued given the cash balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is actively looking at M&A but is cautious given geopolitical uncertainty. Criteria include synergies, founders, source and destination jurisdictions, revenue and EBITDA; the target is EBITDA-accretive at 10-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone results hold up while consolidated results fell, and was the INR 57 crore termination fee one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone India books revenue on application processing, ahead of UK subsidiaries, which book on enrolment. The termination fee to Crizac Informatics UK (INR 57 crore vs INR 21.5 crore in FY25) was a one-time item that will not recur in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for employee cost and EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost is largely fixed and rose with acquisitions and tech hiring. Salary cost is expected at 3-4% of revenue in the medium to long term, and steady-state EBITDA margin is 25-26%.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company diversify away from the UK, and when will non-UK revenue reach 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no date for 10% non-UK revenue. It expects 30% of revenue from outside the UK by FY30, citing New Zealand (via Medway), Netherlands, Europe and expected openings in Australia, Canada and the US.

Trade receivables rose to about INR2.64 billion at year-end on EATS ramp-up, which management expects to normalise by H1 FY27.

EBITDA rose 11% to INR1.6 billion, but margin moderated to 35.8% on pre-operating and employee costs for new airports (Noida, Cochin, Delhi). PAT was helped by a INR131 million one-time GST provision write-back in other income.

financial_highlights.change: ex-Mumbai, Guwahati and some South India markets about 7%
Adjusted for INR223 million lounge aggregation cost reclassification: INR3.65 billion, about 81%
+35.6% YoY vs 25.3% margin last year; includes INR131 million GST provision write-back

segments.name: Travel QSR and lounges (system-wide)
segments.commentary: 580 outlets and lounges at June end across 21 airports; 153 brands; 87 travel QSR outlets and two lounges added over last 12 months. Noida International Airport commenced operations in the quarter.

segments.name: JV / associate business
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 15% per management's implied figure as questioned by analysts; drag from Western India airports with Middle East exposure. Management said JV ramp-up continues.

segments.name: Passenger services (Elite Assist)
segments.commentary: Launched at Noida International Airport with meet-and-greet and porter services; to integrate into the EATS platform and expand to more airports.

guidance_outlook: Management expects H2 FY27 passenger traffic bounce-back as airlines restore long-haul international routes from September and October 2026.
About 90 units commissioned over last 12 months expected to normalise over next 12 months; benefits to play out in H2 FY27.
Over 50 outlets under development, mostly to open in FY27; 12-18 months to mature at existing terminals, 18-24 months at greenfield airports.
Pre-operating costs for Cochin, Delhi and Noida ramp-up expected to normalise in about 12 months, returning to traditional cost levels.
Delhi T3 contract runs to 30 September 2026; GHL JV bid result pending. Chennai and Kolkata renewals due end-March 2027 and early Q1 FY28.
Bhogapuram Airport opened 17 August 2026 with multiple outlets under JV GHL.
capex_capacity: Over 50 outlets under construction or about to start construction across airports including Delhi, Navi Mumbai, Bhogapuram and Noida.
Noida International Airport outlets and passenger services commissioned in the quarter.
Asia focus for international expansion; Dubai entity set up for the Middle East and Indonesia entity set up recently to enable local bids.
Highways wayside amenities (WSA) under evaluation, with government plan of about 1,000 wayside amenities; management says medium-to-long term.
demand_pricing: Passenger traffic broadly flat YoY in Q1: April declined, May rebounded to record domestic month, June softened on renewed conflict. Management says traffic in July-August similar to Q1 trend, with international the drag.
LFL growth normally runs 5-7 percentage points above passenger traffic; management did not take significant price increases this year, with growth from premiumisation, bundles and brand changes.
Mumbai and Guwahati hit by traffic migration to new airport infrastructure; South India markets hit by Middle East exposure.
Contract renewal rate moved from about 94% to 92%, attributed to non-renewal of small highway outlets.
Management says bidding discipline stays on cash return; net contract gains are lumpy and not guided.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 4.2% LFL came from higher spend per passenger, and what is sustainable LFL?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said LFL is typically 5-7 points above passenger traffic; it was 7% ex-affected markets. Growth came from premiumisation, bundles, brand edits and limited pricing, with price increases kept tempered.

qa_highlights.question: Lounge aggregation cost and other expenses rise in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: INR223 million of lounge aggregation cost sits in other expenses; excluding it, other expenses rose 22% YoY. Management expects normalisation within about 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why are JV and associate revenues growing slower than consolidated?
qa_highlights.answer: Some JV contracts are moving to JV structures over time, and Western airports with Middle East exposure, which form a bulk of JV portfolio, were hit.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Delhi T3 contract moving to JV in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Delhi T3 contract runs to 30 September 2026; GHL has bid and results are awaited. The new SPV with GMR has 30% TFS shareholding, so it will not be consolidated going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Are the 50 outlets under development in existing airports?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, a blend of already-announced airports such as Delhi, Navi Mumbai and Bhogapuram; these were won 3-8 months ago and are in build-out.

qa_highlights.question: Highways strategy: is it accelerating?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said highways are a medium-to-long-term opportunity tied to government wayside amenity plans, with a return threshold that must be met; it will be calibrated, not immediate.

risks_watch: International traffic recovery depends on airline route restorations from September-October 2026; Middle East conflict renewed in June.
EBITDA margin (35.8%) under pressure from pre-operating and employee costs at new airports; watch normalisation in next 12 months.
Delhi T3 contract ends 30 September 2026 and the GHL JV bid outcome is unknown; it moves out of consolidation.
Chennai and Kolkata renewals due end-March 2027 and early Q1 FY28 may bring cost resets.
PAT growth flattered by INR131 million one-time GST write-back; underlying growth is lower.
544443|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on medium-term growth and balance sheet, but cautious on near-term traffic; management repeatedly attributes weakness to temporary external factors. Evasive on specific numbers such as net contract gain targets and JV economics, and on the Delhi T3 bid outcome.

Those are the leverages that we tend to enjoy, in terms of bringing the required economies of scale.
In the new SPV, our shareholding with GMR is 30% and therefore it doesn't get consolidated going forward.

So, the investment is already made, the capacity is in place, and we are ready. When traffic returns, and history tells us it will, TFS is well -positioned to benefit from the network and groundwork we have put in place over the past 12 months.

544444|2026-03.headline: Glen Industries H2 FY26 PAT of INR8.20 crore on INR108.60 crore income; management targets INR500 crore turnover and INR90 crore EBITDA in FY28.
544444|2026-03.overview: FY26 total income was INR205.16 crore, EBITDA INR38.50 crore and PAT INR16.50 crore, with H2 FY26 income of INR108.60 crore, EBITDA INR18.69 crore and PAT INR8.20 crore. Management attributed margin compression from about 23-24% in FY25 to about 18-19% in FY26 to passing on PLA price benefits to customers. A capacity expansion (plastic food containers roughly 3x, plus about 750 MT paper-based food packaging including paper cups) has a revised project cost of INR130-135 crore, now expected to start commercial production from September 2026. Raw material prices rose sharply after the West Asia conflict, with polypropylene peaking near INR150/kg and now about INR135/kg.

financial_highlights.metric: EBITDA margin FY26 (as cited on call)
financial_highlights.change: down from about 23-24% in FY25 per management and analyst

financial_highlights.value: Thin-wall food containers 82.72%; PLA and paper straws 17.16%; mould designing 0.12%

segments.name: Thin-wall food containers
segments.commentary: About 82.72% of FY26 revenue with capacity utilisation of about 77.74%. Raw-material price pass-through is monthly, impacting turnover by about INR2.5 crore per month during the recent price rise.

segments.name: PLA and paper straws
segments.commentary: About 17.16% of FY26 revenue; utilisation about 28.33% (PLA) and 34.13% (paper). Management says these are seasonal, peak-season-only (4-4.5 months), and sees utilisation capped near 35%; no further straw capex planned.

segments.name: Mould designing services
segments.commentary: About 0.12% of FY26 revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY28 target: turnover above INR500 crore with EBITDA of about INR90 crore (about 18-19% margin), based on pre-war raw material prices.
Expansion revenue: existing capacity about INR200-215 crore; new project adds about INR300 crore; combined about INR500 crore per annum.
FY27 incremental revenue from new capacity estimated at INR100-125 crore, depending on stabilisation speed; some revenue expected in FY27.
Commercial production targeted from September 2026, with full project operational by October-December 2026.
Management says EBITDA margin sustainable at 18-19% over the long run; paper cup margin around 18%.
Eight additional injection moulding machines (20 to 29) expected to add about INR15 crore annual revenue.
capex_capacity: Expansion project cost revised to INR130-135 crore from about INR100 crore, citing rupee depreciation (85-86 to about 96 per USD-equivalent as stated), wider scope in building and machinery, and printing machines.
Funding: INR50 crore term loan and INR50 crore IPO proceeds for original INR100 crore; incremental INR30-32 crore from internal accruals; no additional debt or equity planned.
Commissioning delayed about three months due to SIR and West Bengal elections holding up building plan approvals; commercial production now expected from September 2026.
Injection moulding machines raised from 20 to 29.
Existing land parcel remains mortgaged to bank; to be released after new facility is capitalised.
Management says no further straw capex; straw capacity sufficient for demand.
demand_pricing: PLA price about INR205/kg now vs INR195-197/kg pre-war; polypropylene about INR135/kg now vs INR90-92/kg pre-war, peaking near INR150/kg; paper stable (locally sourced).
Pass-through: PLA price changes passed on to customers from March; food container prices adjusted monthly; management says absolute margin preserved though percentage margin falls.

Raw material sourcing: about 85% imported (mainly Middle East earlier), 15% from Indian Oil; imported material from China at 5-6% price advantage; Middle East supply expected to normalise in 1-2 months.
Raw material inventory above 3 months currently; finished goods 2-2.5 months.

Customer concentration: no customer above 5-6% of total sales; top 4-5 export customers (US, UK, Greece) account for about 50-60% of export sales; over 300 domestic distributors; Parle about 25% of corporate sales as stated.
Exports: about 40 recurring international clients across Europe, US, Australia, South Korea; export revenue declined in FY26 due to lower polymer prices vs FY25, not volume or war.
Geography: eastern India about 35% of revenue; north and west next.
Competition: few national/export players in India with HACCP and FSSC certifications; management cites brand and standards as barriers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin decline and what is the sustainable range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PLA price benefits were passed to customers in FY26, lowering margin from about 23% (FY25) to about 18-19%; sustainable range stated as 18-19%.

qa_highlights.question: Expansion capex, timeline and revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Project cost revised to INR130-135 crore; commercial production from September 2026, full operations by December 2026; combined revenue potential about INR500 crore per annum.

qa_highlights.question: Utilisation of straws and paper products given seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said straw utilisation can not exceed about 35% due to 4-4.5 month peak season; paper cups are not currently manufactured, and the expansion includes paper cups with about 18% margin.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of raw material price rise on FY27 turnover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated about INR2-2.5 crore per month turnover uplift from price pass-through, with no change to absolute margin; guidance remains based on pre-war prices.

qa_highlights.question: Was there any production disruption from the war?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no disruption; about two months of inventory was held and two months' requirement was imported from China.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility: PP and PLA prices remain elevated; management says guidance excludes current prices and could reverse within about two months of conflict ending.
Margin percentage compression in price-rising periods; EBITDA margin moved from about 17-18% to higher levels in prior halves.
Execution risk on the new project: approvals delayed about three months, commissioning expected September 2026, with capacity ramp-up pace determining FY27 revenue.
Seasonal demand in straws (beverage sector) keeping utilisation low around 28-34%.
Working capital build: raw material inventory above 3 months and inventory cycle of 5-5.5 months against about 4 months normal, affecting ROCE.

Undisclosed land parcel and future diversification plans; management declined to specify new products.

544447|2026-06.headline: Smartworks Q1 FY27 revenue rose 44% YoY to INR 546 crores, with normalized EBITDA margin at 19.6% and guidance of 28-30% revenue growth reaffirmed.
544447|2026-06.overview: Revenue reached INR 546 crores, up 44% YoY and 5% QoQ, while normalized EBITDA grew 74% YoY to INR 107 crores at a 19.6% margin. Normalized PAT nearly tripled YoY to INR 39 crores. Growth was supported by mature-centre occupancy (committed 92%) and a higher share of 1,000+ seat clients, GCCs and multi-city clients, though overall occupancy dipped to 81% from 82% QoQ as new centres filled up. Management reaffirmed FY27 guidance (28-30% revenue growth, 19-20% normalized EBITDA margin, 13 million sq ft by March 2027) and started a heavy capex cycle of INR 550-600 crores for the year.

financial_highlights.change: vs 16.2% in Q1 FY26 and 19% in Q4 FY26
vs negative INR 4.9 crores a year ago
vs INR 22 crores in same quarter last year

segments.name: Core rental (enterprise annuity)
segments.commentary: Enterprise annuity demand is 92% of rental revenue; 1,000+ seat cohort is 41% of revenue (37% in FY26). Committed contracted revenue is about INR 5,400 crores, covering 87% of FY27 revenue.

segments.name: GCC clients
segments.commentary: GCCs contribute 21% of revenue, up from 15% in FY26. Recent wins include a Swiss bank and a manufacturing GCC; a Japanese NBFC subsidiary took space in Mumbai.

segments.name: Singapore
segments.commentary: Work Studio acquired, taking the portfolio to over 1,500 seats (about 2% of revenue); 400-450 seats now available to sell, funded from Singapore cash flows. Management says no further meaningful expansion planned.

segments.name: Value-added services (VAS)
segments.commentary: Non-lease rental revenue rose to over INR 68 crores from INR 22 crores YoY, and is take-rate based with no direct cost. VAS guidance is not built into the FY27 projections.

guidance_outlook: Reaffirmed FY27 revenue growth of 28-30%, normalized EBITDA margin of 19-20%, and operational footprint above 13 million sq ft by March 2027.
Plans to add 2.5-3 million sq ft of operational space in FY27; more than 3.5 million sq ft signed, giving a buffer of about 0.7-0.8 million sq ft.
Capex guided at INR 550-600 crores for FY27, with heavy spend in the next two quarters.
Management expects ROCE to expand meaningfully through FY28 as capex cohorts mature.
Revenue jump expected mainly in Q3 or Q4 as new centres ramp up (about 12 months to ramp).
capex_capacity: Operational footprint 10.4 million sq ft as of June 2026; 1.9 million sq ft under fit-out; 0.3 million sq ft added in Q1 and 2.1 million sq ft over the last 12 months.

About 3 million sq ft to come online over the next 9 months, including Eastbridge (Mumbai) and Eastside (Pune), both landing in H2 FY27. Vikhroli asset is 8.15 lakh sq ft, described as the world's largest standalone managed campus.
New fit-out capex is INR 1,350 per sq ft, rising about 5% a year; refurbishment is about 15% of initial capex every three years (around INR 5 per sq ft per year, by management's estimate).
Every building needed for the next two years is secured; FY29 work has begun. Long-term rights give 10-15 years of access.
Security deposits of INR 33 crores paid to landlords to lock buildings for FY28 and part of FY29.
demand_pricing: Occupancy 81% (vs 82% in Q4 FY26), reflecting new centres still filling. Mature centres at 89% on 9.1 million sq ft; committed occupancy 92%. Management guides 80-85% occupancy over the next three quarters.

Seat retention 74% in Q1, with client count down while occupied seats and revenue rose. Management says the churn is deliberate repricing of older, lower-rate clients; the annual retention range it cited was 80-88%.
Realization on incremental mature-footprint seats leased in Q1 FY27 was about INR 181 per sq ft per month, up from about INR 170 a year earlier. Management cited a rental INR 185 per seat figure.
Mix: IT/ITES down to 35% of clients (from over 40%); target 25-30/35%. Multi-city clients 35% of revenue (31% in FY26).
Pre-commitment: about 30-35% of new buildings is pre-committed by existing or incoming clients. Landlord mix is about 65% non-institutional and 35% institutional.

qa_highlights.question: Rationale for the Singapore Work Studio acquisition, expected revenue and occupancy, and whether fit-out costs of INR 1,350 face inflation.
qa_highlights.answer: Acquired from internal cash flows at roughly construction cost; the target was about 60% occupied. Singapore is about 80,000 sq ft in total and 2% of revenue, with 400-450 seats now available to sell. Expansion will not be meaningful, and capex is set at INR 550-600 crores for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the expansion is speculative, and how much is pre-leased?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 30-35% of any new building is pre-committed by existing clients, and occupancy ramps to 80-85% within 13-14 months, as seen on prior centres.

qa_highlights.question: Is the drop in retention a sign of demand weakness, and will similar churn continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 74% was Q2-seasonal churn; mature committed occupancy is 92%, and most churned space is already re-let. Churn is expected to fall in Q3 and Q4, as in prior years.

qa_highlights.question: Is there supply risk from developer delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Supply is covered by a buffer of 0.7-0.8 million sq ft over the 2.5-3 million sq ft target, and management is working with institutional developers such as DLF, Hiranandani, Tata, Panchshil and Salarpuria.

qa_highlights.question: How is the 28-30% guidance built, given the existing base is at 92% committed occupancy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the base is almost fully sold, so growth depends on new centres that take about 12 months to ramp. Growth is expected to show mainly in Q3 or Q4, and the range is one management is confident about.

qa_highlights.question: Why did OCF/EBITDA dip, and what about VAS margins and pricing power?
qa_highlights.answer: The dip reflects INR 33 crores of security deposits paid to landlords. VAS is take-rate based with no direct cost, so it is margin accretive, but it is only in pilot stages and not in FY27 projections. Management said the nearest competitor prices 10-15% higher than Smartworks.

risks_watch: Occupancy may stay at 80-85% in the next three quarters as large new centres ramp, and it could drop further.
Revenue guidance depends on new-centre ramp-up and handover timing, with most of the uplift in Q3-Q4 FY27.
Capex of INR 550-600 crores is front-loaded; FCF is negative (INR -56 crores in Q1) and depends on OCF recovering after deposit payments.
IT/ITES share is falling, and management could not give a call-centre (AI-exposed) breakdown.
Retention of 74% in Q1 needs to recover in the seasonally stronger H2 to validate the 80-88% annual range management cited.
Revenue and EBITDA margin depend on keeping the 19-20% range while absorbing new cohorts.
Management corrected several numbers during the call (Singapore occupancy, seat count, IT/ITES share, retention), so the transcript figures should be checked against the presentation.

544447|2026-09.headline: Smartworks Q2 FY27 revenue rose 39% YoY to INR 591 crore; FY27 revenue growth guidance raised to 33-35% from 28-30%.
544447|2026-09.overview: Revenue from operations reached INR 591 crore, up 39% YoY and 8% QoQ, the sixth straight quarter of sequential growth since listing. Normalised EBITDA was INR 117 crore at a 19.8% margin (up 340 bps YoY), and normalised PAT was INR 43 crore (up 136%). Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 33-35% and kept the normalised EBITDA margin guidance at 19-20%, trending to the upper end. 544449|2026-03.headline: Anthem FY26 consolidated revenue Rs 2,124 crore (+18% incl. other income), with Q4 record revenue Rs 611 crore (+26% YoY) and Q4 EBITDA margin 48.1%.
544449|2026-03.overview: Anthem closed FY26 with its highest-ever quarterly revenue in Q4, up 26% YoY to Rs 611 crore, with CRDMO up 31% and specialty ingredients up 8%. FY26 EBITDA reached Rs 990 crore (43.4% margin, +31%) and PAT Rs 592 crore (+31%), though full-year revenue growth of about 15% fell short of the company's stated 20% aspiration. Management said destocking by customers is largely behind it and refused to give FY27 or FY28 guidance. Capex is shifting to Unit 4, with Phase 1 of about Rs 1,200 crore to finish by March 2028.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 352 crore (17%); Q4 Rs 98 crore, +8% YoY, the first revenue growth after flat first three quarters. Management aspires to around 20% growth; products include serratiopeptidase, vitamins, probiotics and enzymes, sold mainly to India and RoW markets.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 or FY28 guidance given; management aspires to around 20% growth in revenue, EBITDA and PAT, citing a 10-year revenue CAGR near 20%.
FY26 revenue growth was about 15% versus a 20% aspiration; management says EBITDA and PAT growth of 30%+ more than compensated.
EBITDA margin: asked whether 38-40% is a fair assumption, CFO said the company has delivered these levels and will continue to deliver, with operating leverage expected to hold margins steady.
Destocking is described as behind the company; management expects restocking to lift FY27 top and bottom line.
Biosimilar project expected to hit P&L next year (FY27) and would be classified under CRDMO.
Unit 3 expected to be EBITDA-positive this year; Unit 4 ready by next financial year per CEO closing remarks.
capex_capacity: Unit 4 is the largest project, with Phase 1 at about Rs 1,200 crore across FY27 and FY28, targeted for completion in the latter half of March 2028.
Phase 1 adds about 365 kilolitres custom synthesis (vs current 425 KL) and 100 KL fermentation (vs current 180 KL), roughly doubling custom synthesis and adding about 50% fermentation capacity.
Capex guidance: about Rs 700 crore in FY27, then about Rs 500 crore per year after that (including maintenance).
Unit 2 expanded from 246 KL to about 376 KL (50% addition); Unit 3 fully operational, and more Unit 2/3 expansion sits in CWIP in H1 FY27.
Unit 4 has two further phases after Phase 1; Phase 1 at least doubles capacity and Phase 2 could triple overall size.
Unit 3 added lab space to handle more projects; management says the company can handle 200 projects versus 100 today.
demand_pricing: Management said destocking happened in FY26 across many customers, and restocking is now under way.
Orders are coming in for both chemistry and biology, with growth in peptides and RNAi (oligonucleotide) work.
Four commercial molecules went live in FY26 (one with big pharma, three with emerging biotechs); they contribute about 8-9% of revenue now, with a 2-3 year ramp expected.

Commercial pipeline rose to 14 molecules; Phase 3 pipeline stands at 10 molecules, all from emerging biotechs (four added in FY26, non-lateral), spanning ADC, peptides, oligonucleotides and biotransformation.

Two new direct big pharma relationships added in FY26; more than 100 early-stage R&D projects. Biotech funding up about 50% YoY through April (per CFO); early-stage requests rising in number though smaller in size.
Management sees tariffs as no impact so far, since commercial big pharma products have separate arrangements with the US administration.

qa_highlights.question: How should FY27 growth for CRDMO research and manufacturing be framed, and are destocking issues resolved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aspires to about 20%+ growth as per track record but gave no FY27 guidance; it says destocking is largely behind and restocking should benefit FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is capacity a constraint for adding big pharma customers?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Unit 2 expansion (246 to about 376 KL) and Unit 3 give headroom until Unit 4 comes online; capacity is not a constraint now.

qa_highlights.question: Capex outlook for FY27 and the medium term?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about Rs 700 crore in FY27 and about Rs 500 crore thereafter, with Unit 4 Phase 1 at about Rs 1,200 crore over two years.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin improvement and EBITDA margin sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Backward integration into one intermediate was completed, improving material margins in Q3 and Q4 FY26; management expects 38-40% EBITDA margins to be sustained with operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Phase 3 pipeline composition?
qa_highlights.answer: All four Phase 3 additions were non-lateral, from the emerging biotech funnel; the basket of 10 spans ADC, peptides, oligos and biotransformation, with at least one molecule per modality.

qa_highlights.question: Contribution from the four newly commercial molecules?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO estimated about 8-9% of current revenue, with peak sales estimated four to five years after launch and a two-to-three-year ramp.

Q4 PAT includes a Labour Code-related exceptional credit of Rs 98 lakh.

544449|2026-06.headline: Anthem Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell to Rs 418 crore with 39.6% EBITDA margin; management guides to H2-weighted recovery, not a number.
544449|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was Rs 418 crore, with CRDMO at Rs 341 crore (81.5%) and Specialty Ingredients at Rs 78 crore (18.5%). EBITDA including other income was Rs 176 crore (39.6% margin), PAT Rs 120 crore (27.1% margin), and net cash stood at Rs 1,720 crore at June 30, 2026. Management attributed the soft quarter to customers deferring deliveries into Q2–Q4 rather than to demand weakness, and reiterated full-year growth in line with historical double-digit performance. Analysts pressed on the roughly 25% YoY decline in Q1; management pushed investors to judge the business on a YoY and full-year basis.

segments.name: CRDMO
segments.commentary: Rs 341 crore in Q1 FY27 (81.5% of revenue); management says order book is about 60% of full-year plan after replenishment, with deliveries deferred to Q2–Q4. Analyst cited roughly 25% YoY decline in Q1.

segments.name: Specialty Ingredients
segments.commentary: Rs 78 crore in Q1 FY27 (18.5% of revenue); India-focused B2B business with rolling forecasts revised every 3 to 6 months. Management cited raw material and supply chain pressure from the war and expects decent growth by year-end.

guidance_outlook: Management says Q1 FY27 is the softest quarter of the year and expects sequential growth from Q2 onward, with recovery in Q2, Q3 and Q4.

Full-year FY27 growth expected in line with historical performance (double-digit over the last 10 years, per CFO); no specific percentage guided. Analyst's 20% growth figure was not confirmed by the company.
EBITDA and PAT margins expected to be broadly intact for FY27; management sees no margin challenge this year given the order book.
FY27 capex target about Rs 700 crore; capex elevated in FY28 due to Unit 4, then declining.
Tax rate expected to normalise to about 25% to 25.5% for the full year as Neo Anthem moves toward breakeven and profitability.
Semaglutide API commercial supply to domestic players expected after CDSCO approval, guided as likely within a quarter or two and in any case this year.
capex_capacity: Unit 1 utilisation about 78% in Q1 FY27 (about 74% at FY26 end), custom synthesis.
Unit 2 utilisation about 50% in Q1 on expanded custom synthesis capacity (about 130 kilolitres added); fermentation about 50% on 140 kilolitres. Unit 2 averaged about 65% in FY26.
Unit 3 (Neo Anthem) utilisation about 30% to 35% in Q1 FY27, up from about 15% in FY26; new projects including peptide synthesis and oncology manufacturing being moved in.

Unit 4: Rs 1,200 crore Phase 1 capex on about 30 acres (half of land used in Phase 1), adding about 365 kilolitres custom synthesis and 100 kilolitres fermentation, plus food and nutra plant. Groundbreaking last year; civil work nearly done; equipment orders starting; capex split about 50:50 across FY27 and FY28; commissioning by end FY28.
Management expects all units to approach optimum utilisation within about two years.
demand_pricing: Added one new Big Pharma customer in the quarter; agreement not yet signed, expected to contribute in later quarters of FY27. Management describes it as multi-dimensional (R&D, new projects, supply diversification).

One large biotech customer was acquired by a Big Pharma; management says impact is not material for the rest of FY27 and no meaningful discussions with the acquirer yet. The affected contract is a late-Phase 3 development contract, not commercial.

Four new molecules commercialised by customers last year; sizeable supplies expected only after a couple of years of market penetration. About 14 commercial molecules and 10 late-phase molecules, with 100+ early-stage programmes; commercialisation of late-phase molecules 18 to 24 months away. Two late-phase programmes are ADC-related.
Q1 deferrals attributed to customers rerouting stock between geographies and approval delays for growing molecules; management says confirmed orders remain in place.
Semaglutide: sampled almost all large domestic players; sales not yet started, pending CDSCO approval. Regulatory work started for other markets but none targeted yet.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity utilisation at Units 1, 2 and Neo Anthem, and US FDA or EU inspection timing for Unit 3?
qa_highlights.answer: Unit 1 about 78%, Unit 2 about 50% (fermentation also about 50%), Unit 3 about 30% to 35%. Unit 3 growth is from new projects rather than shifting volume from existing units. Management did not give an inspection timeline in the answer.

qa_highlights.question: Visibility on the next quarter and the split of the remaining 40% of the year's business across CRDMO, R&D and Specialty Ingredients?
qa_highlights.answer: The 60% order book figure applies to the whole business. Specialty Ingredients is month-to-month with rolling forecasts; CRDMO orders are placed in advance due to raw material procurement and manufacturing lead times. The remaining volume is expected from new customers and volume increases from existing ones.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year CRDMO growth after a weak Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said growth prospects remain intact and in line with historical double-digit growth, with recovery expected in Q2 to Q4 and margins mostly intact. CEO asked investors to judge on a YoY basis and not to treat any single quarter as a benchmark.

qa_highlights.question: Semaglutide commercial supply timing and inbound interest from domestic peers facing scale-up issues?
qa_highlights.answer: No commercial supply yet; awaiting CDSCO approval, expected this year. Management said the company is ready to scale, has sampled most large players, and was not responding to a peer's scale-up problem.

qa_highlights.question: Unit 4 capex, timeline and FY27 capex total?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs 1,200 crore Phase 1 outlay, about 50:50 across FY27 and FY28, with commissioning by end FY28. FY27 capex target about Rs 700 crore; FY28 stays elevated before declining.

qa_highlights.question: Margin sustainability over 3 to 5 years, and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites a 60% order book and known cost base for FY27, and points to flow chemistry and biocatalysis as cost reducers. Material margin rose in Q1 despite lower revenue. Management expects some PAT dilution when new units start.

risks_watch: Lumpy CRDMO deliveries: Q1 soft due to customer deferrals; Q2 to Q4 must absorb the shortfall to hold full-year growth.
Semaglutide CDSCO approval timing; delay would push back the GLP-1 revenue ramp.

Unit 4 execution (Rs 1,200 crore, commissioning end FY28) and FY28 capex; PAT dilution as new units start.
Specialty Ingredients under raw material and supply pressure; management expects growth by year-end but gave no figure.
Neo Anthem (Unit 3) turning breakeven this year is needed to support the 25% tax rate assumption.

544449|2026-09.headline: Anthem Biosciences Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose to INR594 crore with a 50.6% EBITDA margin; H1 revenue INR1,012 crore and net cash INR1,534 crore.
544449|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue from operations was INR594 crore, with CRDMO at INR509 crore and Specialty Ingredients at INR85 crore. EBITDA was INR330 crore (50.6% margin, including INR59 crore other income) and PAT was INR211 crore (32.04% margin). Management attributed the margin uptick to operating leverage on a sharp revenue ramp after a weak Q1, with costs broadly flat. H1 FY27 revenue was INR1,012 crore, and an analyst noted an implied 7% H1 decline versus the prior year, which management did not dispute but addressed through a catch-up narrative for Q3 and Q4.

financial_highlights.change: Approx. 8% YoY as cited by an analyst; not confirmed by management
Other income INR59 crore vs INR48 crore in Q2 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR1,012 crore; CRDMO INR850 crore, Specialty Ingredients INR162 crore
financial_highlights.change: Analyst cited about 7% H1 de-growth; management did not dispute
Other income INR84 crore vs INR70 crore in H1 FY26

segments.name: CRDMO
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR509 crore; H1 FY27 INR850 crore. Around 85% of business is CDMO, of which about 65% is commercial manufacturing of approved molecules and the remaining about 20% is R&D and development supplies.

segments.name: Specialty Ingredients
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR85 crore; H1 FY27 INR162 crore. Management targets at least 20% of sales, and said the segment tends to be muted when CRDMO sales are strong.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to give a full-year revenue number but targets double-digit revenue growth, in line with historical delivery.

Management said it is confident of EBITDA and PAT growth, and expects FY26-level EBITDA margins (about 43% including other income) to be sustainable; the Q2 margin of about 50% was described as higher than this.
Catch-up expected in Q3 and Q4 to offset a weak Q1 FY27.
Specialty Ingredients expected at around 20% of sales by year end.
Capex guidance of about INR1,200 crore over two years for Unit 4 Phase 1 reaffirmed; Phase 2 is of similar size, with guidance to follow board approval.
Currency assumed range-bound (INR94.5 to INR96.5 per USD in the quarter), so no significant currency tailwind is assumed.
capex_capacity: Unit 4 is a large-scale facility on 30 acres; Phase 1 is equivalent to Units 1, 2 and 3 combined, with commissioning expected around March 2028.
Of the Phase 1 capex, management expects at least 30-35% in biology (fermentation/biologics) and the rest in chemistry.
Asset turns are currently about 1.2x-1.3x against an aspirational 1.5x; utilisation is below optimum and expected to improve over the next year.
Investments are underway in biologics drug product (fill-finish), oligonucleotides (Unit 4), an oncology facility expansion and cybersecurity.
demand_pricing: Portfolio: 15 commercial molecules (up from 14) and 9 late-stage molecules (down from 10); one molecule moved to commercial in Q2 on approval, from an emerging biotech portfolio in chronic care.

Geography: about 84% of revenue is international and about 16% India. Within international, US is about 22-24%, Europe about 60%, and rest of world 1-2%; customers are large pharma and the company says this split reflects where drug product is made.
Concentration: top five customers about 50% of business and top 10 about 80%.
Procurement: about 75-78% domestic on H1 basis, China about 20-21%, down from earlier reliance on a Chinese vendor for one product.

Five newly commercial molecules (last 18 months) split equally between APIs and advanced intermediates; management says the company is currently sole supplier, with second-source risk expected after acquisitions.
Management says it is seeing more RFPs and RFQs over the last quarter, though biotech funding revival is mixed given geopolitical uncertainty.
Company works with 8-9 large pharma customers, and two came in directly rather than via acquisition.
Peak sales estimates of the new molecules range from $1bn to $5bn, around $10bn aggregate, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin rose about 3%; is this due to lower China reliance?
qa_highlights.answer: Gawir Baig said the mix reflects reduced China sourcing, in-house manufacturing and product/customer mix differences, with no single driver isolated.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainability of the 50% EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 was driven by operating leverage on higher revenue with flat costs; FY26-level margins (about 43%) are sustainable, and management avoided committing to 50%.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year FY27 growth construct?
qa_highlights.answer: No full-year number given; management targets double-digit growth and expects catch-up in Q3 and Q4 after a low Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Timing of late-stage molecules moving to commercial?
qa_highlights.answer: Outcomes are expected over the next 18-24 months, with a few possibly in FY27, dependent on Phase III results; management said timing is not controllable.

qa_highlights.question: Prospects of the newly commercial molecule in the portfolio?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose indication details or peak sales, citing contract confidentiality; it described the indication as chronic care.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue per molecule for new vs older products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said on average per-molecule revenue should be similar to the existing base, with some large-indication molecules expected to exceed that; approvals for additional indications are expected in the next two quarters for some molecules.

qa_highlights.question: Why limited lateral (second-source) contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said customers have many qualified suppliers and switching is slow; the company is receiving samples and qualification work, which it sees as a positive.

risks_watch: Lumpiness of CRDMO project revenue: H1 revenue was down about 7% YoY per an analyst, with Q1 weak and reliance on Q3/Q4 catch-up.
Customer concentration: top 10 customers about 80% of business.
Patent expiries: first key patent expiry in 2032, with some extending to 2037-2040.
Late-stage pipeline (9 molecules) binary Phase III outcomes; 18-24 month commercialisation window.
Capex execution on Unit 4 (about INR1,200 crore Phase 1, commissioning around March 2028) and asset turn improvement from 1.2-1.3x toward 1.5x.
Residual China dependence (about 20-21% of procurement) and development of domestic captive vendors.
Biotech funding environment described as mixed amid geopolitical uncertainty.
544449|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on margins and capex, with management repeatedly saying Q2 margins are sustainable. Cautious and at times evasive on forward numbers: it declined to give full-year revenue guidance, peak sales, molecule details, or Phase 2 capex, and framed timelines as dependent on customers and trial outcomes.
key_quotes: We have further solidified our industry -leading margins and are well -positioned to sustain this performance for the whole year.
Our customers do depend on us to pro vide a very competitive cost of goods. That's only possible if we are backward integrated.
So, historically, what we have delivered in the past, we will be able to deliver on those numbers.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin was 50.6% on operating leverage with flat costs, but management guides FY26-level margins of about 43% as sustainable and avoided committing to 50%, so margins likely normalise toward 43%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Unit 4 Phase 1 (INR1,200 crore, 30 acres, equal to Units 1-3 combined) is under construction with commissioning around March 2028, which falls outside the 2-4 quarter window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets double-digit full-year CRDMO growth with a Q3/Q4 catch-up, but H1 revenue of INR1,012 crore implied about a 7% decline and no full-year number was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Phase 2 is of similar size (about INR1,200 crore) with guidance to follow board approval, and asset turns of 1.2-1.3x versus a 1.5x target with utilisation below optimum make a Phase 2 announcement possible but not dated.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No full-year revenue number was given, H1 was down about 7% YoY, and the currency is assumed range-bound with no tailwind, so an upgrade is not supported.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 was weak and H2 relies on a catch-up, with lumpy CRDMO project revenue, top-10 customers at about 80% of business and Phase III binary outcomes.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: 15 commercial molecules and 9 late-stage molecules, with a few late-stage outcomes possibly in FY27 dependent on Phase III, and approvals for additional indications expected in the next two quarters.

rows.label: Increased RFP/RFQ flow
rows.why: Management sees more RFPs and RFQs over the last quarter, and two of 8-9 large pharma customers came in directly, but biotech funding is mixed.

rows.label: Lower China sourcing
rows.why: China procurement fell to about 20-21% from earlier reliance on one Chinese vendor, with domestic at about 75-78%, which supported the Q2 gross margin rise of about 3%.

rows.label: Second-source qualification
rows.why: Five newly commercial molecules are currently single-sourced, with second-source risk expected after acquisitions, and samples and qualification work are under way.

tone.note: Management was confident on Q2 margins, capex and EBITDA/PAT growth, but cautious and evasive on full-year revenue, peak sales and Phase 2 capex; analysts pushed on the implied ~7% H1 decline and the sustainability of the 50% margin.

544450|2026-03.headline: Chembond Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue hit a record Rs 101.4 crore, but management flagged a ~3% margin hit from war-driven input cost inflation.
544450|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated revenue of Rs 326.15 crore (up 12%), EBITDA of Rs 51 crore (up 7%) and PBT of Rs 45 crore (up 7%), with H2 revenue of Rs 188 crore, up 35% over H1. Q4 FY26 revenue of Rs 101.4 crore and EBITDA of Rs 15.7 crore were the highest of the last nine quarters. Management said margins are under pressure from metal-linked raw material costs that rose after the war declaration, with force majeure invoked and public-sector customers resisting price changes. The call was held after the demerger, which moved the water and construction businesses into the new listed entity.

financial_highlights.change: Highest of last nine quarters; management said above Q4 FY25 and Q4 FY24

financial_highlights.value: Rs 46.3 crore (presentation also cites Rs 51 crore), 14% of sales
financial_highlights.change: Rs 51 crore is +7% YoY per management

segments.name: Water technologies
segments.commentary: About 87% of FY26 revenue and the fastest-growing unit; H2 revenue Rs 162 crore, up 36% over H1, with volume of 4,813 MT vs 3,205 MT... (H1 volume stated as 9,905 MT in transcript, which conflicts with H2 4,813 MT; not reconciled on call). Record single-month revenue of about Rs 32 crore in March.

segments.name: Construction chemicals
segments.commentary: About 7% of revenue; H2 revenue Rs 13 crore vs H1 Rs 11 crore (+18-20%), H2 volume 2,590 MT (+30%). Management claimed PBT margin of about 20%; DSO about 88 days at 31 March 2026.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: About 6% of revenue; H2 revenue Rs 12.5 crore vs H1 Rs 9 crore (+40%), H2 volume 1,049 MT vs 594 MT in H1; DSO about 80 days.

segments.name: Cleaning and hygiene (JV with Calvatis)
segments.commentary: About 1% of revenue; H2 growth of 15%. Management described it as subpar for seven years, with early traction from integration into water channel.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 volume growth expected at about 15-20% in construction chemicals and about 10% in water chemicals.
Management said next four quarters at Rs 100 crore-plus are possible, subject to Q1 seasonality, and sequential quarters should improve on the prior year.
Around 3% margin impact seen in the immediate month from input cost inflation; a couple of quarters expected to pass costs through, with new contracts bid at higher prices.
Rs 1,000 crore revenue within four years described as an aspiration, not a commitment.
Water business entering FY27 with a strong chemicals and equipment order book; chemical contracts run to around mid-year, and FY27 budget already reflects the volume trend.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex of about Rs 20-21 crore, mainly PPE transferred on the demerger and office renovation (management).
About Rs 65 crore of cash on books; management said some would go to network growth and geographic expansion, with no new plant planned.
Construction chemicals: de-bottlenecking of production lines; repair mortars outsourced to contract manufacturers.
Limited surplus water chemical inventory was rationed across customers during the force majeure period; volumes were kept below potential.
demand_pricing: Growth was mainly volume-driven, with new customer acquisition as the main driver; price growth contributed very little in FY26.
Construction chemicals realisation fell to about Rs 51,274/MT in H2 from about Rs 55,584/MT in H1, which management attributed to product mix (admixtures vs sealants).
Distribution realisation fell to about Rs 1.19 lakh/MT in H2 from about Rs 1.51 lakh/MT in H1, attributed to product mix.

Water business: about 70% private sector and 28-30% public sector (PSUs such as IOCL, HPCL, BPCL, NTPC, NPCIL). Private customers granted temporary price increases of 5-12% for about three months; public-sector customers refused to amend terms.
Input costs: metal-linked raw materials (zinc, molybdenum) rose from late February/March; management said 15 A-group items are up more than 120%.
Competitors named: Ecolab, Nalco, Solenis, Suez/Veolia, Ion Exchange, Thermax; Vasu Chemicals now owned by Dorf Ketal.
Largest customer under 5-6% of revenue; Nigeria export business exited after the customer refused LC terms.

qa_highlights.question: Can the Rs 100 crore-plus quarterly run-rate continue for the next four quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes is possible, with Q1 seasonally slower than Q4, but quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year comparisons should improve.

qa_highlights.question: How much margin pressure from input costs, and can margins return to last year's levels?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3% margin impact in the immediate month; cost pass-through takes a couple of quarters, and new contracts are being priced at higher baselines. Chemical prices have softened only slightly.

qa_highlights.question: Why is other income negative this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Fair-value adjustment on investments: net gain was lower than in the prior quarter and the loss on fair value of investments was higher.

qa_highlights.question: Why are construction and distribution realisations lower in H2 than H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Product mix; admixtures lower realisation, sealants higher. Distribution is purely trading, so mix depends on customer demand.

qa_highlights.question: Can water business margins reach construction-level PBT of about 20%, and why are they lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said peer margins are at par, within about 0.5 percentage points; employee cost is about 18% of revenue in water versus 14% in other businesses.

qa_highlights.question: What is the public/private split in water and how is force majeure being handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Public sector is about 28-30% and private about 70%. Private customers accepted temporary increases; public-sector customers refused, and the company is preparing contingency actions if disruption extends beyond another month.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation in metal-linked raw materials; about 3% immediate margin impact and pass-through lag of a couple of quarters.
Public-sector water customers (28-30% of water revenue) refusing price amendments; force majeure invoked and contingency plans in place if disruption extends beyond about one month.
Working capital: DSO of about 88 days in construction and about 80 days in distribution.
Construction and distribution realisation decline from product mix; water realisation not disclosed on the call.
FY26 capex of about Rs 20-21 crore was largely demerger-related; further capex and cash deployment plans still unclear.
Data inconsistency: H2 water volume of 4,813 MT compared with 9,905 MT in H1 needs reconciliation; FY26 EBITDA quoted as both Rs 46.3 crore and Rs 51 crore.
544450|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on revenue momentum and the order book, but cautious on margins; management repeatedly said near-term profitability is a challenge tied to the war-driven cost spike. Evasive on budgets and on the public-sector price question.
key_quotes: Unfortunately, this story has changed post this war, having started this financial year.
So it's a synergy with our water business that we are now exploiting more efficiently.
So the track remains positive and on the positive growth for all quarters.
Yes, it's possible, but some seasonality comes into this business.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management flagged a ~3% immediate margin hit from metal-linked input costs (zinc, molybdenum; 15 A-group items up more than 120%), with pass-through taking a couple of quarters and public-sector customers (28-30% of water revenue) refusing price changes.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant planned; FY26 capex was about Rs 20-21 crore, mostly demerger-transferred PPE and office renovation, and construction chemicals relies on de-bottlenecking and outsourced repair mortars.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guided Q1 FY27 volume growth of 15-20% in construction chemicals and about 10% in water chemicals, backed by a strong water order book and new customer acquisition, though surplus inventory was rationed during force majeure.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed and no new plant is planned, but about Rs 65 crore of cash on books is earmarked partly for network growth and geographic expansion, with deployment plans still unclear.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said Rs 100 crore-plus quarterly revenue is possible for the next four quarters, with sequential and YoY comparisons improving, but this is conditional on Q1 seasonality and the water order book.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The war-driven ~3% margin hit may persist if public-sector price refusals extend beyond about one month, and management is preparing contingency actions for that scenario.

rows.label: Cost pass-through via higher-priced new contracts
rows.why: Private water customers accepted temporary 5-12% increases for about three months, and new contracts are being bid at higher prices, though pass-through takes a couple of quarters.

rows.label: Receivable days elevated
rows.why: DSO was about 88 days in construction and about 80 days in distribution at 31 March 2026, and no improvement plan was discussed.

rows.label: Network and geographic expansion
rows.why: Management said part of the Rs 65 crore cash balance would go to network growth and geographic expansion, but Nigeria export was exited after the customer refused LC terms.

tone.note: Management was confident on record revenue, the water order book and volume growth, but cautious on margins from the war-driven input cost spike; analysts pushed on margin recovery, the public-sector price refusals and the Rs 100 crore quarterly run-rate.

544450|2026-09.headline: Chembond H1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 32% to Rs 182.25 crore, but PBT was flat at Rs 19.79 crore as material cost rose to 56% of sales.
544450|2026-09.overview: Consolidated H1 FY27 revenue was Rs 182.25 crore, up 32% YoY, with Q2 revenue at Rs 95.8 crore (up 11% QoQ and 31% YoY). Operating EBITDA was Rs 22.55 crore (12% of sales vs 16% a year ago) and PBT was Rs 19.79 crore (11% of sales vs 14%), so absolute profit was flat despite higher volumes. Management attributed the squeeze to raw material inflation linked to the Iran war, solvent and China-sourced component costs, and a lag in passing price increases to customers. Q2 EBITDA was Rs 8.4 crore versus Rs 14 crore in Q1, and management said price increases are still being requested and no normalisation timeline can be given.

segments.name: Water technologies
segments.commentary: Revenue up 28% YoY on order book growth; about 82% of group revenue and the main source of margin erosion. Volume rose to 13,343 MT from 9,268 MT.

segments.name: Construction chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue up 30% YoY, about 8% of group revenue. Volume fell to 1,330 MT from 1,988 MT on product mix (admixtures run-off replaced by sealants); price increases partly offset.

segments.name: Distribution (trading)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 86% YoY, about 9% of group revenue; volume rose to 1,367 MT from 690 MT. Margin erosion is not concentrated here per management.

segments.name: Cleaning and hygiene (JV with Calvatis)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 59% YoY; about 1% of group revenue.

guidance_outlook: No guidance on margin recovery timing; management could not give assurance on when costs normalise, hoping for stability by end of FY27.
If the Iran war effects ease and crude and logistics return to pre-war levels, management expects cost increases to be absorbed in one or two quarters.
Management expects H2 to be stronger than H1, citing a strong order book and Q4 as a historically high-sales quarter.
Raw material cost deflation would give a couple of quarters of tailwind; new higher-priced business acquired in recent months should support margins.
Management said it would consider buybacks or higher payout if cash is not needed; no decision announced.

Management did not commit to returning to the 15-15.5% EBITDA margin cited by an analyst; said the Rs 1,000 crore three-year revenue aspiration is organic plus smaller businesses plus inorganic options.
capex_capacity: Management said capacity is not a constraint: plants are modular and capacity can be added in about two months without disturbing operations.
A production line at the Gujarat plant was repurposed to make additional sealants.
Equipment pipeline (water business) is about Rs 15-20 crore for FY27.
Three manufacturing sites; head office and R&D in Navi Mumbai.
Management said its focus is on profitability and cash flow management rather than capex.
demand_pricing: Management said all end-industries grew in volume, including refining, petchem, chemicals, agrochemicals, fertiliser, power, steel and cement.
Data centres are a growing customer: the top telecom company's data centres are served, plus NTT, Yotta and others, mainly via automated online monitoring plus makeup chemicals.
New-age industries (solar, copper, data centres) are about 7-8% of water revenue, expected to reach 12-15% over three years if the project pipeline executes.
About 80% of business revenue comes from technical-service-driven contracts, 15-16% from pure product sales, and the rest is hybrid.
About 25-30% of water sales are from PSU fixed-price contracts; private sector customers have been passing on part of increases.

Competition: a competitor was acquired by a larger process chemicals company, which management expects to be positive for Chembond over the next few quarters. Management also said customer attrition is very low and some lost accounts have returned at better prices.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins return to 15-15.5% EBITDA and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Q1 solvent-driven and Q2 China-import component cost increases, with Q3 similar to Q2. It could not give visibility on normalisation, but hopes costs ease by end of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is margin erosion across segments or concentrated in distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Erosion is across segments, mainly water; distribution is only about 8-9% of revenue. Management said margins at Q1 levels would have added about Rs 20 crore to profit (gross profit basis, Q2 at Q1 levels).

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise from Rs 11 crore to Rs 16.5 crore QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said technical service labour costs, freight and travel rose as more revenue came from technical service orders.

qa_highlights.question: What is the construction chemicals product mix change?
qa_highlights.answer: Admixture projects ended and were replaced by sealants; the Gujarat line was repurposed for sealants. Management described the chemical sealant as a benchmark product in the industry.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the tax rate reach about 35% in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to capital gains on redemption of investments; CFO was to explain further but no detailed figure was given in the transcript.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for margins and pricing with customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Public sector contracts are fixed price and hard to revise; private sector clients pass on part of the increases. New bids reflect current material costs. Management said margin improvement depends on raw material prices falling.

risks_watch: Raw material cost volatility (solvents, China-sourced components, freight), with price increases lagging and sales-team fatigue.
Q3 FY27 margins: management said Q3 is tracking the same as Q2.
PSU fixed-price contracts (25-30% of water sales) limit pass-through.
Effective tax rate of about 35% in H1 FY27, attributed to capital gains on investment redemptions.
Construction chemicals volume decline (1,988 MT to 1,330 MT) despite revenue growth.
Whether the Rs 1,000 crore three-year revenue aspiration and new-age industry share targets are delivered.
Customer concentration was not disclosed.
544450|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on volume growth, order book and customer stickiness, but cautious and candid on margins: management repeatedly declined to give timelines for cost normalisation and said profitability has not met its own expectations.
key_quotes: So revenues grew on the back partially due to price increases, but the major component was the volume growth.
We were just doing a quick calculation that had margins even remained at Q1 levels, our profit would have been higher by about Rs. 20 crores.
On profitability management, we've tried, but due to some reasons beyond our control, we have not been able to deliver to our own expectations, and I'm sure your expectations too.

financial_highlights.change: down from Rs 14 crore in Q1
down from Rs 12.8 crore in Q1

financial_highlights.value: 20% of sales in H1 FY26 vs 17% in H1 FY27

rows.why: Q2 EBITDA fell to Rs 8.4 crore from Rs 14 crore in Q1 and H1 EBITDA margin is 12% vs 16% a year ago, with material cost at 56% of sales vs 46%; Q3 is tracking the same as Q2 and management gave no normalisation timeline, only hope for stability by end FY27.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management says capacity is not a constraint and capacity can be added in about two months, with equipment pipeline of only Rs 15-20 crore for FY27 and focus shifted to profitability and cash flow rather than capex; no new plant was announced.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Water volume rose to 13,343 MT from 9,268 MT, distribution volume doubled to 1,367 MT from 690 MT, management expects H2 stronger than H1 on a strong order book and all end-industries grew in volume.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said its focus is on profitability and cash flow rather than capex, with only a Rs 15-20 crore equipment pipeline for FY27 and capacity addable in about two months, and utilisation was not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management expects H2 to beat H1 with Q4 a historically high sales and profit quarter, but margin recovery has no committed timeline and H1 PBT was only Rs 19.79 crore (11% of sales).

rows.why: Gujarat line was already repurposed to make additional sealants and new-age industry (solar, copper, data centres) is 7-8% of water revenue targeted at 12-15% over three years, but no specific launch date was given.

rows.why: Management says price increases are still being requested, private clients are passing on part of the increases, and management expects cost increases to be absorbed in one or two quarters only if Iran war effects ease, which it cannot assure.

rows.label: Competitor acquisition could benefit Chembond
rows.why: A competitor was acquired by a larger process chemicals company, which management expects to be positive for Chembond, and lost accounts have returned at better prices, though customer concentration was not disclosed.

rows.label: Raw material deflation tailwind
rows.when: FY28 if crude and logistics normalise
rows.why: Management expects a couple of quarters of tailwind if raw material costs deflate, and Q1 cost levels would have added about Rs 20 crore to gross profit, but no timeline was committed.

tone.note: Management was confident on volume growth, order book and customer stickiness but candid and cautious on margins, declining to give normalisation timelines or the 15-15.5% EBITDA margin; analysts pushed on margin recovery timing and whether erosion was concentrated in distribution.

544452|2026-03.headline: Swastika Castal FY26 total income rose 19.50% to INR36.19 crore, EBITDA INR6.22 crore, PAT INR3.28 crore; operating cash flow turned negative on deliberate working capital build.
544452|2026-03.overview: First earnings call since BSE SME listing, covering H2 and full-year FY26. Management attributed growth mainly to volume rather than price, with pricing impact described as very limited. Operating cash flow turned negative, which management said was a deliberate choice: advance payments to vendors, locked raw material pricing, and higher strategic inventory ahead of commissioning of expansion machinery in March 2026. Management expects FY27 to be a full year of enhanced capacity and says growth should be stronger than FY26, but declined to give a numeric guidance.

financial_highlights.metric: Revenue growth (as cited by analyst on call)
financial_highlights.change: YoY, analyst figure, not confirmed by management
Driven by higher working capital; amount not disclosed on call

segments.name: Power transmission and electrical equipment
segments.commentary: Management said power is the largest end-market for the company and has strong potential; named customers include Hitachi, ABB, Siemens, GE and Toshiba.

segments.name: Other industrial end-markets
segments.commentary: Company also serves infra/power capital equipment, railways, oil and gas, and fire-fighting equipment; railways is being expanded and government GeM tenders for defence components have recently been pursued.

guidance_outlook: No numeric FY27 revenue guidance; management said FY27 has potential for stronger growth than FY26.
FY27 will be the first full year with the benefit of enhanced capacity from the expansion.
Management expects some benefits from the expansion in the near term and a larger financial impact in the medium term.
Margins expected to be sustainable and to improve with scale, operating leverage, fixed-cost absorption and productivity gains; raw material and market conditions noted as influences.
Expects working capital and cash conversion to improve as supply chain stabilises and customer collections normalise, which management said happened in April and May 2026.
capex_capacity: Expansion capex was completed and all machinery was commissioned in March 2026, per management.
Management said the company held higher inventory to feed the newly commissioned machines.
Management cited an order book and improved capacity as drivers of higher volumes, but did not quantify capacity or utilisation.
Capex for the year was described as strategic, though the amount was not disclosed on the call.
demand_pricing: Volume, not price, drove FY26 revenue growth; management said pricing impact was very limited.
Management said current customers are booked for at least the next five years, per what he was told by them.
Two new export customers added in FY26: QAG (Australia-based multinational) and Trench (Europe). Also won orders from another Hitachi factory where the company had not previously supplied.
Export presence cited in Europe, Mexico and the US.
Raw material and fuel costs are passed through to customers monthly under price variation clauses with most customers.
