qa_highlights.question: What is driving the rise in one-time VAS revenue, and how will VAS mix evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said one-time items are upfront sales of IT products, design-and-build and furniture, and are hard to predict; VAS share is expected to rise from 15% to 17-18%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is capex per sq ft rising, and what was the IPO fund reallocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said material costs rose 5-7% due to the war, taking capex to INR 16.5 per sq ft from INR 15.5, absorbed by the company. The IPO reallocation moved INR 187 crore of capex to design-and-build, security deposits, solar and adjacent investments.

qa_highlights.question: Why not grow faster given available cash and about 50% headroom in area under management?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prioritises sustainable growth and micro-market defensibility, avoids overbuilding, and values landlord relationships; it said it is trying to push growth faster within those limits.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company disclose quarterly rent-paying area additions in advance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed to consider disclosing expected quarterly rent-paying area; it said it adds about 1-1.5 lakh sq ft per month of RPA, with about 1-1.25 lakh sq ft per month of rent-yielding area.

risks_watch: Quarterly occupancy volatility from large deliveries (Q4 end-March occupancy 81% vs 84% annual average); ramp-up takes 9-12 months to reach 90%.
Capex per sq ft rising (INR 15.5 to 16.5), with war-linked material inflation; management is absorbing it.
Dependence on one-time VAS sales, which management cannot predict; VAS margins of 10-15% are below space EBITDA.
Tier-2 expansion still early; management calls it a 10-year story with supply and landlord-maturity issues.
Data-centre and power-intensive client demand requires further solar and power additions.
Commitment to 1.5-2 million sq ft annual additions and 25-30% growth depends on supply pick-up and demand continuity.

Institutional share of portfolio rose from 16% to 18%. Tier-2 described as a 10-year story; Coimbatore cited as a promising city. Management described the rental inflation of 4-5% in key micro-markets as sustainable.

544454|2026-06.headline: Indiqube Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR428 crore (+37% YoY) and PAT rose 91% to INR35 crore, with PAT margin at 8%.
544454|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue of INR428 crore (+37% YoY), EBITDA of INR87 crore (+34%), EBIT of INR55 crore (+59%) and PAT of INR35 crore (+91%). Margins expanded, with EBIT margin at 13% (11% a year ago) and PAT margin at 8% (6%). Rent-paying area was flat QoQ, which management attributed to the timing of building handovers, with about 2 million sq ft of annual additions still guided. Q&A centred on VAS revenue (INR39 crore one-time in the quarter), solar capex, a large new Noida centre, and occupancy and margin ranges. Management declined to give quarterly OCF or capex figures ahead of the H1 audit.

segments.commentary: GCCs ~52-53% of revenue, startups and unicorns ~23%, Indian enterprises ~28% (of which GCCs ~10-12%). Multi-center clients ~41% of revenue; top five clients 12% of revenue; 855 clients as of June 2026.

segments.name: VAS (DesignQube, IndiCare, Eco)
segments.commentary: VAS is ~17% of revenue and management expects it to rise by about 2-4 percentage points. VAS EBIT margin is guided at ~15% for the next one to two years, as growth takes priority over margin.

segments.name: Solar / sustainability
segments.commentary: About 30 MW of solar capacity is operational. Plan to add 25-30 MW this year at INR100-120 crore capex; solar IRR stated at 18-22%.

Corporate occupancy guided at 80-85% (stated later as 82-86%); mature centres (over 12 months) at 85-90% (stated as 86-90%/88-90%).

New Noida centre is a large single building; live by mid-2027 (Q2/Q3 FY28).
demand_pricing: Institutional supply share rose to ~20% of portfolio from ~12% a couple of years ago; institutional buildings carry higher rents and CAM costs but management says margins are consistent across supply types.
Tier-2 centres: real estate cost INR50-70 per sq ft; seat pricing INR6,500-7,500 per seat; unit economics said to be similar to Tier-1.
Bangalore is ~60-64% of area; Chennai ~10%. Management expects Bangalore share to fall as NCR, Hyderabad, Mumbai and West India grow.

Tech parks are ~20% of portfolio. North Bangalore exposure is under 0.5 million sq ft of ~6.5 million sq ft in Bangalore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there no QoQ rise in rent-paying area despite 2 million sq ft annual guidance, and is supply slowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said additions are lumpy and tracked annually; H2 FY26 added ~1.14 million sq ft. No slowdown is seen, and ~3.9 million sq ft of signed headroom is available.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the INR39 crore one-time VAS revenue and how sustainable is it?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue came across DesignQube, IndiCare and Eco. Management said it is non-recurring in quarters but will keep recurring over time, with VAS share rising 2-4 percentage points.

qa_highlights.question: How much solar capex is planned and what IRR is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Plan of 25-30 MW more at INR100-120 crore; solar IRR 18-22%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the large Noida centre and is it demand-backed?
qa_highlights.answer: Live by mid-2027 (Q2/Q3 FY28). Management said it was largely proactive supply, not pre-leased, based on NCR micro-market research.

qa_highlights.question: Will new centres dilute margins given slow break-even?
qa_highlights.answer: Operational break-even takes 5-6 months at 52-57% occupancy and steady state ~12 months, so no margin pressure expected. The 36 months referred to full capex recovery.

qa_highlights.question: What margin will VAS deliver and will it drive group margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: VAS margin ~15% for the next one to two years; management prioritises scale. Group-level margins are expected to stay within the stated ranges.

544454|2026-09.headline: IndiQube Q2 FY27 revenue rose 34% YoY to INR475 crore and PAT grew 63% to INR57 crore, with VAS at 17% of operating revenue.

H1 revenue was INR904 crore (up 35%) and H1 PAT INR92 crore (up 66%). Steady-state occupancy improved to 91% from 89%, and VAS revenue reached INR154 crore in H1 (up 74%). Management guided to FY27 EBITDA margin of 19-21% (INR380-400 crore) and about 2 million sq ft of rent-paying area additions this year, while introducing new initiatives: a co-investment land pilot (SaiEdge, about INR35 crore), solar expansion, and a retail bank-branch fit-out business.

segments.commentary: H1 VAS revenue INR154 crore, up 74% YoY, about 17% of operating revenue. Management says VAS margin improved to about 20% from 15% and expects a range of about 18-20% going forward.

segments.commentary: About 30 MW operational capacity with another 30 MW expected within a year; about INR15 crore revenue in H1 against about INR46 crore invested. Payback about 3 years; planned about INR100 crore capex per year in Karnataka, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu.

segments.commentary: Early pilot with a large gold bank for about 30 branches; banks cited as 500-1,000 branch rollouts a year. Management described it as early, with capex models of INR1,400-1,800 per sq ft.

Solar capex about INR100 crore per year over the next two years across Karnataka, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of the Q2 margin uptick and whether the 20% VAS margin is a floor.
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the uptick to occupancy gain (89% to 91%, about 40% of growth), finance cost reduction of 1% (about 25%), VAS margin improvement and operating leverage from a 1% reduction in salary and other costs. VAS margin was not set as a floor; it is expected at about 18-20% as VAS is used as a foot-in-the-door.

544455|2026-03.headline: GNG Electronics Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 43% YoY to INR651.7 crore, with PAT nearly tripling to INR42.1 crore and PAT margin at 6.5%.

For FY26, revenue grew 34% to INR1,891 crore, PAT rose 91% to INR132 crore and PAT margin reached 7%. Net debt fell to about INR300 crore at March-end from INR466 crore in December, while inventory rose to about INR743 crore and debtor days moved up to about 40. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of around 25% and PAT margin expansion of at least 50 bps.

544455|2026-09.headline: GNG Electronics Q2 FY27 revenue rose 42% YoY to INR624.8 crore with gross margin up 515 bps to 25.1%; FY27 top-line guidance raised to 40%.

544458|2026-09.headline: Shree Refrigerations H1 FY27 revenue rose about 84-85% YoY to roughly INR 100 crore, with EBITDA margin up to 13.5% from 11%; FY27 margin guided at about 22%.
544458|2026-09.overview: H1 FY27 revenue was roughly INR 100 crore, up about 84-85% YoY, and EBITDA margin improved to 13.5% from 11% despite commodity inflation. Management reiterated 40% revenue CAGR and about 22% annual EBITDA margin guidance, while H1 margins remain skewed low versus H2. Order book stood at about INR 198.6-200 crore at September, down from INR 270 crore at the start of the year, and operating cash flow was negative about INR 42 crore in H1. Management said the data centre opportunity is excluded from guidance and is expected to take 6-12 months to gain traction.

financial_highlights.change: Up about 84-85% YoY vs H1 FY26
Down from INR 270 crore at start of year
Up from INR 105 crore; about 250 days
Up from about 370 days after IPO-era improvement

segments.name: Refrigeration vertical (HVAC, AC plant, Ref plant)
segments.commentary: Management reports a single refrigeration vertical with no separate product segments; HVAC is a larger share than AC plant, and Ref plant is a very small share. Retrofit is the major business line, with defence spares a large component, alongside installation, commissioning and service.

segments.name: Non-defence / industrial
segments.commentary: Industrial chillers and test equipment are described as negligible today. A new wholly owned subsidiary for sub-zero chillers (Aquilon) targets chemical, food and pharma, with commercial operations expected from next financial year.

segments.name: Data centre (oil-free / magnetic-bearing chillers)
segments.commentary: No data centre orders yet; the Danfoss Turbocor-based offering is sourced from an Australian partner. Management expects traction in 6-12 months and excludes data centre revenue from FY27 and FY28 projections.

guidance_outlook: Revenue to grow at about 40% CAGR; management reaffirmed this for FY27 and beyond, noting the guidance excludes data centre revenue.
EBITDA margin about 22% at annual level for FY27; H1 at 13.5% implies a steep H2 ramp, which management attributes to higher H2 volumes and product mix.
Working capital days expected to fall to about 350 days (CEO) and receivable days to about 200 days (CFO) over time.
Operating cash flow expected to turn positive by year-end FY27.
Order book expected to be healthy by year-end; management said orders will come in continuously rather than concentrated in Aug-Sep as last year.
Subsidy for the Karad unit 2 facility (Maharashtra D-class area) is not in projections and could add to margin.
capex_capacity: Unit 2 (Karad/Hanbarwadi) recently opened with about 50,000 sq ft in use; combined with unit 1 (about 20,000 sq ft) total manufacturing area about 70,000 sq ft.
Adjacent land of about 50,000 sq ft is already levelled, so a new shed can be built quickly if a new opportunity arises.
Management says current capacity is sufficient for guidance; no fresh equity needed unless a new opportunity emerges.
Unit 1 (about 20,000 sq ft) being converted into a full testing facility, including an ambient-controlled AC test room.
Small CapEx expected for the Aquilon sub-zero chiller initiative; a small manufacturing unit is being set up.
demand_pricing: Navy fleet support ship turnkey project is among about 10 live projects; management cites a large AC/HVAC/Ref plant order for the Indian Navy.

Management cites a market of about INR 2,750 crore over two years from naval ship approvals (about 1% share) and about INR 2,500 crore in non-naval shipbuilding (about 0.5% share), for an estimated INR 4,000-5,000 crore opportunity.
Next-generation corvette (NGC) orders reportedly cleared by CCS; management expects part of the orders to convert into firm orders in FY27 and the rest in FY28.
Eight orders are in the pipeline.
Imports reduced from about 30%+ to single digit in AC plants, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why are H1 margins low again, and what H2 margin is needed to hit guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited commodity (copper, metals) inflation on fixed-price contracts, offset by strategic sourcing and higher inventory. H2 is seasonally stronger due to higher volumes absorbing overheads and product mix. Management said the 22% guidance is annual, not half-yearly, and skewness should fade over 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why are receivable days high and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said receivable days fell from about 350 in FY25 to 250 at March 2026, were held at about 250 in H1 despite 84% growth, and should go to about 200. Management said there is no one-off and that shipyard milestone-based payments limit faster reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow negative and when does it turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed negative operating cash flow of about INR 42 crore to strategic sourcing, H2 deliveries and higher receivables. Management expects cash flow to turn positive by the end of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the data centre plan and are orders expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no data centre orders yet; the oil-free/magnetic-bearing technology is sourced from an Australian partner, with no manufacturing in India until volumes justify it. Traction is expected in 6-12 months and is excluded from FY27-28 projections.

qa_highlights.question: Can capacity support 40% growth and are new capex or funds needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is sufficient for current guidance. Land is levelled for a further shed if needed. Funding would be raised only if a new opportunity needs it; the additional working capital is to come mainly from internal accruals and some bank borrowing.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the depreciation method changed to straight line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said straight-line depreciation better reflects asset use and was adopted in a year of heavy capex. No quantified impact was given on the call.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation (copper, metals) on fixed-price contracts could compress margins if strategic sourcing is insufficient.
Negative operating cash flow and rising receivables (INR 128 crore) and inventory (INR 80 crore); working capital days were about 400 against a target of about 350.
Order book fell from INR 270 crore to about INR 200 crore; the H2 order ramp is not yet visible.
Dependence on naval shipbuilding timelines and government budget or election-related delays were raised as questions; management disputed the risk.
Data centre traction is unproven and excluded from guidance; management acknowledged no orders yet.
ROCE currently about 14-15% per analyst; management says the same capital base should lift returns as growth is funded by working capital.

544459|2026-03.headline: Shanti Gold Q4 FY26 revenue rose 121.65% YoY to INR 658.93 crore, a record quarter, with EBITDA margin at 10.17%.
544459|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR 658.93 crore, up 121.65% YoY, the highest quarterly revenue in company history, driven by new customers, higher volumes and elevated gold prices. FY26 revenue reached INR 2,018.71 crore (+82.46%), with PAT of INR 140.15 crore (6.94% margin). Management changed inventory valuation from FIFO to weighted average cost with retrospective effect from April 1, 2024. Much of the profit uplift was attributed by management to inventory gains from gold bought outright with IPO proceeds, and management guided to a core PAT margin of around 4%.

financial_highlights.change: from INR 9.19 crore in Q4 FY25

segments.name: Studded / bridal jewellery (existing line)
segments.commentary: Management said about 70% of revenue comes from the existing studded line; bridal jewellery carries higher margins and contributed to the Q4 EBITDA improvement.

segments.name: Plain gold jewellery (new line)
segments.commentary: About 30% of revenue is from the newly entered machine-made plain gold segment, which management described as lower margin, higher volume.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: volume growth of 30% to 40% and value growth of 60% to 70%; management cited FY27 turnover of around INR 3,000 to 3,500 crore in one answer and about INR 4,000 crore in another.

Core PAT margin guided at around 4% (management cited a 3.5% to 4% core range); the FY26 margin above this was attributed to inventory gains on gold bought outright with IPO proceeds, which management says is now mitigated and not included in guidance.
Export share guided to rise from about 5-10% to 10-20% this year, with Dubai subsidiary incorporation extended to June 2026.
Management expects to reach full 7,900 kg capacity in three to four years.
Working capital: management said inventory and trade receivables are each under 50 days; plain jewellery is expected to improve working capital cycle over time.
Debt-equity: management said it is comfortable at up to 1:1 (currently 0.36) to fund growth.
capex_capacity: Existing Andheri facility: installed capacity about 2,700 kg per annum, operating at around 65% utilisation.
Marol facility in Mumbai: adds about 4,000 kg per annum; management said it should be ready in about a month, starting at roughly 100 kg per month before ramping up.
Jaipur facility: adds 1,200 kg per annum; expected to start around September-October 2026.
Post-expansion total installed capacity is about 7,900 kg per annum, roughly three times the current capacity.
Quarterly volume reported at about 145-150 kg per month in a Q&A answer, which management said was disclosed quarterly in the presentation.
demand_pricing: Management said the structural shift from unorganised to organised jewellery retail is driving outsourcing to scalable manufacturers.

Management said demand is resilient, particularly in wedding and occasion-led categories; new products include Turkish jewellery (Turkish artisans onboarded for Marol), Mangalsutra and Cuban bracelets.
Management said the company has more than 400 customers and about 7% of volume or value from its top customer; it does not supply Titan/Tanishq currently.

Gold price context: management cited a move from about INR 78,000 to about INR 108,000 per 10 g and an assumed price of about INR 1,50,000 for guidance; it said guidance is based on current prices and not speculation.
Management said the 15% import duty increase would not hurt demand, citing a period when duty was 15% for many years and was cut to 6% last year.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY26 growth mainly price-driven, and what is the demand outlook ex-gold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume grew about 15% in FY26 after the IPO and value growth was higher; FY27 is guided at 30-40% volume and 60-70% value growth.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainable margin and how much of FY26 profit was from gold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a core PAT margin of around 4% is sustainable; the extra profit came from gold bought outright with IPO money, when gold prices rose.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity utilisation and volume per month?
qa_highlights.answer: Current utilisation is about 65%; volume is about 145-150 kg per month per the quarterly figures in the presentation.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and maximum debt level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt-equity of up to 1:1 is the target ceiling, with the current ratio at 0.36; inventory and receivables are each under 50 days.

qa_highlights.question: Why did volume guidance fall from 60-70% to 30-40%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 volume grew 15% and FY27 guidance of 40% plus is an increase, not a reduction; no contradiction in volume guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hedging policy and inventory held?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its hedging policy is to buy as it sells; it said about 600 kg of stock plus debtors is left, and it does not chase price movements.

risks_watch: Gold price volatility: management acknowledged gains and losses from inventory price movements; FY26 profit included inventory gains that management says are now excluded from guidance.
Margin gap: FY26 PAT margin was 6.94% versus the 4% core margin guided for FY27, and an analyst noted that doubling revenue to INR 4,000 crore at 4% implies only about INR 160 crore PAT.
Execution of the Marol (about 4,000 kg) and Jaipur (1,200 kg) ramp-ups, and the timing of the Jaipur start in September-October 2026.
Working capital and receivables: debtor days rose from 42 to 48-49; management expects new plain jewellery to improve the cycle.
Leverage: debt-equity expected to rise towards 1:1 to fund growth from 0.36 currently.
Geopolitical risk: the Dubai subsidiary has been delayed to June 2026 and export share targets depend on it.
Management said the 15% import duty would not hurt demand, but the duty increase is a demand-side watch item.
544459|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on volumes and demand, but defensive and at times evasive on margin sustainability and gold-price exposure, repeatedly redirecting to a 4% core margin. Answers on the inventory gains and PAT trajectory were inconsistent, and the call was marked by answers that were brief and sometimes unclear.
key_quotes: Q4FY26, we achieved the highest ever quarterly revenues in the histo ry of the company, reflecting our strong execution capabilities, improving scales, and increased relevance as a trusted manufacturing partner for organized jewellers.
We are not speculating on the gold market price movement whether it goes North or South.
So our core margin, come what may, will always remain between in the range of 3.4% to 4%, which is the normal industry range.
Our hedging policy is quite simple. We buy as we sell. Simple.

544459|2026-06.headline: Shanti Gold Q1 FY27 revenue rose 144.69% YoY to INR716.38 crores, with PAT of INR50.48 crores, though management flagged about 2-2.5 points of EBITDA margin from one-off inventory gains.
544459|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 144.69% YoY to INR716.38 crores and PAT rose 46.94% to INR50.48 crores, with PAT margin at 7.05%. EBITDA was INR71.45 crores at a 9.97% margin, which management said includes roughly 2-2.5 percentage points of unrealised inventory gain from the FIFO-to-WAC change. Management guided to 7.5-8% EBITDA margin going forward, reiterated FY27 guidance of 50-60% value growth and 30-40% volume growth (about INR3,500 crores revenue), and said the Marol (Mumbai) plant commenced operations in June 2026. A INR100 crore rights issue was approved to fund working capital and growth.

financial_highlights.change: +144.69% YoY vs INR292.78 crores in Q1 FY26
+39% YoY vs INR51.41 crores in Q1 FY26
Management plans to take it up to below 1x

segments.name: Studded jewellery
segments.commentary: Management said about 70% of jewellery sold is studded; in a separate answer it said 75% of revenue is designer jewellery and 25% plain gold, and about 75% is cast-studded. The figures given during the call are inconsistent and need clarification.

segments.name: Plain gold jewellery
segments.commentary: Management cited about 30% of jewellery sold as plain gold, or 25% of revenue, in different answers.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports were 4% of Q1 revenue. A Dubai office is awaiting RBI approval; management described it as the base for international expansion, currently serving three to four countries.

544459|2026-09.headline: Shanti Gold's Q2 FY27 revenue rose 73.4% YoY to INR746 crores, but EBITDA margin compressed to about 5.7% as management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR3,200-3,500 crores.

544465|2026-03.headline: Laxmi India Finance FY26 AUM rose over 27% to INR1,626 crore, PAT up 38% to INR49.7 crore, Gross NPA 2.13%.
544465|2026-03.overview: FY26 was the company's first year as a listed entity after its August 2025 IPO, with AUM of INR1,626 crore (on-book INR1,519 crore) and disbursements of INR821 crore. Net interest income rose nearly 39% to INR161 crore and PAT rose over 38% to INR49.7 crore. Blended cost of borrowing fell to 10.8% from 11.48%, and Acuite upgraded the rating to A/Stable. Management guided to 30-35% AUM CAGR and about 40-45% PAT growth in FY27, with Q4 PAT helped by an upfront gain of INR8.66 crore on a INR41 crore direct assignment (DA) pool.

segments.name: Secured MSME and retail lending
segments.commentary: Portfolio is about 98% secured, with 37% of borrowers first-time borrowers and mostly assessed-income customers. Rajasthan accounts for about 82% of AUM, MP about 11% and Gujarat about 7%.

segments.name: Branch network
segments.commentary: 176 branches across six states (Rajasthan, Gujarat, MP, Chhattisgarh, UP, Maharashtra), with 18 added in FY26. Breakeven takes about 7-8 months and about INR1.5-2 crore of disbursement per branch.

segments.name: Treasury / borrowings
segments.commentary: Over 40 lenders across PSU banks, private banks, SFBs, NBFCs and FIs; bank borrowings are the focus. Incremental cost is about 10.25-10.30%, and post-IPO fresh borrowing is at 10-10.25%.

guidance_outlook: AUM compound growth of around 30-35% annually over the medium term.
PAT growth of around 40-45% expected in the current year (FY27).
Cost of borrowing expected to fall a further 20-25 bps, subject to global rates; rating upgrade benefit to come in FY27.
Medium-term ROE guided at above 12-12.5% minimum; ROA to be kept above 3%.
Up Money balance of INR19 crore with INR11 crore provision; recovery expected in coming quarters via court orders, with the provision to flow to PAT on receipt.

Management said existing branches (including 18 added in FY26) have matured enough to deliver much of the 30-35% growth without new branches.
Agreement e-signing is still manual/physical; electronic signing is planned shortly, with the rest of the underwriting workflow already digital.
demand_pricing: Management says banks and fintechs largely avoid non-income-proof customers, which the company targets through field income verification.
Yield has been stable over the last 3-4 years; NIM is expected to hold at current levels or rise as cost of funds falls.
Q4 NIM and revenue were lifted by an INR8.66 crore upfront gain on a INR41 crore DA pool sale.
Management sees little stress from oil and energy prices, citing rural cash-flow borrowers and a vehicle portfolio of only 9%; it conceded some slowdown is possible if oil prices stay high.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a mandatory credit visit, bureau checks on all family members and a joint-family repayment base; it said multi-borrower income and liability checks limit overleveraging.

544465|2026-06.headline: Laxmi India Finance Q1 FY27 PAT rose ~70% YoY to INR16.4 crore, NIM expanded to 11.36%, while credit cost jumped to 0.95% on vehicle loans.
544465|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 showed strong growth: AUM up 28% YoY to INR1,721.7 crore, own book up 31.7% to INR1,626.9 crore, and disbursements of INR232 crore versus INR166 crore a year ago. Profitability improved sharply, with PBT up ~72% to INR21.9 crore and PAT up ~70% to INR16.4 crore, driven by a 67 bps fall in cost of borrowing to 10.66%. Asset quality improved sequentially (GNPA 2.08%, NNPA 0.93%), but credit cost rose to INR3.69 crore (0.95%) from 0.58%, attributed mainly to vehicle finance and an extra 10% provisioning on up-money cases. Management kept FY27 PAT growth guidance of 40-45% and AUM growth of 30-35% unchanged.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR166 crore in Q1 FY26 (~+40%)

financial_highlights.value: INR3.69 crore (0.95% of avg gross loan)

financial_highlights.metric: Debt to equity / net debt to equity

segments.name: MSME (secured SME)
segments.commentary: Core vertical at ~INR1,395 crore AUM; management says core MSME and construction credit costs remain moderate. A new prime MSME product for INR25-50 lakh tickets was recently launched.

segments.name: Vehicle finance (wheels)
segments.commentary: AUM ~INR131 crore; source of the credit cost rise, attributed to older vintages in specific geographies. Acceptance criteria tightened and field follow-ups increased.

segments.name: Construction and loan against property
segments.commentary: AUM ~INR90 crore.

segments.name: Wholesale lending
segments.commentary: AUM ~INR58 crore.

segments.name: Personal loans
segments.commentary: AUM ~INR49 crore.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth target of ~30-35% annually maintained.
FY27 PAT growth guidance of ~40-45% maintained; Q1 PAT growth stated to be significantly ahead of this range, with revision to be considered after the next few quarters.
Targeted ROA of 3.5-3.75% by year-end, per analyst question and management reply.
Further 20-25 bps reduction in cost of borrowing expected over coming quarters, assuming stable global rates and no RBI hike.
Cost-to-income ratio currently below 50%; internal target ~42-44%.
Plan to add 30-35 branches across existing states in FY27; 10 added in Q1. One or two new states planned per year.
Capital raise of ~INR300-350 crore planned in roughly 1-1.5 years (start of next financial year), when leverage reaches ~3.5-4x (pre-IPO level ~4-4.5x).
capex_capacity: Branch network at 184 across six states (Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra); 25 branches added over the last year, including 10 in UP and 6 in Maharashtra.
New branches reach breakeven in ~7-9 months (range 5-12 months) at an AUM of ~INR1.5-2 crore per branch; one of the 25 new branches is already at breakeven.
Branches are tiered: Tier 1 with 5-6 relationship officers, Tier 2 with 5-6, Tier 3 with 2-5.
Rajasthan (mother state, ~90 branches) remains the largest contributor; other states are expected to gain share over 3-4 years.
Digitised LOS/LMS, CKYC, RCU, eNACH and auto-dialer; only physical loan signing remains, expected to move to eSign shortly.
demand_pricing: Disbursements of INR232 crore grew ~40% YoY, ahead of 28% AUM growth; management attributes the gap to repayments and closures.
Portfolio yield broadly stable at 21.67%; NIM gain came from lower funding cost, not yield.
Management said it may pass on borrowing-cost relief to borrowers depending on asset quality and board decision.
37% of borrowers are first-time borrowers; customer base at ~43,946 vs 37,122 a year ago.
Management flagged rising competitive intensity in MSME lending and said underwriting discipline will be maintained.

qa_highlights.question: How are the new branches performing versus the mature network, and what is the gestation period to steady-state productivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Of 25 branches opened in the last year, one has reached breakeven. Breakeven takes about 7-9 months (5-12 months range) at branch AUM of roughly INR1.5-2 crore; Tier 1, 2 and 3 branches are staffed with 5-6, 5-6 and 2-5 relationship officers respectively.

qa_highlights.question: Over 3-5 years, what must change to move from a regional NBFC to a pan-India MSME franchise, and what is the biggest constraint?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will enter one or two new states per year, having started in Rajasthan and expanded through Gujarat, MP, Chhattisgarh, UP and Maharashtra. Management said it targets ROA of 3.5-3.75% and expects to reach it by year-end, with current ROA at 3.45%.

qa_highlights.question: What product and geographic mix changes are planned as AUM scales?
qa_highlights.answer: MSME stays the core product, with a new prime MSME product for INR25-50 lakh tickets. Plan is 30-35 branches in existing states in FY27, with 10 added in Q1. Rajasthan (about 90 branches) stays the largest state for the next 3-4 years, with other states gaining share.

qa_highlights.question: Why did credit cost rise to about 1%, and is stress coming from newer geographies or vintages?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to the wheels (vehicle) portfolio, specifically older vintages in certain geographies, and said it is localised. Gopal Krishan Sain said the main P&L driver was an extra 10% provisioning on up-money transactions, with 70% of that provisioning booked so far.

qa_highlights.question: How much balance sheet capacity remains before equity is needed, given CRAR moderation from about 26% to 25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt to equity is 2.57x with liquidity of about INR255.9 crore. Management plans to raise about INR300-350 crore in roughly 1-1.5 years, starting next financial year, when leverage reaches about 3.5-4x (pre-IPO about 4-4.5x).

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 and FY28 growth and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: AUM growth of 30-35% CAGR will be maintained. Margins depend on cost of borrowing and yield; management expects to pass some borrowing-cost relief to borrowers once cost of borrowing is in a declining phase.

qa_highlights.question: Are the El Nino and global uncertainties affecting the portfolio, and is AUM being expanded aggressively?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said global conflict has limited direct impact since customers are in Tier 2/3 cities, though crude prices raise borrower costs. It said growth is risk-based, with funding stopped or LTV reduced where stress is seen, and collection efficiency is expected to be maintained.

qa_highlights.question: What were the net slippages in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Net slippages were INR3.26 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How much further can cost of borrowing fall, what is the sustainable NIM, and where can cost-to-income settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Piyush Somani said another 20-25 bps reduction is expected over coming quarters, assuming stable global rates and no RBI hike; incremental cost of borrowing is about 10.48% over the last 12 months. Cost-to-income is below 50% now, with an internal target of around 42-44%; opex is elevated by new-state branch openings.

qa_highlights.question: How should the gap between 40% disbursement growth and 28% AUM growth be read, and does the run rate support faster AUM growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Kuldeep Singh said the gap reflects repayments and loan closures, and that the current disbursement run rate supports AUM growth.

Up-money cases: an extra 10% provisioning is being applied, with 70% of ECL provision booked so far; further provisioning depends on court-led enforcement and collection progress.
Capital: CRAR moderated to 25.32% from about 26%, and a INR300-350 crore raise is planned in roughly 1-1.5 years; execution timing and dilution are open.
Margin sustainability: NIM gain came from funding cost (10.66%, down 67 bps), not yield; management expects only 20-25 bps further cost reduction and may pass some relief to borrowers.
Branch maturity: new branches take 7-9 months on average to breakeven (range 5-12 months); cost-to-income is still above the 42-44% target, and opex grew about 34% YoY.

Competitive intensity in MSME lending is rising; management said underwriting discipline will be maintained. ROA target of 3.5-3.75% and FY27 PAT guidance of 40-45% (Q1 already well ahead) are to be reviewed after the next few quarters.
key_quotes: At the same time, we remain conscious that as we scale, maintaining the quality of our portfolio and discipline our underwriting will remain the most important priority for us.
We believe this is prudent to maintain our existing guidance at this stage and assess the performance over the next few quarters before considering any revision.
We are not looking to grow simply for the sake of balance sheet expansion.
The only manual step remains in our process is physical signing of loan agreements which we expect to move to eSign shortly.

544466|2026-03.headline: Aditya Infotech Q4 FY26 revenue rose 45.5% YoY to INR1,422 crore with EBITDA margin of 18%; FY27 revenue guidance raised to INR6,000-6,500 crore.
544466|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 45.5% YoY to INR1,422 crore, with EBITDA up 162% to INR258.3 crore and margin up 800 bps to 18%, helped by price rise, low-cost inventory and SKU mix. Full-year FY26 revenue reached INR4,220.8 crore (+35.6%), EBITDA INR579 crore (13.7% margin) and adjusted PAT INR368 crore (+166.1%). Management raised FY27 guidance to revenue INR6,000-6,500 crore, EBITDA margin 14-15% and PAT margin 8.5-9.5%. Management flagged that low-cost inventory is now exhausted and component costs (chips, memory, USD, freight) will keep rising through 2027, so price increases are being passed on monthly in small steps.

financial_highlights.change: Debt repaid from IPO proceeds; Q4 finance cost down 38%

segments.name: CP PLUS brand
segments.commentary: Contributed 86% of AIL revenue in Q4 and FY26; IP products are 73% of the CP PLUS portfolio.

segments.name: Camera/CCTV (India market)
segments.commentary: Company market share about 45.4% as of Q3 FY26, versus about 30% overall and about 25% for CP PLUS at the start of the journey. Management says it is not targeting a specific share number.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance raised to INR6,000-6,500 crore, about 50% growth over FY26.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance 14-15%; PAT margin around 8.5-9.5%. Management called 14-15% the new normal for FY27 and FY28, with Q4 a one-off above that level.
Unit volume growth target 25-30%, against an industry CCTV unit growth estimate of 15-16%.
Average per-unit camera realisation expected to rise 20-25% in FY27 (analyst-cited ASP growth about 25%).
FY27 capex expected at INR200-300 crore, funded mainly from internal accruals and some debt.
FY28 vision: double production capacity versus current levels, complete backward integration in key components, and a fully functional global R&D presence including Taiwan.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing capacity has reached 2.5 million units; management targets 90-100% utilisation.
Housing plant: Phase-1 operational by Q2 FY27 and Phase-2 by Q4 FY27, targeting 30 million housings and enclosures per year.
New lens assembly line commissioning with initial capacity of 5 lakh lenses per month, scalable to 1 million per month; CCTV lens production to start soon at Kadapa.
Kadapa: acquiring additional land and adding a 50,000 sq ft shed. Noida: proposed 3 lakh sq ft facility in Sector 68, operational by Q4 FY27.
Orient Cables JV for LAN and CCTV cable manufacturing: plant in Rajasthan (about 1 lakh sq ft), commercial operations expected between Q2 and Q3 FY27.
HD analog job work planned to move to EMS partners at about 0.5 million units per month. Evaluating further land in North India.
demand_pricing: Price hike of 6-8% taken in January 2026; management now moves prices monthly in small steps (single-digit % per month, varying by category) to avoid shocking customers. Further increases expected in FY27.

Market unit growth expected at 15-16% for FY27. Management says the industry's pent-up demand from the STQC transition was muted in FY26, and ASP increases are heavier on entry-level IP and NVR than on enterprise/project segments.
Consumer purchases are under 10% of the business; the business is largely B2B. Government is 15-20% of revenue and management plans for a similar share.

Competition: about 30 certified brands. A dozen global brands hold about 10% share; about 1.5 dozen domestic brands are each far smaller (about one-tenth of AIL's size or less). Management sees no single clear number-two player.
Memory: half of the 6-7 non-China DDR makers have stopped DDR3 output, pushing supply tightness onto smaller players. Management says scale lets AIL secure supply ahead of competitors.
Volume vs value in FY26: volume growth about 18-20%, with the rest from ASP and mix.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q4 gross margin (about 31.8%) came from low-cost inventory, mix or price rise, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Anup Nair cited a mix of low-cost inventory, the Q4 price rise and higher-end SKUs (STQC-certified project SKUs from H2). He said the low-cost inventory is now mostly used up, but FY27 guidance is above FY26 and slightly below Q4 margin.

qa_highlights.question: Cash conversion cycle and working capital needs with advance chip and memory purchases?
qa_highlights.answer: Anup Nair said the cash conversion cycle has risen because creditors fell as the company secured supply, and some inventory is being blocked with advance payments. Working capital is factored into FY27 plans; capex is to be funded mainly from internal accruals and some debt.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Aditya Khemka said the earlier plan of about INR200 crore has been raised to INR200-300 crore for FY27, with FY28 plans still under work. Funding is through internal accruals and some debt; the debt-equity ratio is very low.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 14-15% EBITDA margin the new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Aditya Khemka said 14-15% should be the new normal for FY27 and FY28, driven by localisation, cost optimisation, the shift to higher-end and enterprise products and premiumisation. Q4 was a one-off.

qa_highlights.question: Export plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Aditya Khemka said export action may start in FY27, but domestic demand comes first. Some thoughts are underway and the outcome is not yet clear.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue split FY26: volume vs price?
qa_highlights.answer: Anup Nair said volume growth was about 18-20% and the rest came from ASP and mix. The price rise was mainly in Q4. For FY27, ASP growth is about 25% and volume growth 25-30%.

risks_watch: Chip and memory supply: lead times are long, contracts are being invalidated under force majeure, and management says costs are rising every fortnight to week. Watch whether monthly price increases keep pace.
Margin sustainability: low-cost inventory is used up, and the cash conversion cycle has lengthened due to advance payments and lower creditors.
Demand: entry-level IP and NVR demand may shift to analog as price rises. Consumer and mobile-style demand softness is a risk in the wider market.
Execution: housing plant (Phase-1 Q2 FY27), lens line, Noida facility (Q4 FY27) and Rajasthan cable JV (Q2-Q3 FY27) all need to meet timelines. Doubling capacity by FY28 is a target.

New brands: Nexivue has started shipping since April 2026. Eyra is delayed by R&D rework and may reach market next quarter. Qualcomm AI platform is in trials and commercial rollout is phased. Certification pace is a watch item.
Competition: a more certified competitor base could arrive from 2028 onward, according to the analyst's question. Management says it has a head start on localisation, capacity and supply.

544466|2026-06.headline: Aditya Infotech Q1 FY27 revenue rose 89.5% YoY to INR1,402 crore; EBITDA margin 14.8%, adjusted PAT INR142.2 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is there further margin upside beyond 14-15% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it stands by the 14-15% guidance, aims to beat it internally, and will comment after H1 results.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the BOM is imported?
qa_highlights.answer: About 55-60% imported (35% Taiwan semiconductors, 15-20% passives) and 40% domestic, targeted over the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How is forex managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Hedging policy keeps cover between 85% and 100% of receivables and payables, currently about 90%, with weekly hedging.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current capacity and utilisation, and what is the capex timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: 2.5 million units per month at 85-90% utilisation; capacity to roughly double in three years, with gradual quarterly ramp-up.

qa_highlights.question: What is the average price increase so far and the remaining need?
qa_highlights.answer: About 15-20% average by end-H1 and around 25% for the full year, reviewed monthly and quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: How secure is chip sourcing and what changed in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: SOC and memory are covered for three to four quarters via rolling forecasts; other expenses rise is in line with seasonality (marketing at 30-32% of annual spend in Q1) and inflation.
